title: An Odyssey: Echoes of War
obs:
You announce your decision to your crew and tell them to wait on the ship until you return.
Demodocus, however, follows you to the shore.
When you look at him, your eyebrows asking him what in Hades he thinks he's doing, he protests. "How am I supposed to sing about your deeds if I don't witness them firsthand?"
"But what if I don't want you to sing about anything?" you ask, to which he responds with a shocked intake of breath. Then, defiant, he walks ahead, to the entrance of the cave.
*****Enter*****
The moment you pass through the threshold, you feel the tips of spears pressing against your skin. A bunch of angry women are scowling at you.
"Who are you?" the woman who seems to be in charge asks.
"User_input are User_input, Ruler of Ithaca and child of Gaia," Demodocus replies in your stead. "And I am Demodocus, the renowned poet," he adds.
"Are you here to claim our Queen Hippolyta's girdle?"
You catch on immediately. "Why yes, that's exactly why we are here."
They lower their spears at once. "Then we shall take you to our queen," the woman replies.
*****Follow Them*****
With the threat of spears removed, or at least postponed, you have a chance to take in your surroundings.
Around you lies a desert, golden and flickering under the sun as if on fire. You can see no sign of cities or palaces anywhere, but the determined way the Amazons are leading you suggest there is something you are missing.
The Amazons themselves seem fully integrated into this environment: clad in thin, light fabrics that cover enough to save them from the sun's unrelenting eye, but not so much as to restrict movement. Each of them carries a spear in hand, and bow and quiver strapped to the back. They seem to have some kind of scorn for shields, however, as if defending oneself is a ridiculous idea.
Demodocus looks quite taken with them, judging by the way he stares at them, his lips moving as if mouthing silent verses devoted to the rippling muscles of their backs.
"Do we have far to go?" you ask.
"Why? Are you tired?" the leader of the women, who has by now introduced herself as Ainippe, asks back. Then, she laughs. "Not at all. In fact, we're here."
The moment she says so, a complex of low buildings comes into view, like a mirage. They are made of the same sand the desert consists of, which would explain why they were not visible from a distance.
It's either that, or more of the gods' games.
When you reach the low gate of the largest building, the women form two lines on either side, spears planted on the ground at their sides.
"Go on in," Ainippe says, a condescending smile on her lips. "She might not even bite."
*****Enter*****
If you expected a palace and a throne room, this is not at all what you find before you. The room is clearly intended for training: it's sparse, equipped with iron weights and wooden sticks and human-shaped figures made of dried palm leaves, and carries the permanent scent of stale sweat that is the identifying trait of all training rooms.
In the middle of the room is a round arena, its ground covered in fine, white dust. And in the middle of that arena stands Hippolyta, Queen of the Amazons. Nothing distinguishes her from the rest of the Amazons you've seen, except for the girdle fastened at her waist.
Noticing you staring at her girdle, Hippolyta speaks: "I see you've spotted the item you came here for."
"I take it others have tried to win it before?"
Hippolyta smirks. "'Tried' being the important part in that statement." She looks at you, sizing you up. "Many have tried," she says. "Nobody has succeeded so far."
"Not even Hercules?" you ask.
She inhales sharply and frowns. "Do not speak that man's name in my presence."
"Why not?"
"We have history," she replies, then adds cryptically: "History that has come to pass, and more that is yet to be."
You study her face. The high cheekbones, the aquiline nose, the stubborn chin. You've seen these features before.
"I fought with your sister Penthesilea in Troy," you say.
She stands up a bit straighter, clenches her jaw. "With, or against?"
"Against," you say, "since she chose to assist the Trojans."
"I see," she says. Her eyes downturn for the first time.
There is still grief there.
"She was a good warrior, a valiant soldier."
"Killed by Achilles," she says. "Friend of yours?"
"Friend, yes," you reply.
"Then this is going to be fun," she says. "I assume you mean to fight me?"

title: Psy High
obs:
"I'm sorry Steve dumped you," you say gently. "He was a real jerk to do it during the prom. He was a jerk to do it at all. I know you really liked him." Actually, you don't know that, but for Mackenzie to be this upset, it must be true.
Mackenzie's eyes narrow. "What are you getting at, user_input? You don't care about me and Steve. You don't care about anything."
Uh-oh. Apparently you didn't sound sincere enough.
"You just get away from me!" she shouts.
You do. But as you do, you hear other people hurrying in your direction, and someone shouts, "Is everything okay?"
Uh-oh. You'd better be far away from here when Mackenzie tells people she just saw you.
You know you can't do this alone, and that's why you've spent so much time gathering up your friends and allies.
Now it's time to call on all those friends to make certain Mr. Pierce and Ms. Clay never get to the Nexus.
As the clock ticks towards midnight, the boat chugs towards the Nexus. From above, you can hear muffled laughter and music—the prom is still going strong. But those happy sounds feel very far away and very out of place compared to what’s happening here.
You’ve found the room on the lowest deck that will look directly out onto the Nexus. Through its single porthole, you can see a faint glow—most people would mistake it for moonlight, but even this far away you can sense the pulse of magic that tells you the Nexus itself is glowing.
You and your friends crowd around the door, blocking the way. When Mr. Pierce, Ms. Clay, and the Gold Crown Team come striding down the hallway, you're ready.
Haley gives you an uncertain look, then draws up straighter and calls, "All right, everyone! Let's go!"
The trouble is, the "everyone" Haley's talking to doesn't include that many people. They do their best—some a little frightened at the thought of facing down the principal, some defiant and resolute—but there just aren't enough people to keep Mr. Pierce away from the Nexus.
You worked hard, and you tried hard, and you counted on your friends, and your friends are helping you.
But it still isn't enough.
"I might have known that it would be you, user_input," snaps Mr. Pierce. "You're a bad seed, and you always have been. You and your little friends—you are nothing but a mob of children. Your priorities are entirely misplaced.
You are unruly and undisciplined.
You are disrespectful to your elders.
You have been given great supernatural power—yes, I know about that," he adds with a thin, superior smirk. "But you do nothing worthwhile with it. None of you children deserve to have the powers that you do. Those powers make you unpredictable. Unruly. It is absolutely evident that you need a grownup to keep you in line. I should have gotten rid of your bad influence on Kingsport High long ago."

The first thing you notice is the sweet, bright light. Everything around you is tinted gold. The sun is shining low, near the end of its daily journey. But it's not just that. Everything around you is golden. The grass under your feet, the flowering shrubs, the gates to the orchard that stands before you.
This, then, is the Garden of Hespera, Hera's orchard, where it is always sunset.
Behind the gates, you can see a single apple tree, its branches bent with golden apples. A fruit from that tree that became the Apple of Discord, which in turn led to the Trojan War.
And behind the tree, you can see two enormous columns–but no, not columns at all, but legs, the legs of a Titan, so tall as to rival the mountain behind him. You look up, and you can hardly make out his torso, his arms, his neck straining under the weight of the sky. Atlas.
The gate squeaks open and three women appear in front of it. They are dressed in ocher, orange, and yellow robes threaded with gold. The Hesperides, daughters of Atlas, nieces of Nyx.
"A visitor," one of them says. "How wonderful. We were getting terribly bored."
"Don't be silly, Aegle," another replies. "User_input just want the apples."
Aegle frowns. "You don't know that," she says. "Maybe this one's different."
The second woman turns to you, sizes you up. "Are you different?"
The third Hesperis takes a step forward. There is something menacing in her face now, something serpent-like. "Tell us what you want," she orders. "Do you want the apples?"

He nods. "That's right."
"You can do better than that, can't you?" You give him an encouraging grin. "You're good enough to get a much bigger role. You could play George, or even the Stage Manager."
Mike listens thoughtfully, but you're not sure if he's convinced. "Thanks, user_input." He sounds sincere, but then again, he [i]is[/i] a good actor. "It's nice of you to care that much, but I'm still going to audition for the Constable. That's the part I really want."
Oh well. It looks like you're still going to have Mike as your competition for the role of the Constable. At least you tried!
**********
The day of the Drama Club auditions rolls around, and everyone who's trying out files into the auditorium as soon as the last bell rings. You're uncomfortably aware of how few people are there. Maybe this will mean you'll have an easier time getting the part you want?
You're also unhappily aware that Mackenzie is there. Of course, she wants to play Emily Webb, one member of the young couple whose love story is the central arc of the plot. Emily gets the big tearjerking moment at the end when, from the afterlife, she says goodbye to the world she's leaving now that she's died.
"Goodbye to clocks ticking," Mackenzie recites, with a little catch in her voice. "And Mama's sunflowers, and food, and coffee…"
You hate to admit it, but Mackenzie's a good actor.
**********
"Thanks, Mackenzie," says Nate, scribbling a few notes on his clipboard. "Okay, user_input, you're up." He flips a few pages. "You'll read the Constable, and I'll read the other lines in the scene. Start whenever you're ready."
This is it! Your big moment.

title: Psy High
obs:
"Wait!" you say. "Actually, I wanted your help with something."
"Okay." Mackenzie's still looking at you suspiciously, but she's not shouting, and she seems to be at least a little distracted from her misery.
"I've got a big plan I need people to help with," you tell her. "Your role is really, really important." That seems to brighten Mackenzie a little, so you repeat, "[i]Really[/i] important."
Mackenzie nods. "Okay…"
"Haley will explain exactly what you need to do."
"Okay," Mackenzie says slowly. "I'll find her." She looks much calmer now—more focused on the plan than on her own unhappiness. Whew.
"Thanks," you say, and head off to take care of your part of the plan.
You know you can't do this alone, and that's why you've spent so much time gathering up your friends and allies.
Now it's time to call on all those friends to make certain Mr. Pierce and Ms. Clay never get to the Nexus.
As the clock ticks towards midnight, the boat chugs towards the Nexus. From above, you can hear muffled laughter and music—the prom is still going strong. But those happy sounds feel very far away and very out of place compared to what’s happening here.
You’ve found the room on the lowest deck that will look directly out onto the Nexus. Through its single porthole, you can see a faint glow—most people would mistake it for moonlight, but even this far away you can sense the pulse of magic that tells you the Nexus itself is glowing.
You and your friends crowd around the door, blocking the way. When Mr. Pierce, Ms. Clay, and the Gold Crown Team come striding down the hallway, you're ready.
Haley gives you an uncertain look, then draws up straighter and calls, "All right, everyone! Let's go!"
The trouble is, the "everyone" Haley's talking to doesn't include that many people. They do their best—some a little frightened at the thought of facing down the principal, some defiant and resolute—but there just aren't enough people to keep Mr. Pierce away from the Nexus.
You worked hard, and you tried hard, and you counted on your friends, and your friends are helping you.
But it still isn't enough.
"I might have known that it would be you, user_input," snaps Mr. Pierce. "You're a bad seed, and you always have been. You and your little friends—you are nothing but a mob of children. Your priorities are entirely misplaced.
You spend your time playing make-believe in the Drama Club, when you should be thinking about your future.
You are unruly and undisciplined.
You are disrespectful to your elders.
You have been given great supernatural power—yes, I know about that," he adds with a thin, superior smirk. "But you do nothing worthwhile with it. None of you children deserve to have the powers that you do. Those powers make you unpredictable. Unruly. It is absolutely evident that you need a grownup to keep you in line. I should have gotten rid of your bad influence on Kingsport High long ago."

title: Siege of Treboulain
obs:
Markov flinches. That barb hit deep. Probably because Markov knows it's true. You close in, not giving him an instant to recover.
Your spear clashes against Markov's spear. You totter around each other, grunting and straining and pushing with all your might.
An image flashes through your mind. A young Treboulain person and a young Skegg man struggling through a late-night study session with bleary-eyed determination, refusing to be the first to fall asleep.
Nothing's changed. Yet everything has.
Your elbow slides under Markov's shield, crunching into his hip. He folds over, gasping. You seize the opening to punch his helmet with an armored fist, sending the metal slapping into his chin. He staggers backward. Blood sprays from his mouth. Along the Pearl Boulevard, your soldiers cheer. But they don't cheer for long. As Markov stumbles away, his spear hooks behind your ankle and flips you backward. Almost in slow motion, you fall.
You collapse onto the hard cobblestones. Stars flash behind your eyes, bile crawls up your throat, and the world grows faint and muffled, as if obscured by a thick fog. Wooziness spins the ground beneath you. The roars and shrieks of the soldiers along the Pearl Boulevard…they are barely audible. All you can focus on is the ground that shakes beneath your head as Markov strides toward you.
"Stay down and surrender your city," says Markov as he comes closer. "And I may spare your life."
You need to stand. But agony wracks your body and your limbs are as fragile as autumn leaves. It will take a mighty effort to rise again.

Yang says, "How did you know that?"
Zahara rolls her eyes. You tell Yang, "It was obvious. He smelled like booze at work." You take a guess and a gamble. "Didn't he drive Moment Slater back to the hotel the night before he missed work?"
They think for a moment. Zahara says, "Yeah. He and Crystal took Moment back after she was eliminated. After that, we lost track of him."
Yang adds, "He wasn't supposed to go to the hotel bar afterward, but he did. He thought he had time to grab a beer before driving back to the set. I think someone drugged him."
"You never told me that!" Zahara says.
Interesting. It's good that Yang isn't a contestant. He can't keep his mouth shut worth a damn.
Even if they can't help you, they also can't keep you locked in your room all weekend. It's time to look for clues around the hotel.
You start pacing up and down the hall, scanning the doors of your castmates.
Zahara asks what you're doing.
"Nothing that's against the rules, Zahara. I'm observing." Nothing unusual in the hallway. A little glitter here and there. Some stray wig hairs.
You know that the eliminated contestants eat in the same dining room you do, but at a different time. You ask Yang to walk you down to the dining room. He'll probably disclose something useful if you make small talk with him.
As you poke around, you chat with him. "So, who do you think will win?"
He stands at the door with his arms crossed. "I have no idea. I haven't seen much on set."
The breakfast buffet has been cleared and the room swept. You think of another question for Yang. "When do the eliminated contestants have breakfast?"
He pulls out his cell phone and starts playing with it. "After you do. Remaining contestants eat an hour before the breakfast buffet opens. Then the eliminated contestants eat with the other hotel guests, but we chaperone them. They aren't allowed to talk to anyone about the game."
You look under a table. Nothing. You ask another question. "Do fans ever figure it out and approach the contestants?"
Yang is still texting or playing a match-three or something. "It's happened before. Sometimes they get recognized. They're supposed to say they're in town auditioning for [i]America's Totally Talented[/i]."
Talented is relative. Yang perks up for a moment. "Hey, what are you doing?"
Oh, [i]now[/i] he's doing his job? Ugh. You're not done checking the dining room for clues. You need to buy a little more time. How will you answer?

title: Psy High
obs:
You clear your throat. "Ms. Clay?" Your voice sounds very loud in the quiet of the detention room.
She peers over at you from behind her desk. "Yes, user_input?"
Your heart pounds faster. Here it goes….
**********
"I've been thinking a lot this afternoon," you begin. "I've realized that I want to do better. I want to do well in school and get into a good college." You're watching Ms. Clay carefully, but her expression doesn't give anything away—you can't tell if you're convincing her or not. You'll just have to keep talking and hope that this works. "Is there any way that I can join the Gold Crown Team? I've seen the good that it's done for Jen Cohen and Will Nichols."
Ms. Clay keeps that flat, steady gaze fixed on you. "Really?" is all she says.
You nod.
"Really." The less you say, the better—you don't want to give her any more chances to figure out that you're lying.
"Really," Ms. Clay repeats. This time her voice is harder. Flatter. More skeptical.
Uh-oh.
"Do you know, for some reason, I don't believe you." Sarcasm starts to sharpen her words, and her gaze fixes on you with an ever-increasing chill. "Perhaps it is because you have such a reputation for poking your nose where it doesn't belong. Perhaps it is because you're just a troublemaker at heart. Or perhaps," she finishes, rising from her desk and stalking towards you, "it is because I suspect that you have been [i]looking[/i] into things that are none of your business."
That emphasis on "looking" sends a sudden chill through you. She knows. She knows about your clairvoyance. She knows [i]everything[/i].
**********
Ms. Clay looms over your desk for a long, long moment.
"But the sentiment is admirable. You [i]would[/i] be much better off if you were not so poorly behaved. You would be a more productive member of the Kingsport community, and you would not be such a disappointment to your parents and teachers." Her smile is sharp, and doesn't reach her eyes. "Let us ensure that you will not disappoint them again."
With a snap of her hand, the door to the closet flies open, and a wave of energy sweeps over you.
The magical energy coming from the Vinculum crashes over you like an enormous wave. It swamps your senses, fills your mind, pulls you into it with a tide you cannot resist. It swells around you, pressing harder and harder until you think you might burst.
There is nothing in the world but light. There is nothing in the world but pain.
**********
Somewhere amid the pressure, a new thought enters your mind: if you just accept this energy, you will be at peace.
You'll be better off. You won't have to fight; you won't have to worry. Your parents won't have to worry, either. Everything will just work out.
Will you accept it?

title: It's Killing Time
obs:
You don't so much as make a move for your pockets, telling the kid to scram.  Making one final attempt he says, "No crowns for Boris?"  A bit startled by the boy's name, you shake you head and he frowns then shakes his head, too, muttering something beneath his breath before walking farther down the street to talk to other people.
As he does, you look back and forth, furtively, trying to make sure you haven't been made.  After a few minutes, you're confident you haven't been, that it was just a coincidence.
Turning back to your thoughts, still a little shocked by the urchin's name, you review Boris's plan for the day.  He's going to be taking lunch in a cafe off the square, meeting with a business acquaintance.  Being in the square yourself, you look around and realize that it's unlikely you'll be able to make a sniper shot due to the close proximity of the buildings near the cafe.
You decide it's best to scope out the restaurant up close and, as you do, you see a network of alleyways leading to other areas of the city.  You figure Boris must want a clandestine meeting place because this part of the town is relatively secluded.  You realize it would be the perfect spot for a run-by shooting, the warren of alleys enabling you to disappear to another part of town after the deed was done.  Saving that as one option, you run down the list to see where else Boris will be going today.
After lunch, Boris is slated to meet with a gambling kingpin in an upscale, historical hotel.  You know that you'll be able to get in with no problem, but reason that guns are going to have to be out because, even with a silenced weapon, with the old Czech construction, you're likely to put a bullet into another room and bring the police running.
Finishing up the list, you realize there's another option if you wait until Boris has dinner.  He's scheduled to have his supper at a place called Golem Cafe.  The message says there's going to be a big event there tonight, so a direct attack of any kind isn't likely to be successful.  You figure that you can likely find a chef to bribe and try to poison Boris and his crew.
**********
Thinking of the options, a you can't help but circle back to the beggar boy and his name.  Boris.  The same name of the man who sold you out, his betrayal made so much worse since he had been like a father to you.
You know in your heart that you had been like a child to Boris, and you wonder if it would be even better revenge to sneak into Boris's home when he was gone, leaving a black lily on his pillow, the Russian symbol of death.  You contemplate the notion, knowing that Boris would not only forever be watching over his shoulder, wondering if you were going to strike, but he would also be confronted with the fact that you could have killed him and didn't.  You wonder if that's crueler, forcing Boris to live with his guilt for the rest of his days.
Contemplating it all, you also realize you have one other option.  You could let it go.  You recognize that you could forgive Boris for what he did and move on, even though it would be difficult.
In the end, you decide to:

title: Psy High
obs:
"Wow, I'm sorry about you and Steve," you say vaguely. Half your mind is elsewhere, though, trying to overhear Mackenzie's thoughts.
Her mind is a miserable jumble. [i]This is horrible! I wish it had never happened. I'm so embarrassed! I want to talk to Casey, but I don't want anyone to know![/i] Of course! Casey's one of her best friends.
"I know I'm not the right person to be here right now," you say gently. "You probably want to talk to Casey, right?"
Mackenzie looks up, startled out of her tears at your perceptive comment. She swallows hard, and nods. "Yes. I do."
All the friends who know what's going on are already doing other things, so you'll have to find Casey yourself.
You rush through the dance floor until you find Casey dancing with her girlfriend Emma. "Hey, Casey?" Emma frowns at you for cutting in, and you give her an apologetic look. "Could you go to the south corridor? Mackenzie needs you."
Emma sighs. "I understand. Go."
So Casey goes. And so do you.
You know you can't do this alone, and that's why you've spent so much time gathering up your friends and allies.
Now it's time to call on all those friends to make certain Mr. Pierce and Ms. Clay never get to the Nexus.
As the clock ticks towards midnight, the boat chugs towards the Nexus. From above, you can hear muffled laughter and music—the prom is still going strong. But those happy sounds feel very far away and very out of place compared to what’s happening here.
You’ve found the room on the lowest deck that will look directly out onto the Nexus. Through its single porthole, you can see a faint glow—most people would mistake it for moonlight, but even this far away you can sense the pulse of magic that tells you the Nexus itself is glowing.
You and your friends crowd around the door, blocking the way. When Mr. Pierce, Ms. Clay, and the Gold Crown Team come striding down the hallway, you're ready.
Haley gives you an uncertain look, then draws up straighter and calls, "All right, everyone! Let's go!"
The trouble is, the "everyone" Haley's talking to doesn't include that many people. They do their best—some a little frightened at the thought of facing down the principal, some defiant and resolute—but there just aren't enough people to keep Mr. Pierce away from the Nexus.
You worked hard, and you tried hard, and you counted on your friends, and your friends are helping you.
But it still isn't enough.
"I might have known that it would be you, user_input," snaps Mr. Pierce. "You're a bad seed, and you always have been. You and your little friends—you are nothing but a mob of children. Your priorities are entirely misplaced.
You are disrespectful to your elders.
You have been given great supernatural power—yes, I know about that," he adds with a thin, superior smirk. "But you do nothing worthwhile with it. None of you children deserve to have the powers that you do. Those powers make you unpredictable. Unruly. It is absolutely evident that you need a grownup to keep you in line. I should have gotten rid of your bad influence on Kingsport High long ago."

title: The Cryptkeepers of Hallowford
obs:
You look to your allies and nod.
This is a chance you have to take.
If you're going to get out of this alive, you're going to have to destroy the Heart. To do that, you'll have to get through Lucan, his Cryptkeepers, and anyone else standing in your way. So long as they're distracted, you might have a chance of getting through.
You take a breath and run toward the cage of alien metal that holds the Heart at the center of the chamber.
But you are not fast enough. Lucan's Cryptkeepers
and Sir Michael's watch
may be fighting for their lives, but they still manage to spot you before you get anywhere near close enough.
A cry of alarm goes up. Someone points an arbalest your way. You back off, moving away to the edge of the central platform.
There are still too many who would stop you from destroying the Heart. Maybe if you waited for a better opportunity, after the Creatures have worn them down more.
It's a morbid prospect, letting the undying kill and maim Hallowford's defenders so that you can get close enough to destroy the Heart, but if that's what it takes to get anyone out alive, then that's what must be done.
**********
The undying surge forward against the last remnants of the forces of the living.
Only a handful are still on their feet and fighting.
Lucan and the last holdouts of his Cryptkeepers are on the verge of destruction. But with magic and steel, they cling to a tiny patch of bloodied stone, even as their knot of defenders grows smaller and smaller.
Sir Michael and his last few watch members are no better off. They fall back the last few steps until their backs are pressed against the harsh light of the Heart itself.
With every passing second, the dead advance. With every moment, despair grows in the eyes of the living. This can't go on for much longer.

obs:

Sleep never comes; it appears you don't need it anymore.

[i]Maybe you should have let me take control, User_input.[/i]

title: Siege of Treboulain
obs:
Your back is straight, each step is measured, and there's a hard assuredness spread across your face. Soldiers salute as you pass. Your own guards stand straighter, and Dimi Floros nods approvingly.
"Stavren wrote that a person breaks only when they choose to be broken," the merchant says. "So you've done well to stay calm. Act as if something is certain, and the world will follow."
*****Back to the Citadel*****
The ground slopes steeply as you follow the Pearl Boulevard up toward Treboulain's Citadel. When you reach the top of the Citadel's steps, you can see the whole of Treboulain, with the streets delineated by the luminescent green of glowshrooms. Beyond the wall, there is darkness. In the far distance, a line of fire breaks that darkness, stretching across the spit of land that Treboulain occupies. It's the Skegg's camp.
The wind shifts, bringing with it the noise of foreign voices and clanking hammers. The Skegg are building. They have committed to destroying Treboulain. And only you can stop them.
*****Crisis Meeting*****
You convene in the throne room to discuss plans with Marshal Heartstone, Dimi Floros, Priestess Saphira, Lord Daen, and dozens of other important officers, nobles, and citizens.
An aide hands Heartstone a report. The marshal grunts in thanks, glowering at the map of Treboulain spread across the table before you. Knives weigh down the corners to stop the map curling up.
As the aide departs, she casts you a look of glowing admiration. Everyone in the army seems to think highly of you after your actions today.
Heartstone skims the report. "Our infantry remains strong, and our archers have retained most of their soldiers."
"It's too bad that we have no arborturgic soldiers to complement our army." Dimi Floros casts a smirk toward Priestess Saphira. "Why, if only we'd had them today, maybe hundreds of lives would have been saved…."
Saphira sniffs. "Our arborturgists are not soldiers. They are priests."
"Everyone's a soldier during war," says Floros.
Saphira refused your earlier request to recruit arborturgists into the army. Perhaps she will feel different now?
Of course, there will be ways for the arborturgists to help without breaking their pacifist vows, so you may not want them to become fighters. They could help strengthen fortifications, assist with growing food, or take on any number of other tasks.

title: An Odyssey: Echoes of War
obs:
You announce your decision to your crew and tell them to wait on the ship until you return.
Demodocus, however, follows you to the shore.
You let him.
*****Enter*****
The moment you pass through the threshold, you feel the tips of spears pressing against your skin. A bunch of angry women are scowling at you.
"Who are you?" the woman who seems to be in charge asks.
"User_input are User_input, Ruler of Ithaca and child of Gaia," Demodocus replies in your stead. "And I am Demodocus, the renowned poet," he adds.
"Are you here to claim our Queen Hippolyta's girdle?"
You catch on immediately. "Why yes, that's exactly why we are here."
They lower their spears at once. "Then we shall take you to our queen," the woman replies.
*****Follow Them*****
With the threat of spears removed, or at least postponed, you have a chance to take in your surroundings.
Around you lies a desert, golden and flickering under the sun as if on fire. You can see no sign of cities or palaces anywhere, but the determined way the Amazons are leading you suggest there is something you are missing.
The Amazons themselves seem fully integrated into this environment: clad in thin, light fabrics that cover enough to save them from the sun's unrelenting eye, but not so much as to restrict movement. Each of them carries a spear in hand, and bow and quiver strapped to the back. They seem to have some kind of scorn for shields, however, as if defending oneself is a ridiculous idea.
Demodocus looks quite taken with them, judging by the way he stares at them, his lips moving as if mouthing silent verses devoted to the rippling muscles of their backs.
"Do we have far to go?" you ask.
"Why? Are you tired?" the leader of the women, who has by now introduced herself as Ainippe, asks back. Then, she laughs. "Not at all. In fact, we're here."
The moment she says so, a complex of low buildings comes into view, like a mirage. They are made of the same sand the desert consists of, which would explain why they were not visible from a distance.
It's either that, or more of the gods' games.
When you reach the low gate of the largest building, the women form two lines on either side, spears planted on the ground at their sides.
"Go on in," Ainippe says, a condescending smile on her lips. "She might not even bite."
*****Enter*****
If you expected a palace and a throne room, this is not at all what you find before you. The room is clearly intended for training: it's sparse, equipped with iron weights and wooden sticks and human-shaped figures made of dried palm leaves, and carries the permanent scent of stale sweat that is the identifying trait of all training rooms.
In the middle of the room is a round arena, its ground covered in fine, white dust. And in the middle of that arena stands Hippolyta, Queen of the Amazons. Nothing distinguishes her from the rest of the Amazons you've seen, except for the girdle fastened at her waist.
Noticing you staring at her girdle, Hippolyta speaks: "I see you've spotted the item you came here for."
"I take it others have tried to win it before?"
Hippolyta smirks. "'Tried' being the important part in that statement." She looks at you, sizing you up. "Many have tried," she says. "Nobody has succeeded so far."
"Not even Hercules?" you ask.
She inhales sharply and frowns. "Do not speak that man's name in my presence."
"Why not?"
"We have history," she replies, then adds cryptically: "History that has come to pass, and more that is yet to be."
You study her face. The high cheekbones, the aquiline nose, the stubborn chin. You've seen these features before.
"I fought with your sister Penthesilea in Troy," you say.
She stands up a bit straighter, clenches her jaw. "With, or against?"
"Against," you say, "since she chose to assist the Trojans."
"I see," she says. Her eyes downturn for the first time.
There is still grief there.
"She was a good warrior, a valiant soldier."
"Killed by Achilles," she says. "Friend of yours?"
"Friend, yes," you reply.
"Then this is going to be fun," she says. "I assume you mean to fight me?"

title: An Odyssey: Echoes of War
obs:
You ready yourself, and then you notice Demodocus preparing to follow you.
"Where do you think you're going?" you ask him.
This stops the poet in his tracks. "With you?" he says uncertainly.
"No," you reply. "I'm going alone."
You squeeze his shoulder. "I'll tell you all about it when I get back," you say.
"Promise?" he asks.
"I promise," you reply.
*****Enter*****
When you step through the threshold, the world shimmers around you and you realize you are not in a cave at all. Instead, you are in a new place altogether.
The first thing you notice is the sweet, bright light. Everything around you is tinted gold. The sun is shining low, near the end of its daily journey. But it's not just that. Everything around you is golden. The grass under your feet, the flowering shrubs, the gates to the orchard that stands before you.
This, then, is the Garden of Hespera, Hera's orchard, where it is always sunset.
Behind the gates, you can see a single apple tree, its branches bent with golden apples. A fruit from that tree that became the Apple of Discord, which in turn led to the Trojan War.
And behind the tree, you can see two enormous columns–but no, not columns at all, but legs, the legs of a Titan, so tall as to rival the mountain behind him. You look up, and you can hardly make out his torso, his arms, his neck straining under the weight of the sky. Atlas.
The gate squeaks open and three women appear in front of it. They are dressed in ocher, orange, and yellow robes threaded with gold. The Hesperides, daughters of Atlas, nieces of Nyx.
"A visitor," one of them says. "How wonderful. We were getting terribly bored."
"Don't be silly, Aegle," another replies. "He just wants the apples."
Aegle frowns. "You don't know that," she says. "Maybe this one's different."
The second woman turns to you, sizes you up. "Are you different?"
The third Hesperis takes a step forward. There is something menacing in her face now, something serpent-like. "Tell us what you want," she orders. "Do you want the apples?"

title: It's Killing Time
obs:
You pat your pockets and shrug your shoulders, holding your hands out in an "I have no money" gesture.  You apologize and tell the boy that you just don't have any cash on you and that he should look for real work.  You even point to another young boy who is working at a food stand.  He nods, seeming to understand you.  Making one final attempt he says, "No crowns for Boris?"  A bit startled by the boy's name, you shake you head and he moves on, walking farther down the street to talk to other people.
As he does, you look back and forth, furtively, trying to make sure you haven't been made.  After a few minutes, you're confident you haven't been, that his name was just a coincidence.
As he does, you look back and forth, furtively, trying to make sure you haven't been made.  After a few minutes, you're confident you haven't been, that it was just a coincidence.
Turning back to your thoughts, still a little shocked by the urchin's name, you review Boris's plan for the day.  He's going to be taking lunch in a cafe off the square, meeting with a business acquaintance.  Being in the square yourself, you look around and realize that it's unlikely you'll be able to make a sniper shot due to the close proximity of the buildings near the cafe.
You decide it's best to scope out the restaurant up close and, as you do, you see a network of alleyways leading to other areas of the city.  You figure Boris must want a clandestine meeting place because this part of the town is relatively secluded.  You realize it would be the perfect spot for a run-by shooting, the warren of alleys enabling you to disappear to another part of town after the deed was done.  Saving that as one option, you run down the list to see where else Boris will be going today.
After lunch, Boris is slated to meet with a gambling kingpin in an upscale, historical hotel.  You know that you'll be able to get in with no problem, but reason that guns are going to have to be out because, even with a silenced weapon, with the old Czech construction, you're likely to put a bullet into another room and bring the police running.
Finishing up the list, you realize there's another option if you wait until Boris has dinner.  He's scheduled to have his supper at a place called Golem Cafe.  The message says there's going to be a big event there tonight, so a direct attack of any kind isn't likely to be successful.  You figure that you can likely find a chef to bribe and try to poison Boris and his crew.
**********
Thinking of the options, a you can't help but circle back to the beggar boy and his name.  Boris.  The same name of the man who sold you out, his betrayal made so much worse since he had been like a father to you.
You know in your heart that you had been like a child to Boris, and you wonder if it would be even better revenge to sneak into Boris's home when he was gone, leaving a black lily on his pillow, the Russian symbol of death.  You contemplate the notion, knowing that Boris would not only forever be watching over his shoulder, wondering if you were going to strike, but he would also be confronted with the fact that you could have killed him and didn't.  You wonder if that's crueler, forcing Boris to live with his guilt for the rest of his days.
Contemplating it all, you also realize you have one other option.  You could let it go.  You recognize that you could forgive Boris for what he did and move on, even though it would be difficult.
In the end, you decide to:

and Sir Michael's watch
may be fighting for their lives, but they still manage to spot you before you get anywhere near close enough.

obs:
There's going to be no convincing Lucan to back down—one look into his eyes will tell you that. If there was a time that a reasoned argument was going to get the Master of the Cryptkeepers to do the right thing, that moment is long past.
You'll have to do this the hard way.

No matter how hard you try, you can't get close to Lucan without being spotted and stopped. Not yet anyway.
You'll have to wait for a better opportunity. When the Cryptkeepers are pressed harder by the Creatures, when they're too busy fighting for their lives to even notice you, let alone interfere with you—that will be the time to make your move.
Until then, you'll just have to watch and wait.

title: An Odyssey: Echoes of War
obs:
Demodocus laughs. He thinks you're joking, the poor lad.
**********
You repair the ship as best you can, but, without fresh timber and time on dry land, there is little you can do. You have saved yourselves from sinking, for now, but your crew's safety, your own safety, and the journey home itself is hanging by a thread.
Nevertheless, the ship sails calmly for two whole days. But on the third day, the sky darkens suddenly and a great roar rises from the depths.
"Poseidon," Circe whispers, and her voice catches in her throat.
A wave as tall as a giant rises before you, and in its heart you glimpse the mighty god, the Earth-Shaker, seizing his trident in his hand, stirring up the sea. He rides a chariot made of shells and corals, dragged by enormous mares. Their manes are made of foam, and their hind legs disappear into fish tails. You've seen the likeness of these beasts before, in pictures assembled by tiny pieces of colored glass adorning the floors of your palace, back in Ithaca. Hippocampi.
Poseidon strikes the edge of the wave with the tip of his trident, and your ship is covered with vapor. "User_input!" he roars. "How dare you
taunt my son?"
This is the result of your pride. Your need to spread your name throughout the world brought this upon you and your crew.
But there is no time for any of that right now.
Poseidon raises his fist to the sky and calls up the winds. And the winds, like obedient servants, gather: the East Wind and the South Wind, full of heat, and the West Wind, the carrier of storms, and the heaven-born North Wind. They drive a vast wave before him and crash against your ship, splintering your deck.
Next to you, Demodocus's joints slacken and he sinks to his knees. "How black the sea, how black the clouds," he whimpers. "Now we are certainly doomed. Blessed and thrice blessed were those Achaeans who fell in Troy. I wish we'd been killed the day when the Trojans were pressing us so sorely on the battlefield around the dead body of Achilles, for then we should have had the burial we deserve and all of the Achaeans would have honored our names, and our bodies wouldn't be lost in the unsung depths of the cold sea."
Ajax grasps the back of Demodocus's neck with his giant arm and pulls him to his feet. It wouldn't be a surprise if he slapped the lad about the face a couple of times, but he refrains. "Pull yourself together, poet!" he shouts. "And if you so wish for death, I'll make sure you get your due, once we're out of this cursed storm!"
**********
Enormous waves keep crashing against the hull of your ship, and you all scramble to keep yourselves tethered to the deck, or you'll be lost for good, drowned, feast for whatever lurks underneath the surface of this sea.
You can no longer see Poseidon, but you can feel his wrath. It batters your ship, soaks your hair and skin with salt water, fills your lungs until you can no longer breathe.
And when you are certain that this is your final hour, that your ship will surely sink this time, the storm abates at once, as suddenly as it started.
You find yourself on calm waters again. The clouds disperse and the sun shines above, slowly drying your skin, your hair, your clothes. Your crew right themselves one by one, timidly, reluctantly, as if unable to believe you made it out alive.
Then, you see.
"Oh no," you hear Circe say. "No no no no no."
**********
At first, you mistake what you see around you for kelp floating just under the surface of the water. Pieces of a shipwreck, perhaps, or driftwood sculpted by the salt-laced craft of the sea.
But then your mind catches up to your eyes, and then you make out the sunken faces, the shriveled skin, the nibbled toes, the tangles of hair still attached to decaying scalps.
"Talk to me, Circe," you say to the sorceress, because she seems to know where you are, what it is that's going on.
"We're in the Sirens' land," she says. "Dreadful creatures–half women, half beasts. They call them the Binders, the Entanglers. These poor wretches were caught by their song. They say that the Sirens' song bestows perfect knowledge and intense pleasure. But this," she gestures at the pieces of humans floating all around you, as far as your eye can see, "this is the price you pay."
"How did they get to be this way?" Polyxena asks.
"They were regular women, once. Some goddess punished them for their poor choices…" She trails off. You both see Polyxena is about to launch into a long and impassioned discussion of what "regular women" are or do, and there is clearly no time for that. "I don't actually know the details," Circe hastens to add. "Only what my grandmother told me when I was growing up."
"Can't we just sail around them?" Ajax asks.
"No," says Circe. She points at a cluster of jagged rocks up ahead. "The currents here are such that any ship caught has to drift by their shores. If we try to go against them, we'll be crushed against those rocks."
Demodocus turns to you. "What are we going to do, User_input?" he asks. "We've already survived so much. Perhaps our fortune has finally run out."

1: Plug everyone's ears and kill the Sirens to save future passing sailors. Riskier, but heroic.
2: Have everyone's ears plugged with beeswax and myself tied to the mast, hoping the rope will hold.
3: This whole heroic setup sounds suspicious to me. Sit down and have a real conversation with these women.

title: Psy High

"You insolent child!" Mr. Pierce shouts. Just as you'd hoped, he turns to face you, aiming the full force of his anger towards you—and turning his back on the Nexus. "How dare you lecture me?"
He's so distracted by berating you that he doesn't even notice your friends coming in to crowd him away from the Nexus.
"This is wrong!" comes a voice from behind you.
It's the first bit of emotion you've heard from Jen in months.
You turn to see her at the head of a growing crowd of Gold Crown Team members, all lined up in perfect rows and all staring at you. "This is wrong!" Jen repeats. She actually sounds surprised. And indignant.
It was hard enough to face down your principal. But what about your friends?
**********
You have to think fast! What are you going to do?

title: Psy High
obs:
Mackenzie sniffs hard, and eyes you suspiciously.
"I'm sorry Steve dumped you," you say gently. "He was a real jerk to do it during the prom. He was a jerk to do it at all. I know you really liked him." Actually, you don't know that, but for Mackenzie to be this upset, it must be true.
Mackenzie's eyes narrow. "What are you getting at, user_input? You don't care about me and Steve. You don't care about anything."
Uh-oh. Apparently you didn't sound sincere enough.
"You just get away from me!" she shouts.
You do. But as you do, you hear other people hurrying in your direction, and someone shouts, "Is everything okay?"
Uh-oh. You'd better be far away from here when Mackenzie tells people she just saw you.
You know you can't do this alone, and that's why you've spent so much time gathering up your friends and allies.
Now it's time to call on all those friends to make certain Mr. Pierce and Ms. Clay never get to the Nexus.
As the clock ticks towards midnight, the boat chugs towards the Nexus. From above, you can hear muffled laughter and music—the prom is still going strong. But those happy sounds feel very far away and very out of place compared to what’s happening here.
You’ve found the room on the lowest deck that will look directly out onto the Nexus. Through its single porthole, you can see a faint glow—most people would mistake it for moonlight, but even this far away you can sense the pulse of magic that tells you the Nexus itself is glowing.
You and your friends crowd around the door, blocking the way. When Mr. Pierce, Ms. Clay, and the Gold Crown Team come striding down the hallway, you're ready.
Haley gives you an uncertain look, then draws up straighter and calls, "All right, everyone! Let's go!"
The trouble is, the "everyone" Haley's talking to doesn't include that many people. They do their best—some a little frightened at the thought of facing down the principal, some defiant and resolute—but there just aren't enough people to keep Mr. Pierce away from the Nexus.
You worked hard, and you tried hard, and you counted on your friends, and your friends are helping you.
But it still isn't enough.
"I might have known that it would be you, user_input," snaps Mr. Pierce. "You're a bad seed, and you always have been. You and your little friends—you are nothing but a mob of children. Your priorities are entirely misplaced.
You spend your time playing make-believe in the Drama Club, when you should be thinking about your future.
You are unruly and undisciplined.
You are disrespectful to your elders.
You have been given great supernatural power—yes, I know about that," he adds with a thin, superior smirk. "But you do nothing worthwhile with it. None of you children deserve to have the powers that you do. Those powers make you unpredictable. Unruly. It is absolutely evident that you need a grownup to keep you in line. I should have gotten rid of your bad influence on Kingsport High long ago."

3: I can overpower him with magic.

title: An Odyssey: Echoes of War
obs:
"For what?" she asks.
"Can we have a few words?" you ask back. You take a seat.
She joins you and crosses her arms against her chest, waiting for you to speak.
"I hear you've been having trouble with some horses," you start.
She sniffles. "And? What is it to you?"
"Maybe I can help."
"How could you help?" she asks. "Nobody can save us from Diomedes and his beasts."
"Can you tell me about the beasts?"
She stares at you for a few moments, trying to decide whether she can trust you. Then, she wipes her nose with the back of her hand and starts talking: "There are four of them. Podarge the swift, Lampre the shining, Xanthe the yellow, and Deine the terrible. But they are all terrible, if you ask me. They come out at night to feast on human flesh. They drag you out of your bed, steal babies from their parents' laps. When they cannot find humans to mangle, they attack the animals." She pauses, her cheeks now red with anger. "Did you see any cattle as you were coming into the village? Any chickens, any pigs? No! The horses have eaten most of them, and driven the rest away." She covers her eyes with her palms. "There is no living for us here, anymore."
"I'm sorry," you say.
She uncovers her eyes and stares at you, or through you, not really seeing you at all. "I can still hear the sound their jaws made as they devoured my brother," she says. "What his flesh sounded like when it was being torn from his body, what his bones sounded like as the horses crunched them between their jaws."
You ask her about Diomedes, the man who controls the mares, to distract her from the horrors she has endured.
"He used to be the King of Thrace. He's the son of Ares and a harsh, unfair, war-loving king. One day, his people revolted against him and removed him, exiled him. He left Thrace, taking with him nothing but his horses. He had raised them on human flesh since they were foals, and so they developed an appetite for it. It drove them mad. Now Diomedes has found this little corner of the world to rule and make himself feel powerful. Whenever we disobey or he fears we might want to drive him away, he looses the horses on the villagers to keep us under control."
From Thrace, she says. You remember the harsh land where you spent the first years of your life. The wild mountains, the deep, unforgiving ravines, the freezing waterfalls.
Land has a way of inscribing itself on the bodies that inhabit it.
You can see why a king of Thrace would be harsh.
You can see how this land's creatures could be manipulated into madness.
"Haven't other heroes been here before me?" you ask. "Killed the mares, defeated Diomedes?"
She looks at you with a puzzled look on her face. "Other heroes?" She shakes her head. "I don't know what that means."
It's the sorcery that makes the caves work the way they do. As if the entire thing resets somehow after you're gone.
"I just have this feeling," she says. "This sense that I'm living and reliving the same nightmare over and over again." She raises her eyes to you, tears shimmering in their corners. "Is it never going to end? Can you really help us?"
"I can try," you say.
"But how?" she asks.

Without hesitation, you grab Demodocus's shoulders and stand him on his feet again.
He looks dazed, so you push him ahead of you and make him run.
You stay behind him the whole time, making sure he runs as fast as he can.
*****Run*****
You stumble down the path to the shore and throw yourselves into the sea as quickly as you can. Your breath burns your throat, your lungs fighting to keep up. You wade water at first and then you swim. Your crew is struggling behind you, weighed down by the supplies and treasure they grabbed.
But you all make it.

The cyclopes are now on the shore. They are grabbing boulders and throwing them at your ship with all their might, missing narrowly.
"Who are you?" they ask. "Who are you that killed our brother?"

The cyclopes' island recedes behind you. Your crew has finally started to calm down from all the excitement and exertion.

"Poseidon," Circe whispers, and her voice catches in her throat.

harm my son?"

But there is no time for any of that right now.
Poseidon raises his fist to the sky and calls up the winds. And the winds, like obedient servants, gather: the East Wind and the South Wind, full of heat, and the West Wind, the carrier of storms, and the heaven-born North Wind. They drive a vast wave before him and crash against your ship, splintering your deck.
Next to you, Demodocus's joints slacken and he sinks to his knees. "How black the sea, how black the clouds," he whimpers. "Now we are certainly doomed. Blessed and thrice blessed were those Achaeans who fell in Troy. I wish we'd been killed the day when the Trojans were pressing us so sorely on the battlefield around the dead body of Achilles, for then we should have had the burial we deserve and all of the Achaeans would have honored our names, and our bodies wouldn't be lost in the unsung depths of the cold sea."
Ajax grasps the back of Demodocus's neck with his giant arm and pulls him to his feet. It wouldn't be a surprise if he slapped the lad about the face a couple of times, but he refrains. You can no longer see Poseidon, but you can feel his wrath. It batters your ship, soaks your hair and skin with salt water, fills your lungs until you can no longer breathe.
And when you are certain that this is your final hour, that your ship will surely sink this time, the storm abates at once, as suddenly as it started.
You find yourself on calm waters again. The clouds disperse and the sun shines above, slowly drying your skin, your hair, your clothes. Your crew right themselves one by one, timidly, reluctantly, as if unable to believe you made it out alive.

title: The Cryptkeepers of Hallowford
obs:
You need to tell Sir Michael what's going on in town. You head for the gatehouse, hoping that the old knight is still in his office.
The trip takes longer than you would have hoped. The gate is almost on the other side of town, and Hallowford's streets are still nowhere as familiar to you as Kendrickstone's.
Still, despite a few false turns, you manage to work your way across the warren of narrow alleys and jumbled houses that make up the bulk of Hallowford's center. Finally you see the stone towers of the gatehouse rising over the houses before you.
**********
You find Sir Michael's cramped office packed with watch members as the veteran knight himself stands over his desk.
"—can't call up everyone just because some of us suspect that something's wrong," you hear him say. "I'd love to go in, swords drawn, but unless we can find some evidence of a crime or a threat to the town, then we'll have to wait for the Cryptkeepers to send us a message."
The entire room seems to turn to face you as you walk through the door.
"Will that do?" one of the guardsmen murmurs.
Sir Michael nods as you give him the gist of the situation at the guildhouse. Despite his age, he is more than vigorous enough to spring into action. Within moments, his subordinates are on their way out to call up the rest of the watch.
"Make no mistake," Sir Michael notes as the door closes shut behind the last messenger. "I am glad you finally ended up telling us what was going on, but couldn't you have at least told us sooner?"
You shake your head. "The Cryptkeepers wanted to keep it a secret."
"How typical of them." Sir Michael sighs. "I expect we'll be having a chat once the dust settles—if the dust settles. I'm getting sick and tired of all this secrecy."
The old knight reaches for his sheathed sword resting against his desk. "I suppose you'll be needed back at the guildhouse," he calls out over his shoulder. "Best get going."
**********
Your trip back from the gatehouse is a lot shorter than your way there. You don't make quite as many wrong turns now that you've gotten the route more or less memorized.
Along the way, you see Sir Michael's subordinates in action. They move from door to door, calling up the members of Hallowford's volunteer watch. You pass steady streams of crafters, laborers, traders, and other ordinary folk, their padded aketons tucked under their arms, as they head for the gatehouses to pick up their weapons and be transformed, at least for a day, into soldiers.
None have reached the guildhouse quite yet, though you can imagine some would start trickling in soon.
You can only hope that "soon" proves to be soon enough, and that their help will be enough to stop the Creatures when they launch their attack.
You're still thinking of what to do next when a shout of alarm calls you to the front doors.
**********
You arrive to find the walls of the guildhouse shedding puffs of whitewash, the wall behind it trembling. The defenders hold steady in their line, weapons at the ready.
The Cryptkeepers still carry only their improvised and scavenged weapons. They shake even as the walls shake, but they stand firm despite the horror that they are about to face. They know what is at stake, both for themselves and their guild. When you look into their eyes, you see the steady determination of those ready to fight and die for an organization that has been their entire life.
Your fellow adventurers are almost relaxed by comparison. They, too, have faced the Creatures, but unlike the others, each one of your colleagues is battle-hardened and experienced, well used to facing down impossible monstrosities and coming out on top. They wait with their weapons and spells at the ready, almost eager for battle.
Your allies are in position, and they are as ready as they'll ever be for what is to come.
The question is, where will you be?

title: The Cryptkeepers of Hallowford
obs:
You look to your allies and nod.
This is a chance you have to take.
If you're going to get out of this alive, you're going to have to destroy the Heart. To do that, you'll have to get through Lucan, his Cryptkeepers, and anyone else standing in your way. So long as they're distracted, you might have a chance of getting through.
You take a breath and run toward the cage of alien metal that holds the Heart at the center of the chamber.
But you are not fast enough. Lucan's Cryptkeepers
and Sir Michael's watch
may be fighting for their lives, but they still manage to spot you before you get anywhere near close enough.
A cry of alarm goes up. Someone points an arbalest your way. You back off, moving away to the edge of the central platform.
There are still too many who would stop you from destroying the Heart. Maybe if you waited for a better opportunity, after the Creatures have worn them down more.
Let the undying horrors do half your job for you. That'll make things easier.
**********
The undying surge forward against the last remnants of the forces of the living.
The last survivors of the two expeditions are on the verge of annihilation.
Lucan stands almost alone. Only two or three of his allies are still fit to fight. The rest lie broken upon the ancient floor or cower in the light of the Heart, in the morbid hope that they will be torn apart last.
Sir Michael and his watch are no better off. Their backs are to the Heart as well. With no place to retreat, the resolve in the handful of survivors at last begins to disintegrate into panic.
Watch, Cryptkeeper, adventurer…the distinctions have ceased to matter. If you don't do something soon, you will all be among the dead.

title: Psy High
obs:
"Wow, I'm sorry about you and Steve," you say vaguely. Half your mind is elsewhere, though, trying to overhear Mackenzie's thoughts.
But it's no use—you're too distracted. And so is she.
Mackenzie's eyes narrow. "What are you getting at, user_input? You don't care about me and Steve. You don't care about anything."
Uh-oh. Apparently you didn't sound sincere enough.
"You just get away from me!" she shouts.
You do. But as you do, you hear other people hurrying in your direction, and someone shouts, "Is everything okay?"
Uh-oh. You'd better be far away from here when Mackenzie tells people she just saw you.
You know you can't do this alone, and that's why you've spent so much time gathering up your friends and allies.
Now it's time to call on all those friends to make certain Mr. Pierce and Ms. Clay never get to the Nexus.
As the clock ticks towards midnight, the boat chugs towards the Nexus. From above, you can hear muffled laughter and music—the prom is still going strong. But those happy sounds feel very far away and very out of place compared to what’s happening here.
You’ve found the room on the lowest deck that will look directly out onto the Nexus. Through its single porthole, you can see a faint glow—most people would mistake it for moonlight, but even this far away you can sense the pulse of magic that tells you the Nexus itself is glowing.
You and your friends crowd around the door, blocking the way. When Mr. Pierce, Ms. Clay, and the Gold Crown Team come striding down the hallway, you're ready.
Haley gives you an uncertain look, then draws up straighter and calls, "All right, everyone! Let's go!"
The trouble is, the "everyone" Haley's talking to doesn't include that many people. They do their best—some a little frightened at the thought of facing down the principal, some defiant and resolute—but there just aren't enough people to keep Mr. Pierce away from the Nexus.
You worked hard, and you tried hard, and you counted on your friends, and your friends are helping you.
But it still isn't enough.
"I might have known that it would be you, user_input," snaps Mr. Pierce. "You're a bad seed, and you always have been. You and your little friends—you are nothing but a mob of children. Your priorities are entirely misplaced.
You are unruly and undisciplined.
You are disrespectful to your elders.
You have been given great supernatural power—yes, I know about that," he adds with a thin, superior smirk. "But you do nothing worthwhile with it. None of you children deserve to have the powers that you do. Those powers make you unpredictable. Unruly. It is absolutely evident that you need a grownup to keep you in line. I should have gotten rid of your bad influence on Kingsport High long ago."

title: An Odyssey: Echoes of War
obs:
"This one looks like it will take as many hands as possible," you say.
"We'll all come," Polyxena replies, looking sternly at everyone around her to preempt any disagreement. "No question about it."
On foot, you all pick up your weapons–Demodocus's is, of course, his lyre–and make your way to the entrance of the cave. Deep darkness lies ahead, and you cannot see nor hear anything beyond the cave's gaping maw.
*****Enter*****
As you step through the threshold, the smell of swamp assaults you. You are no longer in the land of the Heroes' Mist, that much is certain. Before you lies the lake of Lerna, from which the Hydra takes its name.
The smell is vile; it burns your nostrils. "Everyone, cover your noses," you say, and, turning to Demodocus, you ask: "What do you know of the Hydra?"
Demodocus, heartened by the attention, launches into a diatribe on the Lernaean Hydra's lore: How it was reared by Hera for the sole purpose of defeating Hercules with its poisonous blood and deadly teeth; how it terrorized the villages around Lake Lerna; how Hercules used both speed and strength to defeat it with the invaluable help of his friend.
You approach the swampy waters of the lake. As before, there is no sign of the cave you entered to find yourselves here. Only reeds, and rocks, and insects.
As you stand at the edge of the lake, everything seems quiet–serene, almost. And yet there is this sense of foreboding; the certainty that something dangerous lurks here.
You scour the still surface of the lake, green and thick with duckweed, and at first you can see nothing out of the ordinary.
*****Look More Closely*****
Then, you notice it.
In what you thought was a tangle of reeds and brambles, eyes.
Eyes, and teeth, and scales.
Looking straight at you, the head of the snake rises. It knows you've seen it now. It rises and rises until it stands high above you, as tall as two grown humans.
And beside it, eight more heads just like it. Nine slender necks sprouting from a mighty body still concealed beneath the grimy waters of the swamp.
This is it, hero. This is your time. Your moment of truth.

title: An Odyssey: Echoes of War
obs:
You ready yourself, and then you notice Demodocus preparing to follow you.
"Where do you think you're going?" you ask him.
This stops the poet in his tracks. "With you?" he says uncertainly.
"No," you reply. "I'm going alone."
You squeeze his shoulder. "I'll tell you all about it when I get back," you say.
"Promise?" he asks.
"I promise," you reply.
*****Enter*****
When you step through the threshold, the world shimmers around you and you realize you are not in a cave at all. Instead, you are in a new place altogether.
The first thing you notice is the sweet, bright light. Everything around you is tinted gold. The sun is shining low, near the end of its daily journey. But it's not just that. Everything around you is golden. The grass under your feet, the flowering shrubs, the gates to the orchard that stands before you.
This, then, is the Garden of Hespera, Hera's orchard, where it is always sunset.
Behind the gates, you can see a single apple tree, its branches bent with golden apples. A fruit from that tree that became the Apple of Discord, which in turn led to the Trojan War.
And behind the tree, you can see two enormous columns–but no, not columns at all, but legs, the legs of a Titan, so tall as to rival the mountain behind him. You look up, and you can hardly make out his torso, his arms, his neck straining under the weight of the sky. Atlas.
The gate squeaks open and three women appear in front of it. They are dressed in ocher, orange, and yellow robes threaded with gold. The Hesperides, daughters of Atlas, nieces of Nyx.
"A visitor," one of them says. "How wonderful. We were getting terribly bored."
"Don't be silly, Aegle," another replies. "He just wants the apples."
Aegle frowns. "You don't know that," she says. "Maybe this one's different."
The second woman turns to you, sizes you up. "Are you different?"
The third Hesperis takes a step forward. There is something menacing in her face now, something serpent-like. "Tell us what you want," she orders. "Do you want the apples?"

title: Psy High
obs:
You're in study hall with Mike, and you get there early so you can stop him on the way in. "Hey, Mike. I heard you were trying out for the Constable."
He nods. "That's right."
You push your way between Mike and the door, doing your best to fill up the space. "Yeah. About that." Your voice flattens and your eyes narrow. "I don't think it's such a good idea. Maybe you should do something else." Unspoken threats hang on every one of your words.
Mike draws back, but in disbelief, not fear. "What the heck are you doing, user_input? Are you trying to get me to not audition? No way am I going to drop out of Drama Club! Not this year. I'm going to be so busy next year that I might not get a chance to be in it at all, and Nate needs all the actors he can get."
"No, I mean—" you flounder, trying to salvage something from this conversation.
Mike shakes his head. "No way," he says flatly, pushing around you on his way into study hall.
Looks like you're going to have to audition against Mike after all. Oh well. You tried.
**********
The day of the Drama Club auditions rolls around, and everyone who's trying out files into the auditorium as soon as the last bell rings. You're uncomfortably aware of how few people are there. Maybe this will mean you'll have an easier time getting the part you want?
You're also unhappily aware that Mackenzie is there. Of course, she wants to play Emily Webb, one member of the young couple whose love story is the central arc of the plot. Emily gets the big tearjerking moment at the end when, from the afterlife, she says goodbye to the world she's leaving now that she's died.
"Goodbye to clocks ticking," Mackenzie recites, with a little catch in her voice. "And Mama's sunflowers, and food, and coffee…"
You hate to admit it, but Mackenzie's a good actor.
**********
"Thanks, Mackenzie," says Nate, scribbling a few notes on his clipboard. "Okay, user_input, you're up." He flips a few pages. "You'll read the Constable, and I'll read the other lines in the scene. Start whenever you're ready."
This is it! Your big moment.
What's your approach to your reading?

1: I'll put a little twist on the role to make my performance more memorable. It's a little risky, but I can pull it off.

3: I'll look at Nate's clipboard with my clairvoyance. Maybe he's got some notes about what he likes and doesn't like.

title: The Cryptkeepers of Hallowford
obs:
"Yeah, good idea," Adanna replied. "We've wasted enough time here."
It didn't take long for
Sam to pick up the magical trail yet again.
"It's stronger than before," he said half in surprise. "I barely even have to focus now."
You went deep below the surface then. How deep, you did not know. You were isolated from anything that might have told you, and you hadn't seen any signs of the other groups since you left Mundy and the others behind. Only the memory of the path back to the upper catacombs kept you and your companions from being entirely lost.
The tunnels around you didn't help there either. The air started growing warmer and drier, in defiance of all common sense. The torches, too, began to burn brighter even as their sconces took on shapes and forms utterly unrecognisable to you—alien loops and twists of material too hard and shiny to be iron.
It was in that brighter light that you began to notice the walls changing as well. No longer were they worn smooth by the passage of time. There were fewer cracks in them, their corners became even sharper, and their surfaces took on a glossy sheen, enough to reflect the orange light of the torches back onto you and your fellow adventurers.
Your surroundings weren't the only things that changed either.
The magical aura was getting stronger, so strong that even you were feeling it. There was no need to seek it out with your mind. No, it was everywhere, pressing against your head like a helmet that was just a little bit too small.
"Do you feel that?" Adanna asked, her voice full of worry.
"I do," you replied.
"We're getting close," Sam said gravely. "We must be, if the aura is strong enough for both of you to feel."
You nodded. "Then we better get ready to face whatever's pushing out that aura."
"Yeah," Sam agreed. "Maybe we can finally get some answers to wha—"
The rest of his words died on his lips as your fellow adventurer stopped in his tracks. The air filled with the stink of desiccated flesh and the rasping whisper of dry parchment…
…as you first laid your eyes on [i]it[/i].
**********
It had been human once, that much was obvious. It had two arms, two legs, a head, and a face.
Two arms, each one a disjointed horror of twisted bone shrouded in ragged scraps of long-dead skin. Its elbows were shrouded in dusty strands of decaying sinew, its skeletal hands clawed with long slender blades of yellowed nail.
Two legs, gnarled struts protruding from the reeking, distended ruin of a torso. One moment, it seemed on the verge of collapse, then the next it skittered forward with an impossible speed, its gnarled and decayed feet scraping tortured shrieks against the stone.
A head: long-dead flesh stretched over a misshapen and tortured skull.
A face: cold blue light shining out of empty sockets, tattered skin hanging in flaps over a death rictus of yellowed, cracked, and jagged teeth.
It had been human, [i]once[/i].
It wasn't anymore.
**********
You felt your hands tremble as the skeletal monstrosity advanced. Your every muscle and sinew cringed as its yellowed appendages skritched across the stone, as the horrific, impossible thing shambled toward you with terrifying agility.
The icy tentacles of fear crawled up your spine as cold sweat dripped down your back. Dangerous animals you had faced, criminals you had faced, but you had no idea how you could face this.
"We need to get back to the others!" you heard someone shout. Adanna? You weren't sure.
No, it had to have been, for it was Sam who spoke next: "Come on, Nameless! Get out of there!"
You tried to move as your companions retreated, but your legs only half answered. The Creature turned toward you, the baleful blue light from its face fading away to reveal the empty, rotted husks of dead eyes behind it.
Then it sprang at you, its arm coming out of the darkness like the barbed hooks of a whip, five cracked and twisted nails ripping through the damp, fear-soaked air…
**********
It's a miracle you're still alive.
It's a miracle that you managed to get away, that you hadn't gotten lost in the twisted passages of the lower catacombs. A miracle that you made it all the way back to that heavy iron-bound door in more or less one piece.
But you have no time to waste thinking about how you got here. Now, you need to figure out how you're going to get out.
You and your companions face not one but four of the horrific things, and it seems that your luck has finally run out. None of the other adventurers are anywhere to be seen, and the door presses cold and unyielding against your back.
"Great," Adanna snarls, her teeth gritting in frustration at a world that doesn't seem to have much fairness left in it. "What do we do now?"

1: "Break the door down. We need to fall back into the vaults."

You're not letting the cops' attitude get to you, are you? That's just the way they are, you know that."

Maybe I think too much, but that sort of excitement seems more than I like to deal with on a regular basis.
So I'm afraid that's it for me.
I honestly don't know how you can go on doing this. It's madness, and it's not for me.
"As you wish. If that's what you really want, I'm not going to press you."
User_input_2 wanders, almost idly, into the next room, and the door swings to behind them. You follow after, but…there's nobody there.
Opening the nearest window, you address the ledge above: "I'd be more impressed if I didn't know you were up there frantically making that quick change into the Swashbuckler outfit, User_input_2."
User_input_2, already masked, pokes their head over the ledge and grins down at you. "See? You know how it's all done already. Are you sure you won't reconsider?"
