title: The Cryptkeepers of Hallowford
obs:
"Why not just stand and fight here?" the Cryptkeeper asks. "We could defend this room."
You shake your head. "If we do that, the Creatures will just go around us, cut us off, and overwhelm us," you explain. "What we need to do is hold them off as long as we can, then fall back to the next room. We can barricade the doors to buy us some time to recover, but we can't let ourselves get pinned down."
So that's exactly what you do.
The next hour comes as a series of rapid, chaotic clashes as you and your allies fall back, room by room, winning just enough time to catch your breath before being assailed by the monstrosities again.
You fight at the forefront of every skirmish,
and you soon have the wounds to show for it: a handful of deep cuts and a long, bleeding gash along your thigh.
You aren't the only one taking wounds. Despite your best efforts, the constant attacks are taking their toll: bit by bit, your force is being worn to nothing. Only your unwillingness to stop retreating keeps their losses from being worse.
Though you look for ways to try to slow your pursuers down, you don't exactly have the time to plan intricate ambushes. As you give up room after room without seeming to do much damage to the Creatures at your heels, you feel your allies growing more and more disheartened.
You try your best to keep everyone's spirits up, but your best only falls flat as your allies seem to grow more and more hopeless. Soon it seems like you aren't even offering much of a fight at all before falling back again, room by room, until you find yourself fleeing through the front doors and into the courtyard.
**********
You stumble out into the bright light of the courtyard to find
yourself face-to-face with the leveled spear points of the town watch arrayed in readiness before you.
Edith looks at you in surprise. "Did you warn the watch that we were being attacked?"
You shake your head. "I never had the time to send anyone to warn them."
"You didn't need to,"
says a wiry, silver-haired man in maille and surcoat as he strides toward you with the gait of a veteran soldier. So this must be Sir Michael of Torinhall.
"Based on what you told me, I could put together the pieces myself. I
know there's some kind of threat underneath the guildhouse, though it'd be nice to know exactly what it is."
You explain as best you can as quickly as you're able, which admittedly isn't very well. It's hardly easy to describe a swarm of undying abominations to someone who's never seen them before.
Sir Michael evidently thinks so, too. "You're going to have to give me some more details.
These things sound like bone-horrors or rag-shamblers to me, but that can't be right."
"Look," you reply, trying to keep your impatience in check. "I'd love to draw you a sketch or something, but they're right behind us."
The old knight nods grimly as he hefts his blade. "All right, better get to work then." He raises his hand to point beyond his line of the town watch.
"Your fellow adventurers are setting up some kind of staging area just behind that corner. I'm sure they'd welcome your company."
You nod and begin to make your way back.
"Oh and, Nameless?"
You turn. Apparently Sir Michael is not quite finished.
"I should thank you," the gray-haired veteran says.
"We would have been caught off guard if it weren't for the fact that you told us enough of the truth to prepare us for something like this. However—" His eyes grow stern. "—that doesn't mean I won't be wanting the rest of it once this is over."
You nod. After this, you suppose you're going to have to give Sir Michael some answers.
**********
Your fellow adventurers rush toward you the moment they see you.
"Nameless!" Adanna shouts as she takes the lead. "Where betwixt heaven and sand have you been?"
"In there," you reply, jerking a thumb at the bulk of the guildhouse.
Questions follow. "What's going on?", "How bad is it?", "How many of the Cryptkeepers are alive?" You try to answer them as best you can, though with every answer, the faces looking back at you seem to get more and more grim.
"That sounds bad," someone says, as if that weren't obvious enough already.
You nod. "It is. What can I do to help?"
"That's actually what we were talking about," Adanna replies. "How to help out the guards, I mean."
"Got a few suggestions then?" you ask.
That gets your fellow adventurers talking all at once. It seems they've got more than a few ideas. "We could collapse the entrances. Lucan won't like it, but it'll slow the things down," says one.
"We can block the entrances with barricades, give us some proper defenses," suggests another.
"Set up some magical defenses!" pipes up a third. "That might stop them!"
"We should get the townsfolk away," a sober-faced woman suggests. "Warn them to get off the streets."
"Agreed," her companion echoes. "If we don't hold and those things get into town, it'll be a massacre if those people are caught in the open."
"I'm sure you've got some other ideas, too," Adanna adds.
"Although you might want to consider getting your wounds healed up first."
So what to do?
**********
You take another step forward as you try to figure out exactly what to do, but your legs seem to buckle under your weight. Your hand reaches out for the nearest wall as you suddenly find yourself unable to support your own weight.
The pain from your wounds redoubles. You need to see a healer. You can't move around, let alone fight like this.
Luckily for you, more than enough of your fellow adventurers are skilled in the process of magical healing.
It isn't difficult to find one who's willing to fix you up a bit. While the process is hardly pleasant, it does end up being surprisingly quick.
Evidently, she's had a lot of practice.
Unfortunately, your wounds prove too deep to be healed completely without time and a day of bedrest, something none of you have. Still, your healer tries her best. By the time she is done, most of your wounds are closed, and you feel fit enough to at least put up a decent fight, should things come to it.
You can only hope that will be enough.
You're still thinking of what to do next when a shout of alarm calls you to the front doors.
**********
You arrive to find the walls of the guildhouse shedding puffs of whitewash, the wall behind it trembling. The defenders hold steady in their line, weapons at the ready.
The Cryptkeepers still carry only their improvised and scavenged weapons. They shake even as the walls shake, but they stand firm despite the horror that they are about to face. They know what is at stake, both for themselves and their guild. When you look into their eyes, you see the steady determination of those ready to fight and die for an organization that has been their entire life.
Your fellow adventurers are almost relaxed by comparison. They, too, have faced the Creatures, but unlike the others, each one of your colleagues is battle-hardened and experienced, well used to facing down impossible monstrosities and coming out on top. They wait with their weapons and spells at the ready, almost eager for battle.
The members of the town watch stand ready as well.
Your warning gave them enough time to assemble at least a good portion of their force. Sir Michael stands with them now, his sword at the ready, his shield positioned in front of him in a fighter's stance. A half dozen of his volunteers stand behind him, clad in padded jackets and kettle helms, their spears and halberds held in unsteady fingers. Underneath their armor, they are still laborers and crafters, thrown from their mundane work into this sudden and desperate fight.
There are another dozen or so split between the other exits, each commanded by one of the old knight's subordinates.
Your allies are in position, and they are as ready as they'll ever be for what is to come.
The question is, where will you be?

1: I'll support my allies from the rear.
2: I'm going to stay back and make sure none of the Creatures get through.

title: It's Killing Time
obs:
Instantly smitten, like a lost soul who, at long last, has found a worthy mate, Phoenix approaches. She throws her arms around you, and the two of you embrace, your heart racing in your chest.
Her kiss is salty with sweat and seawater, but sweet all the same, and you realize that this is what you wanted all along. You realize, however, that you have one last piece of unfinished business: Boris.
The City of a Hundred Spires is astonishing, a piece of European art brought to life. Each residence and shop is a masterpiece, ornately carved facades adorning the window frames, each roof lined with spectacular tiles building to impeccable points.
Amid the buildings stand relic towers and ancient cathedrals, each lovingly carved and preserved in Gothic style, the brick hand-laid, dark stone standing in sharp counterpoint to the ever-present whitewashed walls and orange-red tile roofs.  Here and there, you see grey, stony accents dotting the white walls, the counterpoint of tones only making the city appear more magical.
Sitting in the Old Town Square of Prague, marveling at this jewel situated in the heart of the Czech Republic, you know the moment you've been dreaming about for the past six months is almost upon you.  Suddenly, a text message appears on your global phone, pulling you out of your reverie.
Glancing down at the words on your cell, you smile.  It's Boris's itinerary for the day, sent by your source inside the Crew.  Gingerly folding the newspaper you'd been using to obscure your face, you leave three hundred Czech crowns to cover the check, and slowly walk to another part of town.
**********
You lean back against a wall, trying to look like a casual tourist as people stroll by.  As you mull over what comes next, you take a moment to think back on how you'd gotten to this point, your target so close now, nearly within striking distance.
After leaving you high and dry, Boris had decided to start anew.  It had taken you some time, but you'd been able to locate the man who caused the destruction of the Syndicate.  When he'd heard about the Fallen Angels' failure, Boris had kept a low profile.  Still, he'd burned quite a few bridges over the years and, despite being a Russian ex-pat, he didn't have the Eastern Bloc ties he once did.  Boris had constructed a new assassin organization, known as the Crew, but you'd been able to get to one of the hitmen in his employ.  All it took was a well-timed bribe to get the guy out of gambling debt, and you now knew their workings inside and out.
[i]It's time for payback[/i], you think to yourself.  The Crew was small, consisting of five members including your source.  Your inside man was slated to feign horrible stomach problems today, so he wasn't a factor.  That left four well-trained, behind-the-Iron-Curtain-type mercenaries to contend with.  From what your source told you, you know that Boris goes nowhere without them.  He also would, no doubt, be on the lookout for danger, which upped the stakes.
You're running over the text and the list of options again, trying to decide the best avenue of attack, when you see a young boy approach.  He's limping, his clothes dirty and face stained with what looks like soot.  He shambles down the cobblestone street toward you and, when he gets close, he mutters in broken English, "A few crowns please? So hungry…"  His words trail off.  You know even ten crowns is only about half an American dollar.
Staring at the boy you decide to:
0: Give him twenty crowns.
1: Give him a hundred crowns.
2: Give him a thousand crowns.

title: Diabolical
obs:
"You fool." Cold claws wrap around your throat. You choke as the fingers of Hackmaster's exoskeleton tighten.
"Dani, what the hell are you doing?" you manage to wheeze out. She screams, and lifts you in front of the exoskeleton's face port. For the first time since you've known her, she opens the port, revealing her badly scarred face. You thought she was merely controlling the mech, but instead she's actually inside it, which make sense since her van can't travel through space.
"My. Name. Is. [i]Hackmaster[/i]!" she screeches, hurling you across the room. She turns her back on you and kneels before Doctor Arachnus.
"Master. Please. Teach me. I thought I knew what hatred was, but…but I look into your eyes and see the purity. Please."
You try to warn her, but there's no breath in your lungs. And so you have to watch as one of Doctor Arachnus's tentacles casually, almost gently, pulls Hackmaster from her armor. There is a snapping sound. You shouldn't feel bad about it. She was a traitor. You shouldn't.
Doctor Arachnus lets out a cackling laugh.
"Foolish mortal. Did you think my offer was genuine? Ara-kunos needs no assistance, has no equals. Only subjects, and slaves."
That's it, no one makes a fool out of you. Not even the world's deadliest supervillain.
**********
Here it is. Life or death. The ultimate fight. Choose wisely. The fate of the Earth depends on it.

"Okay," Mackenzie says slowly. "I'll find her." She looks much calmer now—more focused on the plan than on her own unhappiness. Whew.

You know you can't do this alone, and that's why you've spent so much time gathering up your friends and allies.

title: The Cryptkeepers of Hallowford
obs:
You rush into the melee, staff in hand, trying your best to drive the attacking Creatures back.
Every time, your staff strikes home, but it is you who staggers back, your arms numb from the shock of impact.
And it is your foe who rushes forward, claw flashing in the pale light.
The blow comes too quick to be dodged, too powerful to be parried. It tears deep into your side, rending cloth and flesh as if they're nothing. An explosion of raw agony shoots through your body.
You stagger back, barely on your feet, your vision blurred and your teeth clenched tight from the pain, your hands barely able to keep hold of your weapon.
You won't be able to take another hit like that.
**********
The Creatures do not relent. There is no driving them back. With every moment, more of the horrors claw their way up onto the platform.
The defense is coming apart. The Creatures surge deep into the mass of humanity, leaving a trail of broken bodies and rent limbs in their wake. Driving them back is futile. Your allies can only retreat and fight on.
Lucan and his Cryptkeepers fight hard, but their numbers are dwindling by the moment.
Sir Michael stands almost alone, most of his watch dead at his feet. Only a scant few are in any shape to fight on.
Yet the Creatures keep coming. No matter how hard they are struck or shot or burned, they get back up again. It is only a matter of time before the living are swarmed under by the dead.

Your eyes pick out the shape of the house in front of you. The half-timbered wall might prove a bit difficult to climb, but you spot the shape of a covered walkway to its side. Moving quickly, you hoist yourself up onto the shingled slope of the walkway's covering, then scramble up farther until you are on the roof of the house.
Now you can see the entire situation spread out in front of you. The Creatures are pouring out of all three exits, but your allies seem to be standing their ground, for now.
That doesn't mean they'll be able to hold out forever. The Creatures may seem small and distant from your lofty perch, but they attack with the same mindless ferocity you've come to expect from them.

title: An Odyssey: Echoes of War
obs:
"This one looks like it will take as many hands as possible," you say.
"We'll all come," Polyxena replies, looking sternly at everyone around her to preempt any disagreement. "No question about it."
On foot, you all pick up your weapons–Demodocus's is, of course, his lyre–and make your way to the entrance of the cave. Deep darkness lies ahead, and you cannot see nor hear anything beyond the cave's gaping maw.
*****Enter*****
As you step through the threshold, the smell of swamp assaults you. You are no longer in the land of the Heroes' Mist, that much is certain. Before you lies the lake of Lerna, from which the Hydra takes its name.
The smell is vile; it burns your nostrils. "Everyone, cover your noses," you say, and, turning to Demodocus, you ask: "What do you know of the Hydra?"
Demodocus, heartened by the attention, launches into a diatribe on the Lernaean Hydra's lore: How it was reared by Hera for the sole purpose of defeating Hercules with its poisonous blood and deadly teeth; how it terrorized the villages around Lake Lerna; how Hercules used both speed and strength to defeat it with the invaluable help of his friend.
You approach the swampy waters of the lake. As before, there is no sign of the cave you entered to find yourselves here. Only reeds, and rocks, and insects.
As you stand at the edge of the lake, everything seems quiet–serene, almost. And yet there is this sense of foreboding; the certainty that something dangerous lurks here.
You scour the still surface of the lake, green and thick with duckweed, and at first you can see nothing out of the ordinary.
*****Look More Closely*****
Then, you notice it.
In what you thought was a tangle of reeds and brambles, eyes.
Eyes, and teeth, and scales.
Looking straight at you, the head of the snake rises. It knows you've seen it now. It rises and rises until it stands high above you, as tall as two grown humans.
And beside it, eight more heads just like it. Nine slender necks sprouting from a mighty body still concealed beneath the grimy waters of the swamp.
This is it, hero. This is your time. Your moment of truth.

title: It's Killing Time
obs:
"Goodbye, Phoenix," you say, and she sighs, seeming to have expected it to go this way.  It doesn't take long until the thrashing begins.  Phoenix tries to get the fish away from her, but she is not in a good position, and her sudden movement only makes the fish strike faster.  The spiny tail digs into Phoenix's neck and the reaction is almost instantaneous.
Phoenix's flesh turns purplish as the venom spreads up her neck and face.  The Fire Lady sputters, unable to breathe, and her death, as excruciating as it looks, is mercifully short and quick.
[i]Cut off the head and the body will die[/i], you think to yourself, knowing that the Fallen Angels are no more.  Now, there's one last piece of unfinished business: Boris.
The City of a Hundred Spires is astonishing, a piece of European art brought to life. Each residence and shop is a masterpiece, ornately carved facades adorning the window frames, each roof lined with spectacular tiles building to impeccable points.
Amid the buildings stand relic towers and ancient cathedrals, each lovingly carved and preserved in Gothic style, the brick hand-laid, dark stone standing in sharp counterpoint to the ever-present whitewashed walls and orange-red tile roofs.  Here and there, you see grey, stony accents dotting the white walls, the counterpoint of tones only making the city appear more magical.
Sitting in the Old Town Square of Prague, marveling at this jewel situated in the heart of the Czech Republic, you know the moment you've been dreaming about for the past six months is almost upon you.  Suddenly, a text message appears on your global phone, pulling you out of your reverie.
Glancing down at the words on your cell, you smile.  It's Boris's itinerary for the day, sent by your source inside the Crew.  Gingerly folding the newspaper you'd been using to obscure your face, you leave three hundred Czech crowns to cover the check, and slowly walk to another part of town.
**********
You lean back against a wall, trying to look like a casual tourist as people stroll by.  As you mull over what comes next, you take a moment to think back on how you'd gotten to this point, your target so close now, nearly within striking distance.
After leaving you high and dry, Boris had decided to start anew.  It had taken you some time, but you'd been able to locate the man who caused the destruction of the Syndicate.  When he'd heard about the Fallen Angels' failure, Boris had kept a low profile.  Still, he'd burned quite a few bridges over the years and, despite being a Russian ex-pat, he didn't have the Eastern Bloc ties he once did.  Boris had constructed a new assassin organization, known as the Crew, but you'd been able to get to one of the hitmen in his employ.  All it took was a well-timed bribe to get the guy out of gambling debt, and you now knew their workings inside and out.
[i]It's time for payback[/i], you think to yourself.  The Crew was small, consisting of five members including your source.  Your inside man was slated to feign horrible stomach problems today, so he wasn't a factor.  That left four well-trained, behind-the-Iron-Curtain-type mercenaries to contend with.  From what your source told you, you know that Boris goes nowhere without them.  He also would, no doubt, be on the lookout for danger, which upped the stakes.
You're running over the text and the list of options again, trying to decide the best avenue of attack, when you see a young boy approach.  He's limping, his clothes dirty and face stained with what looks like soot.  He shambles down the cobblestone street toward you and, when he gets close, he mutters in broken English, "A few crowns please? So hungry…"  His words trail off.  You know even ten crowns is only about half an American dollar.

title: Diabolical
obs:
Doctor Arachnus probably assumes you're afraid of him. It's a reasonable assumption to make. After everything he's done, most people would fear him. But this time, it's different.
He should be afraid of you.
You've spent enough time with him that you know his greatest fears. And your mastery of fear as a weapon has taught you that it doesn't matter if you understand why he fears those things or not. title: The Cryptkeepers of Hallowford
obs:
"Cryptkeepers!" you shout. "Are you all so sure that keeping the Heart a secret is the right thing to do?"
"Lucan says that we have no choice," one Cryptkeeper shouts back. "That it's the only way to keep Hallowford prosperous and secure!"
You can't seem to muster a response to that, at least not one that the Cryptkeepers will accept.
Oh you try, of course, but no amount of persuasion seems to sway them. If anything, it only seems to make them more hostile.
Finally, you give up. You're not going to get through to this lot any time soon.
**********
"Enough!" Lucan snaps, his voice cutting the tense air. "There will be enough of this fruitless bickering! I, for one, demand that we waste no more time."
He points at Sir Michael
and the watch. "If you do not swear yourselves to secrecy right here and right now, then none of you will be leaving this chamber at all!"
Lucan's last words echo through the chamber, so loud that they almost seem to make the stone tremble beneath your feet.
Then the echoes stop, and you realize that the stone is trembling.
The others feel it, too. In but a moment, Lucan's ultimatum is forgotten as the shaking is joined by a dry, scraping rattle that grows louder and louder and louder.
Until the claws of the first Creatures crest the lip of the platform.
**********
Cries of shock and fear fill the chamber as the first of the Creatures clambers onto the platform. Cryptkeeper, watch, and adventurer alike turn outward, scrambling for the precious moments needed to mount a defense to this sudden threat.
The desiccated horrors are not waiting. They plunge into the confused mass with relentless speed. Shock and fear are drowned out by screams of agony as ragged claws and time-yellowed teeth rip into still-living flesh.
Your fellow adventurers are the first to get their bearings. They've faced unpleasant surprises before, and so have you. The unprepared watch and Cryptkeepers rally and, with frantic thrusts of spears and torches, begin to fight back.
**********
As the initial shock wears off, your allies and rivals both fight back with dogged ferocity. The line holds firm, and for a moment, it almost seems like you are pushing the Creatures back.
Lucan rallies his Cryptkeepers with remarkable efficiency. They form up around the Heart in a tight, steady formation, bristling with weapons.
The watch assemble at Sir Michael's back. The old knight holds two of the Creatures away from the Heart with his sword and the splintered remnants of his shield. In moments, a tight wall of spears and grimly determined faces guard the Watch Captain's flanks.
But this is the Heart of the Creatures' power, and they keep coming, impervious to steel and spellfire. One by one, the brave townsfolk of Hallowford fall, and unlike the Creatures, they do not get back up again.

title: An Odyssey: Echoes of War
obs:
You let out a scream so primal even the winds pause for a moment to catch their breath. You charge Eurylochus with all the force of your rage and punch him in the face, the shoulders, the chest. You punch and punch until the anger releases your limbs.
Eurylochus does not resist and does not fight you off, as if he deserves every bit of the punishment you unleash on him.
He lets his head hang low now, too bloody and too ashamed to meet your eyes.
You glance at the raw skin over your knuckles and walk away.
There is nothing to do right now but to wait and see where the winds take you.
**********
Many hours later, you find yourself on calm waters again. There is a stillness in the air, and the sun is shining above.
Then, you see.
"Oh no," you hear Circe say. "No no no no no."
**********
At first, you mistake what you see around you for kelp floating just under the surface of the water. Pieces of a shipwreck, perhaps, or driftwood sculpted by the salt-laced craft of the sea.
But then your mind catches up to your eyes, and then you make out the sunken faces, the shriveled skin, the nibbled toes, the tangles of hair still attached to decaying scalps.
"Talk to me, Circe," you say to the sorceress, because she seems to know where you are, what it is that's going on.
"We're in the Sirens' land," she says. "Dreadful creatures–half women, half beasts. They call them the Binders, the Entanglers. These poor wretches were caught by their song. They say that the Sirens' song bestows perfect knowledge and intense pleasure. But this," she gestures at the pieces of humans floating all around you, as far as your eye can see, "this is the price you pay."
"How did they get to be this way?" Polyxena asks.
"They were regular women, once. Some goddess punished them for their poor choices…" She trails off. You both see Polyxena is about to launch into a long and impassioned discussion of what "regular women" are or do, and there is clearly no time for that. "I don't actually know the details," Circe hastens to add. "Only what my grandmother told me when I was growing up."
"Can't we just sail around them?" Ajax asks.
"No," says Circe. She points at a cluster of jagged rocks up ahead. "The currents here are such that any ship caught has to drift by their shores. If we try to go against them, we'll be crushed against those rocks."
Demodocus turns to you. "What are we going to do, Jason?" he asks. "We've already survived so much. Perhaps our fortune has finally run out."

title: Psy High
obs:
And why should you? You've never liked her, and you've got bigger things to worry about right now. You sneak on past, leaving Mackenzie to her tears.
You know you can't do this alone, and that's why you've spent so much time gathering up your friends and allies.
Now it's time to call on all those friends to make certain Mr. Pierce and Ms. Clay never get to the Nexus.
As the clock ticks towards midnight, the boat chugs towards the Nexus. From above, you can hear muffled laughter and music—the prom is still going strong. But those happy sounds feel very far away and very out of place compared to what’s happening here.
You’ve found the room on the lowest deck that will look directly out onto the Nexus. Through its single porthole, you can see a faint glow—most people would mistake it for moonlight, but even this far away you can sense the pulse of magic that tells you the Nexus itself is glowing.
You and your friends crowd around the door, blocking the way. When Mr. Pierce, Ms. Clay, and the Gold Crown Team come striding down the hallway, you're ready.
Haley gives you an uncertain look, then draws up straighter and calls, "All right, everyone! Let's go!"
The trouble is, the "everyone" Haley's talking to doesn't include that many people. They do their best—some a little frightened at the thought of facing down the principal, some defiant and resolute—but there just aren't enough people to keep Mr. Pierce away from the Nexus.
You worked hard, and you tried hard, and you counted on your friends, and your friends are helping you.
But it still isn't enough.
"I might have known that it would be you, user_input," snaps Mr. Pierce. "You're a bad seed, and you always have been. You and your little friends—you are nothing but a mob of children. Your priorities are entirely misplaced.
You are unruly and undisciplined.
You are disrespectful to your elders.
You have been given great supernatural power—yes, I know about that," he adds with a thin, superior smirk. "But you do nothing worthwhile with it. None of you children deserve to have the powers that you do. Those powers make you unpredictable. Unruly. It is absolutely evident that you need a grownup to keep you in line. I should have gotten rid of your bad influence on Kingsport High long ago."

title: The Cryptkeepers of Hallowford
obs:
There's only one place in town where the news might spread fast enough to reach the entire population before things get ugly: the sanctuary.
The building isn't exactly difficult to find. It towers over the houses around it. More important, it's only a few blocks away from the Cryptkeepers guildhouse.
You suppose Lucan would have tried to stop you from warning the town. Even in a crisis like this, he would have wanted to keep the whole thing secret.
But Lucan isn't here to stop you.
**********
You find Justice Hortensia in between audiences, her gavel still in her hand as she sits judgment over the sanctuary's polished stone dais.
Your warning is quick and to the point. The silver-haired Justice's expression settles into a look of grim resolution.
"All right. Our first priority is getting the townsfolk off the streets," she says. She turns to her attendants. "Get the word out. Remind them the sanctuary has stone walls and a stout door. It'll be safer than most houses. If any folk live close to the gates, it might be better for them to get out of town altogether."
One by one, she sends off her junior clerics to warn each district of town. Only when the last leaves does she turn to you.
"You could have warned us sooner," she says with only the barest hint of sourness in her voice. "Knowing that there were monsters under our feet before they actually attacked would have been nice."
"Lucan wanted to keep it a secret," you reply. "He thought he'd be able to handle the situation without it spilling over into town."
"Yes, that certainly went well, didn't it?" The Justice scowls. "Next time something like this happens—if there is a next time, that is—I'll expect you to put the lives of this town's inhabitants over what Lucan of the Cryptkeepers thinks is best for his bottom line."
With that brief scolding, you are sent off back to the guildhouse. By the time you get back, you can already see men and women in Watchers' robes, knocking on doors and shouting warnings from street corners. The townsfolk should be able to get to relative safety in time.
You're still thinking of what to do next when a shout of alarm calls you to the front doors.
**********
You arrive to find the walls of the guildhouse shedding puffs of whitewash, the wall behind it trembling. The defenders hold steady in their line, weapons at the ready.
The Cryptkeepers still carry only their improvised and scavenged weapons. They shake even as the walls shake, but they stand firm despite the horror that they are about to face. They know what is at stake, both for themselves and their guild. When you look into their eyes, you see the steady determination of those ready to fight and die for an organization that has been their entire life.
Your fellow adventurers are almost relaxed by comparison. They, too, have faced the Creatures, but unlike the others, each one of your colleagues is battle-hardened and experienced, well used to facing down impossible monstrosities and coming out on top. They wait with their weapons and spells at the ready, almost eager for battle.
The members of the town watch stand ready as well.
Your warning and your fighting retreat bought some time for them to muster, but perhaps not enough. Only a fraction of the watch seems to have reached you in time. Sir Michael leads a small group of them beside you, with his sword in one hand and a shield emblazoned with the crest of the Duke of Torinhall in the other. His volunteers carry their spears and halberds unsteadily behind him. For all of their padded aketons and steel kettle helms, these are still ordinary townsfolk, thrust from their normal lives into a dire situation they may not survive. They have every right to be afraid.
More of them wait before the other exits, each led by one of Sir Michael's senior watch members.
Your allies are in position, and they are as ready as they'll ever be for what is to come.
The question is, where will you be?

title: The Cryptkeepers of Hallowford
obs:
You look to your allies and nod.
This is a chance you have to take.
If you're going to get out of this alive, you're going to have to destroy the Heart. To do that, you'll have to get through Lucan, his Cryptkeepers, and anyone else standing in your way. So long as they're distracted, you might have a chance of getting through.
You take a breath and run toward the cage of alien metal that holds the Heart at the center of the chamber.
But you are not fast enough. Lucan's Cryptkeepers
and Sir Michael's watch
may be fighting for their lives, but they still manage to spot you before you get anywhere near close enough.
A cry of alarm goes up. Someone points an arbalest your way. You back off, moving away to the edge of the central platform.
There are still too many who would stop you from destroying the Heart. Maybe if you waited for a better opportunity, after the Creatures have worn them down more.
It's a morbid prospect, letting the undying kill and maim Hallowford's defenders so that you can get close enough to destroy the Heart, but if that's what it takes to get anyone out alive, then that's what must be done.
**********
The undying surge forward against the last remnants of the forces of the living.
Only a handful are still on their feet and fighting.
Lucan and the last holdouts of his Cryptkeepers are on the verge of destruction. But with magic and steel, they cling to a tiny patch of bloodied stone, even as their knot of defenders grows smaller and smaller.
Sir Michael and his last few watch members are no better off. They fall back the last few steps until their backs are pressed against the harsh light of the Heart itself.
With every passing second, the dead advance. With every moment, despair grows in the eyes of the living. This can't go on for much longer.

With an overhand twirl, you bring your weapon up over your head. You spin the weapon once, twice, building momentum, before loosing your shot into the tide of the undying.
At this range, it's almost impossible to miss. Your shot flies true and strikes home with a sharp crack.
Yet the Creature you hit only flinches for an instant, almost more in surprise than anything else. Then it springs forward, once again on the attack.
**********

The last survivors of the two expeditions are on the verge of annihilation.
Lucan stands almost alone. Only two or three of his allies are still fit to fight. The rest lie broken upon the ancient floor or cower in the light of the Heart, in the morbid hope that they will be torn apart last.

Watch, Cryptkeeper, adventurer…the distinctions have ceased to matter. If you don't do something soon, you will all be among the dead.

title: The Cryptkeepers of Hallowford
obs:
You rush into the melee, staff in hand, trying your best to drive the attacking Creatures back.
Every time, your staff strikes home, but it is you who staggers back, your arms numb from the shock of impact.
And it is your foe who rushes forward, claw flashing in the pale light.
The blow comes too quick to be dodged, too powerful to be parried. It tears deep into your side, rending cloth and flesh as if they're nothing. An explosion of raw agony shoots through your body.
You stagger back, barely on your feet, your vision blurred and your teeth clenched tight from the pain, your hands barely able to keep hold of your weapon.
You won't be able to take another hit like that.
**********
The Creatures do not relent. There is no driving them back. With every moment, more of the horrors claw their way up onto the platform.
The defense is coming apart. The Creatures surge deep into the mass of humanity, leaving a trail of broken bodies and rent limbs in their wake. Driving them back is futile. Your allies can only retreat and fight on.
Lucan and his Cryptkeepers fight hard, but their numbers are dwindling by the moment.
Sir Michael stands almost alone, most of his watch dead at his feet. Only a scant few are in any shape to fight on.
Yet the Creatures keep coming. No matter how hard they are struck or shot or burned, they get back up again. It is only a matter of time before the living are swarmed under by the dead.

title: It's Killing Time
obs:
You pat your pockets and shrug your shoulders, holding your hands out in an "I have no money" gesture.  You apologize and tell the boy that you just don't have any cash on you and that he should look for real work.  You even point to another young boy who is working at a food stand.  He nods, seeming to understand you.  Making one final attempt he says, "No crowns for Boris?"  A bit startled by the boy's name, you shake you head and he moves on, walking farther down the street to talk to other people.
As he does, you look back and forth, furtively, trying to make sure you haven't been made.  After a few minutes, you're confident you haven't been, that his name was just a coincidence.
As he does, you look back and forth, furtively, trying to make sure you haven't been made.  After a few minutes, you're confident you haven't been, that it was just a coincidence.
Turning back to your thoughts, still a little shocked by the urchin's name, you review Boris's plan for the day.  He's going to be taking lunch in a cafe off the square, meeting with a business acquaintance.  Being in the square yourself, you look around and realize that it's unlikely you'll be able to make a sniper shot due to the close proximity of the buildings near the cafe.
You decide it's best to scope out the restaurant up close and, as you do, you see a network of alleyways leading to other areas of the city.  You figure Boris must want a clandestine meeting place because this part of the town is relatively secluded.  You realize it would be the perfect spot for a run-by shooting, the warren of alleys enabling you to disappear to another part of town after the deed was done.  Saving that as one option, you run down the list to see where else Boris will be going today.
After lunch, Boris is slated to meet with a gambling kingpin in an upscale, historical hotel.  You know that you'll be able to get in with no problem, but reason that guns are going to have to be out because, even with a silenced weapon, with the old Czech construction, you're likely to put a bullet into another room and bring the police running.
Finishing up the list, you realize there's another option if you wait until Boris has dinner.  He's scheduled to have his supper at a place called Golem Cafe.  The message says there's going to be a big event there tonight, so a direct attack of any kind isn't likely to be successful.  You figure that you can likely find a chef to bribe and try to poison Boris and his crew.
**********
Thinking of the options, a you can't help but circle back to the beggar boy and his name.  Boris.  The same name of the man who sold you out, his betrayal made so much worse since he had been like a father to you.
You know in your heart that you had been like a child to Boris, and you wonder if it would be even better revenge to sneak into Boris's home when he was gone, leaving a black lily on his pillow, the Russian symbol of death.  You contemplate the notion, knowing that Boris would not only forever be watching over his shoulder, wondering if you were going to strike, but he would also be confronted with the fact that you could have killed him and didn't.  You wonder if that's crueler, forcing Boris to live with his guilt for the rest of his days.
Contemplating it all, you also realize you have one other option.  You could let it go.  You recognize that you could forgive Boris for what he did and move on, even though it would be difficult.
In the end, you decide to:

title: Psy High
obs:
Your car is battered and ancient, but it is indubitably free.
Fortunately, Simone doesn't seem to mind that the ride is a little less than glamorous. She's too focused on the prom itself.
**********
Members of the Gold Crown Team have been preparing for weeks to ensure that the prom will be a satisfactory and well-run event. Part of that planning was to bring on board the Vinculum, which has been in Room 014 all year. You are not entirely certain what the Vinculum's purpose is. Whenever you try to think about it, you hear an odd hum in your mind, and you cannot concentrate.
But Mr. Pierce and Ms. Clay instructed you to bring the Vinculum to the prom, and so you all agreed.
One person dared to question Mr. Pierce and Ms. Clay, asking, "What is it for?"
Mr. Pierce smiled thinly. "It is art."
That seemed to be a satisfactory answer. All you need to know is that you were instructed to do this, and so you did it.
**********
Under the bright stars in the darkness of a spring evening, the junior class of Kingsport High—and a few assorted non-junior dates—walk up the gangplank of the huge boat to begin the prom.
Strings of sparkling lights wrap around the railings of the boat and outline a glittering archway at the entrance to the dance floor, which takes up almost the entire upper deck. Belowdecks there are a few private rooms where people can go for quiet moments away from the dancing—there's a game room and one with couches for talking—but most of the action will take place here, under the stars.
You've done enough research on the boat to know which rooms will have the best access to the Nexus, and to locate the bridge, where the boat's pilot will be. There's also a private room for the Gold Crown Team, of course.
In the meantime, though, everyone is dancing, laughing, and parading around in tuxes and gowns. Lisa and Dave are wrapped in each other's arms, slowdancing to every song, even the fast ones. Casey and Emma wear shimmery gowns and radiant grins as they mingle with the popular crowd. Mackenzie makes sure everyone notices her, too—she's with Steve, captain of the football team.
**********
The prom is an entirely frivolous pursuit. You do not care at all about romance or clothing or fashion—those are not the priorities of a model citizen. You are only attending because Mr. Pierce said that every member of the Gold Crown Team should be present. You will follow Mr. Pierce's instructions, and in doing so, you will help make Kingsport High a better and more orderly place.
In a private room at the bow of the boat, you mingle with the rest of the Gold Crown Team. It's a very quiet group: nobody is dancing; nobody is admiring each other's clothes or joking about getting dressed up. Instead, they're talking about school. You spot Jen holding an earnest conversation with Antonio—who used to be in the drama club before he became a model citizen—about college applications and summer internships.
After a few more minutes, Mr. Pierce steps up to the front of the room, and everyone falls silent. "Good evening, members of the Gold Crown Team. This is going to be a great night for all of us. You are truly doing your part to make Kingsport High a better place, and after tonight, we will be even further along on our road to success.
"Here is the procedure that I expect all of you to follow tonight. First, there will be an intermission at midnight. At that time, all of you are to proceed to the room directly below where we are now. You must keep away the rowdier elements who would try to disrupt me. Not everyone cares as much about Kingsport High as you do."
As he talks, his hand rests over his heart. At first, you think it's just a gesture of sincerity. Then, you think he's just fiddling with his antique tie-charm. But then, you realize that the antique silver tie-charm has a little design on it that looks just like the Vinculum. That's almost definitely the silver talisman that will help him focus his magic.
**********
"You are dismissed, citizens," Mr. Pierce concludes. "I will see you again shortly before midnight."
Everyone files out of the room in a neat line—no shoving or cutting, just orderly movement.
**********
While the rest of the Gold Crown Team heads off to enjoy the prom, you stay behind. You're determined to stick with Mr. Pierce all night, and if that means skipping some of the dancing, so be it.
Simone isn't quite as determined as you are, though. "Um, user_input?" she whispers. "Can we go dance now? We're supposed to be having fun! We'll look like losers if we don't dance at least a little."

1: "Just once dance, but then I need to come back here."
2: "Well…okay."

title: The Cryptkeepers of Hallowford
obs:
You look to your allies and nod.
This is a chance you have to take.
If you're going to get out of this alive, you're going to have to destroy the Heart. To do that, you'll have to get through Lucan, his Cryptkeepers, and anyone else standing in your way. So long as they're distracted, you might have a chance of getting through.
You take a breath and run toward the cage of alien metal that holds the Heart at the center of the chamber.
But you are not fast enough. Lucan's Cryptkeepers
and Sir Michael's watch
may be fighting for their lives, but they still manage to spot you before you get anywhere near close enough.
A cry of alarm goes up. Someone points an arbalest your way. You back off, moving away to the edge of the central platform.
There are still too many who would stop you from destroying the Heart. Maybe if you waited for a better opportunity, after the Creatures have worn them down more.
It's a morbid prospect, letting the undying kill and maim Hallowford's defenders so that you can get close enough to destroy the Heart, but if that's what it takes to get anyone out alive, then that's what must be done.
**********
The undying surge forward against the last remnants of the forces of the living.
Only a handful are still on their feet and fighting.
Lucan and the last holdouts of his Cryptkeepers are on the verge of destruction. But with magic and steel, they cling to a tiny patch of bloodied stone, even as their knot of defenders grows smaller and smaller.
Sir Michael and his last few watch members are no better off. They fall back the last few steps until their backs are pressed against the harsh light of the Heart itself.
With every passing second, the dead advance. With every moment, despair grows in the eyes of the living. This can't go on for much longer.

title: An Odyssey: Echoes of War
obs:
You know you shouldn't tell him. You know that not much good will come of this, but you are too proud of yourself. You can't help but brag about how clever you and your crew are. You duped Polyphemus, Poseidon's own son. Why shouldn't you take ownership of your glory?
"Polyphemus!" you shout, your chest puffing with pride. "My name is Ramseus. I could have stolen your treasure and you gave it to me without my even having to ask. What a fool I have made of you!"
**********
The cyclopes' island recedes behind you. Your crew has finally started to calm down from all the excitement and exertion.
The ship sails calmly for two whole days. But on the third day, the sky darkens suddenly and a great roar rises from the depths.
"Poseidon," Circe whispers, and her voice catches in her throat.
A wave as tall as a giant rises before you, and in its heart you glimpse the mighty god, the Earth-Shaker, seizing his trident in his hand, stirring up the sea. He rides a chariot made of shells and corals, dragged by enormous mares. Their manes are made of foam, and their hind legs disappear into fish tails. You've seen the likeness of these beasts before, in pictures assembled by tiny pieces of colored glass adorning the floors of your palace, back in Ithaca. Hippocampi.
Poseidon strikes the edge of the wave with the tip of his trident, and your ship is covered with vapor. "Ramseus!" he roars. "How dare you
taunt my son?"
This is the result of your bragging. Your pride brought this upon you and your crew.
But there is no time for any of that right now.
Poseidon raises his fist to the sky and calls up the winds. And the winds, like obedient servants, gather: the East Wind and the South Wind, full of heat, and the West Wind, the carrier of storms, and the heaven-born North Wind. They drive a vast wave before him and crash against your ship, splintering your deck.
Next to you, Demodocus's joints slacken and he sinks to his knees. "How black the sea, how black the clouds," he whimpers. "Now we are certainly doomed. Blessed and thrice blessed were those Achaeans who fell in Troy. I wish we'd been killed the day when the Trojans were pressing us so sorely on the battlefield around the dead body of Achilles, for then we should have had the burial we deserve and all of the Achaeans would have honored our names, and our bodies wouldn't be lost in the unsung depths of the cold sea."
Ajax grasps the back of Demodocus's neck with his giant arm and pulls him to his feet. It wouldn't be a surprise if he slapped the lad about the face a couple of times, but he refrains. "Pull yourself together, poet!" he shouts. "And if you so wish for death, I'll make sure you get your due, once we're out of this cursed storm!"
**********
Enormous waves keep crashing against the hull of your ship, and you all scramble to keep yourselves tethered to the deck, or you'll be lost for good, drowned, feast for whatever lurks underneath the surface of this sea.
You can no longer see Poseidon, but you can feel his wrath. It batters your ship, soaks your hair and skin with salt water, fills your lungs until you can no longer breathe.
And when you are certain that this is your final hour, that your ship will surely sink this time, the storm abates at once, as suddenly as it started.
You find yourself on calm waters again. The clouds disperse and the sun shines above, slowly drying your skin, your hair, your clothes. Your crew right themselves one by one, timidly, reluctantly, as if unable to believe you made it out alive.
Then, you see.
"Oh no," you hear Circe say. "No no no no no."
**********
At first, you mistake what you see around you for kelp floating just under the surface of the water. Pieces of a shipwreck, perhaps, or driftwood sculpted by the salt-laced craft of the sea.
But then your mind catches up to your eyes, and then you make out the sunken faces, the shriveled skin, the nibbled toes, the tangles of hair still attached to decaying scalps.
"Talk to me, Circe," you say to the sorceress, because she seems to know where you are, what it is that's going on.
"We're in the Sirens' land," she says. "Dreadful creatures–half women, half beasts. They call them the Binders, the Entanglers. These poor wretches were caught by their song. They say that the Sirens' song bestows perfect knowledge and intense pleasure. But this," she gestures at the pieces of humans floating all around you, as far as your eye can see, "this is the price you pay."
"How did they get to be this way?" Polyxena asks.
"They were regular women, once. Some goddess punished them for their poor choices…" She trails off. You both see Polyxena is about to launch into a long and impassioned discussion of what "regular women" are or do, and there is clearly no time for that. "I don't actually know the details," Circe hastens to add. "Only what my grandmother told me when I was growing up."
"Can't we just sail around them?" Ajax asks.
"No," says Circe. She points at a cluster of jagged rocks up ahead. "The currents here are such that any ship caught has to drift by their shores. If we try to go against them, we'll be crushed against those rocks."
Demodocus turns to you. "What are we going to do, Ramseus?" he asks. "We've already survived so much. Perhaps our fortune has finally run out."

1: Plug everyone's ears and kill the Sirens to save future passing sailors. Riskier, but heroic.
2: Have everyone's ears plugged with beeswax and myself tied to the mast, hoping the rope will hold.

title: Siege of Treboulain
obs:
"The Skegg live a nomadic life on barren grasslands far to the north of Treboulain," you say. "A summer's day could see brutal heat that burns skin and drains water. Yet that same night could plummet to temperatures well below freezing. Their winters are long and harsh, with food growing extremely scarce. Yet despite all this adversity, they've survived this lifestyle for hundreds of years, continuing to expand their reach ever-further into the north. The average Skegg person is much tougher than us. That doesn't help our case, not when we're fighting against superior numbers."
You remember studying in Ralexia with Markov. No matter how hard you studied, he always stayed up later. There was a grit about him that you've never seen in a Treboulain citizen. Here, arborturgists make sure there's plenty of food, the weather is decent all year, and people live great lives without ever leaving the city's walls.
Life in Treboulain is comfortable. Most people see that as a blessing, but when it comes to a contest against the Skegg…well, their hardship has certainly given them sharper teeth. Hopefully you'll have the smarts to make up for this disadvantage.
"That's a great bit of context," says Heartstone. "I'm always telling my soldiers they need to understand their enemies before they can defeat them."
He grabs a saber from a nearby table. It's a slightly curved, double-edged weapon that narrows to a pointed end designed for thrusting. According to Markov, the curve makes it easier to wield from atop a horse.
"This is a standard-issue Skegg blade." Heartstone holds it aloft so that the soldiers can see. "We recovered it from a dead soldier. Sovereign Ivy, perhaps you would like to take this blade and demonstrate some common Skegg attacks? We've blunted the edge, so you don't have to worry about harming me."
Heartstone hands you the blade. He draws a wooden training longsword made in the standard Treboulain style, then gestures for you to attack.
What aspect of the Skegg's combat style will you demonstrate?

title: An Odyssey: Echoes of War
obs:
"I think I'll take this one on my own," you say.
You turn to Demodocus, who's obviously itching to argue his case about how essential he is to all of your feats. "You can come along," you say.
Demodocus beams at you. Together, you
make your way to the entrance of the cave that will lead you to the land of the Stymphalian birds.
*****Enter*****
As soon as you step through the threshold, you find yourself on an island in the Euxine sea. You are at the top of a cliff. Behind you lies the vast sea with its winds and waves, and before you is a forest, thick and evergreen.
"Talk to me, Demodocus," you say. "What do you know of these birds?"
"Brought up by Ares, the god of war, they used to reside near the swamp in Stymphalia, from which they received their name. They have bronze beaks, with which they gorge themselves on the flesh of humans, and metallic feathers that they can launch at their pursuers like spears." Demodocus smooths back his hair, clearly disturbed by his own recounting of the story. "They terrorized the people of Stymphalia, killing livestock and villagers alike, until Hercules killed half of them and drove the rest away."
"And now, here they are, and it is our turn to face them," you say.
And indeed, there they are, rising from the canopy, their beaks reflecting the light of the sun, their metal wings clanging as they stab the air. And there, where wing connects with body, a crescent of soft, unarmored flesh.
"According to some versions of the story," Demodocus adds, "they are not birds at all, but women, the daughters of Stymphalus and Ornis, punished for being inhospitable to Hercules." He shrugs, motioning towards the metal beasts. "But, obviously, this is not the case."
They screech as they rise, their voices like the clanging of swords in battle.
You can see five birds in total.
"This is it, Demodocus," you say. "Let's see what we are worth."

title: The Cryptkeepers of Hallowford
obs:
You rush into the melee, staff in hand, trying your best to drive the attacking Creatures back.
Every time, your staff strikes home, but it is you who staggers back, your arms numb from the shock of impact.
And it is your foe who rushes forward, claw flashing in the pale light.
The blow comes too quick to be dodged, too powerful to be parried. It tears deep into your side, rending cloth and flesh as if they're nothing. An explosion of raw agony shoots through your body.
You stagger back, barely on your feet, your vision blurred and your teeth clenched tight from the pain, your hands barely able to keep hold of your weapon.
You won't be able to take another hit like that.
**********
The Creatures do not relent. There is no driving them back. With every moment, more of the horrors claw their way up onto the platform.
The defense still holds, but it won't for much longer. The Creatures rip and tear at the fringes, cutting down anyone who is not forced back. The stink of fear mingles with the stench of fresh blood.
Lucan and his Cryptkeepers fight hard, but their numbers are dwindling by the moment.
The watch holds firm, for now. But with each fresh attack, fewer of
Sir Michael's
followers remain standing.
Yet no effort can change the simple fact that the undying monsters cannot be felled, their numbers cannot be thinned. Inevitably, the living will give way to the dead.

title: An Odyssey: Echoes of War
obs:
You let out a scream so primal even the winds pause for a moment to catch their breath. You charge Eurylochus with all the force of your rage and punch him in the face, the shoulders, the chest. You punch and punch until the anger releases your limbs.
Eurylochus does not resist and does not fight you off, as if he deserves every bit of the punishment you unleash on him.
He lets his head hang low now, too bloody and too ashamed to meet your eyes.
You glance at the raw skin over your knuckles and walk away.
There is nothing to do right now but to wait and see where the winds take you.
**********
Many hours later, you find yourself on calm waters again. There is a stillness in the air, and the sun is shining above.
Then, you see.
"Oh no," you hear Circe say. "No no no no no."
**********
At first, you mistake what you see around you for kelp floating just under the surface of the water. Pieces of a shipwreck, perhaps, or driftwood sculpted by the salt-laced craft of the sea.
But then your mind catches up to your eyes, and then you make out the sunken faces, the shriveled skin, the nibbled toes, the tangles of hair still attached to decaying scalps.
"Talk to me, Circe," you say to the sorceress, because she seems to know where you are, what it is that's going on.
"We're in the Sirens' land," she says. "Dreadful creatures–half women, half beasts. They call them the Binders, the Entanglers. These poor wretches were caught by their song. They say that the Sirens' song bestows perfect knowledge and intense pleasure. But this," she gestures at the pieces of humans floating all around you, as far as your eye can see, "this is the price you pay."
"How did they get to be this way?" Polyxena asks.
"They were regular women, once. Some goddess punished them for their poor choices…" She trails off. You both see Polyxena is about to launch into a long and impassioned discussion of what "regular women" are or do, and there is clearly no time for that. "I don't actually know the details," Circe hastens to add. "Only what my grandmother told me when I was growing up."
"Can't we just sail around them?" Ajax asks.
"No," says Circe. She points at a cluster of jagged rocks up ahead. "The currents here are such that any ship caught has to drift by their shores. If we try to go against them, we'll be crushed against those rocks."
Demodocus turns to you. "What are we going to do, Ramseus?" he asks. "We've already survived so much. Perhaps our fortune has finally run out."
0: Plug everyone's ears with beeswax and sail past them. This is the smartest, least risky thing to do.
1: Plug everyone's ears and kill the Sirens to save future passing sailors. Riskier, but heroic.
2: Have everyone's ears plugged with beeswax and myself tied to the mast, hoping the rope will hold.
3: This whole heroic setup sounds suspicious to me. Sit down and have a real conversation with these women.

title: The Cryptkeepers of Hallowford
obs:
"Right, let's go," Adanna replied impatiently. "We've wasted enough time here."
It didn't take long for Adanna to pick up the trail of the missing Cryptkeepers. Within moments, she was forging on ahead, leading you and Sam once more into the tunnels.
You went deep below the surface then. How deep, you did not know. You were isolated from anything that might have told you, and you hadn't seen any signs of the other groups since you left Mundy and the others behind. Only the memory of the path back to the upper catacombs kept you and your companions from being entirely lost.
The tunnels around you didn't help there either. The air started growing warmer and drier, in defiance of all common sense. The torches, too, began to burn brighter even as their sconces took on shapes and forms utterly unrecognisable to you—alien loops and twists of material too hard and shiny to be iron.
Yet even as your surroundings became more and more impossible, Adanna advanced with greater and greater excitement. "The trail's getting stronger," she said as she pointed at a set of marks in the stone, showing bright under the unnaturally powerful torches.
"Look, scuff marks," she continued, her words spilling out faster and faster. "They were made in a hurry, and they still smell like stale sweat, the kind that a cornered animal gives off." She looked at you, eyes flashing. "Do you know what that means?"
The answer was obvious. "They were running."
"Not just running," Adanna corrected. She turned to point at a shiny sliver embedded deep into a jagged crack in the stone floor—a fragment from a steel blade. "They were fighting it, too."
Fighting and losing. Not ten paces beyond the piece of shattered steel was another clue, a trail of brown stains on the floor. Only a few at first, but they quickly grew in size, until the stains marred the lit stone in great rivulets, flooding the tunnel floor with the color of rust—
—and the air with the unmistakable stink of dried blood.
**********
You found the missing Cryptkeepers not long after that.
Well, what was left of them.
Whatever preserved the corpses in the vaults had done its work here, too. The bodies of the guildmembers you'd been sent down to find looked as if they'd been killed the moment before.
Which meant that with every breath, the horrific miasma of death filtered through your nose and mouth: the sharp stink of voided bowels mixed with the iron tang of fresh blood and the cloying, sweet smell of human flesh.
They looked even worse than they smelled.
The Cryptkeepers had gone into the lower tunnels prepared, or so they had likely thought. Glimmers of steel maille links still clung to the shredded remnants of their clothes. One savaged hand still clutched the splintered remnants of a shield, even as it lay a full two paces away from the nearest arm.
Clearly, their preparations had not helped them.
Sam looked away, his face ashen even under the ruddy glow of the torches. Adanna's teeth gritted as she leaned against the wall, her eyes wide.
Then the smell of fresh death was joined by the dusty stink of a far older mortality. The air filled with the rasping of dry parchment…
…and you found yourself face-to-face with the answer.
**********
It had been human once, that much was obvious. It had two arms, two legs, a head, and a face.
Two arms, each one a disjointed horror of twisted bone shrouded in ragged scraps of long-dead skin. Its elbows were shrouded in dusty strands of decaying sinew, its skeletal hands clawed with long slender blades of yellowed nail.
Two legs, gnarled struts protruding from the reeking, distended ruin of a torso. One moment, it seemed on the verge of collapse, then the next it skittered forward with an impossible speed, its gnarled and decayed feet scraping tortured shrieks against the stone.
A head: long-dead flesh stretched over a misshapen and tortured skull.
A face: cold blue light shining out of empty sockets, tattered skin hanging in flaps over a death rictus of yellowed, cracked, and jagged teeth.
It had been human, [i]once[/i].
It wasn't anymore.
**********
You felt your hands tremble as the skeletal monstrosity advanced. Your every muscle and sinew cringed as its yellowed appendages skritched across the stone, as the horrific, impossible thing shambled toward you with terrifying agility.
The icy tentacles of fear crawled up your spine as cold sweat dripped down your back. Dangerous animals you had faced, criminals you had faced, but you had no idea how you could face this.
"We need to get back to the others!" you heard someone shout. Adanna? You weren't sure.
No, it had to have been, for it was Sam who spoke next: "Come on, Nameless! Get out of there!"
You tried to move as your companions retreated, but your legs only half answered. The Creature turned toward you, the baleful blue light from its face fading away to reveal the empty, rotted husks of dead eyes behind it.
Then it sprang at you, its arm coming out of the darkness like the barbed hooks of a whip, five cracked and twisted nails ripping through the damp, fear-soaked air…
**********
It's a miracle you're still alive.
It's a miracle that you managed to get away, that you hadn't gotten lost in the twisted passages of the lower catacombs. A miracle that you made it all the way back to that heavy iron-bound door in more or less one piece.
But you have no time to waste thinking about how you got here. Now, you need to figure out how you're going to get out.
You and your companions face not one but four of the horrific things, and it seems that your luck has finally run out. None of the other adventurers are anywhere to be seen, and the door presses cold and unyielding against your back.
"Great," Adanna snarls, her teeth gritting in frustration at a world that doesn't seem to have much fairness left in it. "What do we do now?"

1: "Break the door down. We need to fall back into the vaults."
2: "What can we do but stand and fight?"

title: The Cryptkeepers of Hallowford
obs:
You rush into the melee, staff in hand, trying your best to drive the attacking Creatures back.
Every time, your staff strikes home, but it is you who staggers back, your arms numb from the shock of impact.
And it is your foe who rushes forward, claw flashing in the pale light.
The blow comes too quick to be dodged, too powerful to be parried. It tears deep into your side, rending cloth and flesh as if they're nothing. An explosion of raw agony shoots through your body.
You stagger back, barely on your feet, your vision blurred and your teeth clenched tight from the pain, your hands barely able to keep hold of your weapon.
You won't be able to take another hit like that.
**********
The undying surge forward against the last remnants of the forces of the living.
Only a handful are still on their feet and fighting.
Lucan and the last holdouts of his Cryptkeepers are on the verge of destruction. But with magic and steel, they cling to a tiny patch of bloodied stone, even as their knot of defenders grows smaller and smaller.
Sir Michael and his last few watch members are no better off. They fall back the last few steps until their backs are pressed against the harsh light of the Heart itself.
With every passing second, the dead advance. With every moment, despair grows in the eyes of the living. This can't go on for much longer.

title: The Cryptkeepers of Hallowford
obs:
Perhaps now is the chance you've been waiting for.
With your erstwhile "allies" fighting for their lives against the undying tide, there's nobody stopping you from simply running in and taking the Heart. If you move quickly and quietly, you might not even get noticed at all until you are well out of harm's way.
Should be easy, right?
**********
Maybe not as easy as you think.
You only manage to take a few steps toward the Heart before one of its protectors spots you.
They're not exactly waving a weapon in your face yet, but if you make any attempt to steal the Heart while they're still watching, that will surely change in a hurry.
So you retreat to the edge of the central platform, to wait for a better opportunity. Maybe when the Heart is less well-guarded—or at least when the would-be guards are far more distracted—you'll have a better chance.
**********
The undying surge forward against the last remnants of the forces of the living.
The last survivors of the two expeditions are on the verge of annihilation.
Lucan stands almost alone. Only two or three of his allies are still fit to fight. The rest lie broken upon the ancient floor or cower in the light of the Heart, in the morbid hope that they will be torn apart last.
Sir Michael and his watch are no better off. Their backs are to the Heart as well. With no place to retreat, the resolve in the handful of survivors at last begins to disintegrate into panic.
Watch, Cryptkeeper, adventurer…the distinctions have ceased to matter. If you don't do something soon, you will all be among the dead.

title: The Cryptkeepers of Hallowford
obs:
You fall back, behind your allies as the Creatures begin to boil out of the breached doorway.
You hear the snap of miniature thunder, and the air fills with the stench of ozone behind you. The wards you and the other defenders placed go off.
You hear the sound of skittering, ragged claws on cobblestones as the swarm of monstrosities begins its terrible, silent charge.
Your eyes pick out the shape of the house in front of you. The half-timbered wall might prove a bit difficult to climb, but you spot the shape of a covered walkway to its side. Moving quickly, you hoist yourself up onto the shingled slope of the walkway's covering, then scramble up farther until you are on the roof of the house.
Now you can see the entire situation spread out in front of you. The Creatures are pouring out of all three exits, but your allies seem to be standing their ground, for now.
That doesn't mean they'll be able to hold out forever. The Creatures may seem small and distant from your lofty perch, but they attack with the same mindless ferocity you've come to expect from them.
Your allies need your help. What will you do?

title: The Cryptkeepers of Hallowford
obs:
There's going to be no convincing Lucan to back down—one look into his eyes will tell you that. If there was a time that a reasoned argument was going to get the Master of the Cryptkeepers to do the right thing, that moment is long past.
You'll have to do this the hard way.
**********
But not yet.
No matter how hard you try, you can't get close to Lucan without being spotted and stopped. Not yet anyway.
You'll have to wait for a better opportunity. When the Cryptkeepers are pressed harder by the Creatures, when they're too busy fighting for their lives to even notice you, let alone interfere with you—that will be the time to make your move.
Until then, you'll just have to watch and wait.
**********
The Creatures do not relent. There is no driving them back. With every moment, more of the horrors claw their way up onto the platform.
The defense is coming apart. The Creatures surge deep into the mass of humanity, leaving a trail of broken bodies and rent limbs in their wake. Driving them back is futile. Your allies can only retreat and fight on.
Lucan and his Cryptkeepers fight hard, but their numbers are dwindling by the moment.
The watch holds firm, for now. But with each fresh attack, fewer of
Sir Michael's
followers remain standing.
Yet the Creatures keep coming. No matter how hard they are struck or shot or burned, they get back up again. It is only a matter of time before the living are swarmed under by the dead.

title: An Odyssey: Echoes of War
obs:
You ready yourself, and then you notice Demodocus preparing to follow you.
"Where do you think you're going?" you ask him.
This stops the poet in his tracks. "With you?" he says uncertainly.
"No," you reply. "I'm going alone."
You squeeze his shoulder. "I'll tell you all about it when I get back," you say.
"Promise?" he asks.
"I promise," you reply.
*****Enter*****
When you step through the threshold, the world shimmers around you and you realize you are not in a cave at all. Instead, you are in a new place altogether.
The first thing you notice is the sweet, bright light. Everything around you is tinted gold. The sun is shining low, near the end of its daily journey. But it's not just that. Everything around you is golden. The grass under your feet, the flowering shrubs, the gates to the orchard that stands before you.
This, then, is the Garden of Hespera, Hera's orchard, where it is always sunset.
Behind the gates, you can see a single apple tree, its branches bent with golden apples. A fruit from that tree that became the Apple of Discord, which in turn led to the Trojan War.
And behind the tree, you can see two enormous columns–but no, not columns at all, but legs, the legs of a Titan, so tall as to rival the mountain behind him. You look up, and you can hardly make out his torso, his arms, his neck straining under the weight of the sky. Atlas.
The gate squeaks open and three women appear in front of it. They are dressed in ocher, orange, and yellow robes threaded with gold. The Hesperides, daughters of Atlas, nieces of Nyx.
"A visitor," one of them says. "How wonderful. We were getting terribly bored."
"Don't be silly, Aegle," another replies. "She just wants the apples."
Aegle frowns. "You don't know that," she says. "Maybe this one's different."
The second woman turns to you, sizes you up. "Are you different?"
The third Hesperis takes a step forward. There is something menacing in her face now, something serpent-like. "Tell us what you want," she orders. "Do you want the apples?"

title: Psy High
obs:
And why should you? You've never liked her, and you've got bigger things to worry about right now. You sneak on past, leaving Mackenzie to her tears.
You know you can't do this alone, and that's why you've spent so much time gathering up your friends and allies.
Now it's time to call on all those friends to make certain Mr. Pierce and Ms. Clay never get to the Nexus.
As the clock ticks towards midnight, the boat chugs towards the Nexus. From above, you can hear muffled laughter and music—the prom is still going strong. But those happy sounds feel very far away and very out of place compared to what’s happening here.
You’ve found the room on the lowest deck that will look directly out onto the Nexus. Through its single porthole, you can see a faint glow—most people would mistake it for moonlight, but even this far away you can sense the pulse of magic that tells you the Nexus itself is glowing.
You and your friends crowd around the door, blocking the way. When Mr. Pierce, Ms. Clay, and the Gold Crown Team come striding down the hallway, you're ready.
Haley gives you an uncertain look, then draws up straighter and calls, "All right, everyone! Let's go!"
The trouble is, the "everyone" Haley's talking to doesn't include that many people. They do their best—some a little frightened at the thought of facing down the principal, some defiant and resolute—but there just aren't enough people to keep Mr. Pierce away from the Nexus.
You worked hard, and you tried hard, and you counted on your friends, and your friends are helping you.
But it still isn't enough.
"I might have known that it would be you, user_input," snaps Mr. Pierce. "You're a bad seed, and you always have been. You and your little friends—you are nothing but a mob of children. Your priorities are entirely misplaced.
You are unruly and undisciplined.
You are disrespectful to your elders.
You have been given great supernatural power—yes, I know about that," he adds with a thin, superior smirk. "But you do nothing worthwhile with it. None of you children deserve to have the powers that you do. Those powers make you unpredictable. Unruly. It is absolutely evident that you need a grownup to keep you in line. I should have gotten rid of your bad influence on Kingsport High long ago."
