title: Psy High
obs:
"Wait!" you say. "Actually, I wanted your help with something."
"Okay." Mackenzie's still looking at you suspiciously, but she's not shouting, and she seems to be at least a little distracted from her misery.
"I've got a big plan I need people to help with," you tell her. "Your role is really, really important." That seems to brighten Mackenzie a little, so you repeat, "[i]Really[/i] important."
Mackenzie nods. "Okay…"
"Haley will explain exactly what you need to do."
"Okay," Mackenzie says slowly. "I'll find her." She looks much calmer now—more focused on the plan than on her own unhappiness. Whew.
"Thanks," you say, and head off to take care of your part of the plan.
You know you can't do this alone, and that's why you've spent so much time gathering up your friends and allies.
Now it's time to call on all those friends to make certain Mr. Pierce and Ms. Clay never get to the Nexus.
As the clock ticks towards midnight, the boat chugs towards the Nexus. From above, you can hear muffled laughter and music—the prom is still going strong. But those happy sounds feel very far away and very out of place compared to what’s happening here.
You’ve found the room on the lowest deck that will look directly out onto the Nexus. Through its single porthole, you can see a faint glow—most people would mistake it for moonlight, but even this far away you can sense the pulse of magic that tells you the Nexus itself is glowing.
You and your friends crowd around the door, blocking the way. When Mr. Pierce, Ms. Clay, and the Gold Crown Team come striding down the hallway, you're ready.
Haley gives you an uncertain look, then draws up straighter and calls, "All right, everyone! Let's go!"
The trouble is, the "everyone" Haley's talking to doesn't include that many people. They do their best—some a little frightened at the thought of facing down the principal, some defiant and resolute—but there just aren't enough people to keep Mr. Pierce away from the Nexus.
You worked hard, and you tried hard, and you counted on your friends, and your friends are helping you.
But it still isn't enough.
"I might have known that it would be you, user_input," snaps Mr. Pierce. "You're a bad seed, and you always have been. You and your little friends—you are nothing but a mob of children. Your priorities are entirely misplaced.
You think you are being kind when you take care of other people, but you are really just soft.
You are disrespectful to your elders.
You have been given great supernatural power—yes, I know about that," he adds with a thin, superior smirk. "But you do nothing worthwhile with it. None of you children deserve to have the powers that you do. Those powers make you unpredictable. Unruly. It is absolutely evident that you need a grownup to keep you in line. I should have gotten rid of your bad influence on Kingsport High long ago."

title: The Cryptkeepers of Hallowford
obs:
It's not hard to gather people willing to help you lay down some makeshift barriers.
Your fellow adventurers seem eager to pitch in.
It isn't particularly difficult finding material either: carts, tables, railings. The Cryptkeepers will probably have to reimburse their owners eventually, but for now, they'll do more than a good enough job of slowing the Creatures down.
The main problem is actually getting them into place. You barely have enough people with you to shift more than one piece at a time, and moving heavy wood and iron objects makes for tiring work.
By the time you get the first barricade up, a lot of your helpers are panting and sweating hard.
By the time you're halfway through the second, you're all on the verge of exhaustion.
Yet before long, you find yourself joined by more of your allies, with Selim Chain-Breaker at their head. The Khazari soon springs into action, hauling in oxcarts and heavy counters as if they were toys.
"I could not let you labor alone," he exclaims as he handles a length of heavy wooden rail like a stick of firewood.
Before too long, the other two barricades are finished, just as tall and stout as the first.
You're still thinking of what to do next when a shout of alarm calls you to the front doors.
**********
You arrive to find the walls of the guildhouse shedding puffs of whitewash, the wall behind it trembling. The defenders hold steady in their line, weapons at the ready.
The Cryptkeepers still carry only their improvised and scavenged weapons. They shake even as the walls shake, but they stand firm despite the horror that they are about to face. They know what is at stake, both for themselves and their guild. When you look into their eyes, you see the steady determination of those ready to fight and die for an organization that has been their entire life.
Your fellow adventurers are almost relaxed by comparison. They, too, have faced the Creatures, but unlike the others, each one of your colleagues is battle-hardened and experienced, well used to facing down impossible monstrosities and coming out on top. They wait with their weapons and spells at the ready, almost eager for battle.
The members of the town watch stand ready as well.
Your warning and your fighting retreat bought some time for them to muster, but perhaps not enough. Only a fraction of the watch seems to have reached you in time. Sir Michael leads a small group of them beside you, with his sword in one hand and a shield emblazoned with the crest of the Duke of Torinhall in the other. His volunteers carry their spears and halberds unsteadily behind him. For all of their padded aketons and steel kettle helms, these are still ordinary townsfolk, thrust from their normal lives into a dire situation they may not survive. They have every right to be afraid.
More of them wait before the other exits, each led by one of Sir Michael's senior watch members.
Your allies are in position, and they are as ready as they'll ever be for what is to come.
The question is, where will you be?

1: I'll support my allies from the rear.

title: An Odyssey: Echoes of War
obs:
"Ow!" you exclaim, making sure your facial expression matches your dismay.
Circe laughs. "Sorry, captain," she says. She pushes the substance deep into your wound, hurting you even more. It's unclear how necessary this is.
"Take your time, why don't you," you say.
She laughs again, like you're suddenly the funniest person on the ship. "Almost done," she says. She covers your wound with some linen and stands up. "Make sure you keep this clean, yes?" she says and walks away.
**********
The ship sails calmly for two whole days. But on the third day, the sky darkens suddenly and a great roar rises from the depths.
"Poseidon," Circe whispers, and her voice catches in her throat.
A wave as tall as a giant rises before you, and in its heart you glimpse the mighty god, the Earth-Shaker, seizing his trident in his hand, stirring up the sea. He rides a chariot made of shells and corals, dragged by enormous mares. Their manes are made of foam, and their hind legs disappear into fish tails. You've seen the likeness of these beasts before, in pictures assembled by tiny pieces of colored glass adorning the floors of your palace, back in Ithaca. Hippocampi.
Poseidon strikes the edge of the wave with the tip of his trident, and your ship is covered with vapor. "User_input!" he roars. "How dare you
harm my son?"
This is the result of your pride. Your need to spread your name throughout the world brought this upon you and your crew.
But there is no time for any of that right now.
Poseidon raises his fist to the sky and calls up the winds. And the winds, like obedient servants, gather: the East Wind and the South Wind, full of heat, and the West Wind, the carrier of storms, and the heaven-born North Wind. They drive a vast wave before him and crash against your ship, splintering your deck.
Next to you, Demodocus's joints slacken and he sinks to his knees. "How black the sea, how black the clouds," he whimpers. "Now we are certainly doomed. Blessed and thrice blessed were those Achaeans who fell in Troy. I wish we'd been killed the day when the Trojans were pressing us so sorely on the battlefield around the dead body of Achilles, for then we should have had the burial we deserve and all of the Achaeans would have honored our names, and our bodies wouldn't be lost in the unsung depths of the cold sea."
Ajax grasps the back of Demodocus's neck with his giant arm and pulls him to his feet. It wouldn't be a surprise if he slapped the lad about the face a couple of times, but he refrains. "Pull yourself together, poet!" he shouts. "And if you so wish for death, I'll make sure you get your due, once we're out of this cursed storm!"
**********
Enormous waves keep crashing against the hull of your ship, and you all scramble to keep yourselves tethered to the deck, or you'll be lost for good, drowned, feast for whatever lurks underneath the surface of this sea.
You can no longer see Poseidon, but you can feel his wrath. It batters your ship, soaks your hair and skin with salt water, fills your lungs until you can no longer breathe.
And when you are certain that this is your final hour, that your ship will surely sink this time, the storm abates at once, as suddenly as it started.
You find yourself on calm waters again. The clouds disperse and the sun shines above, slowly drying your skin, your hair, your clothes. Your crew right themselves one by one, timidly, reluctantly, as if unable to believe you made it out alive.
Then, you see.
"Oh no," you hear Circe say. "No no no no no."
**********
At first, you mistake what you see around you for kelp floating just under the surface of the water. Pieces of a shipwreck, perhaps, or driftwood sculpted by the salt-laced craft of the sea.
But then your mind catches up to your eyes, and then you make out the sunken faces, the shriveled skin, the nibbled toes, the tangles of hair still attached to decaying scalps.
"Talk to me, Circe," you say to the sorceress, because she seems to know where you are, what it is that's going on.
"We're in the Sirens' land," she says. "Dreadful creatures–half women, half beasts. They call them the Binders, the Entanglers. These poor wretches were caught by their song. They say that the Sirens' song bestows perfect knowledge and intense pleasure. But this," she gestures at the pieces of humans floating all around you, as far as your eye can see, "this is the price you pay."
"How did they get to be this way?" Polyxena asks.
"They were regular women, once. Some goddess punished them for their poor choices…" She trails off. You both see Polyxena is about to launch into a long and impassioned discussion of what "regular women" are or do, and there is clearly no time for that. "I don't actually know the details," Circe hastens to add. "Only what my grandmother told me when I was growing up."
"Can't we just sail around them?" Ajax asks.
"No," says Circe. She points at a cluster of jagged rocks up ahead. "The currents here are such that any ship caught has to drift by their shores. If we try to go against them, we'll be crushed against those rocks."
Demodocus turns to you. "What are we going to do, User_input?" he asks. "We've already survived so much. Perhaps our fortune has finally run out."

title: The Cryptkeepers of Hallowford
obs:
There's going to be no convincing Lucan to back down—one look into his eyes will tell you that. If there was a time that a reasoned argument was going to get the Master of the Cryptkeepers to do the right thing, that moment is long past.
You'll have to do this the hard way.
**********
But not yet.
No matter how hard you try, you can't get close to Lucan without being spotted and stopped. Not yet anyway.
You'll have to wait for a better opportunity. When the Cryptkeepers are pressed harder by the Creatures, when they're too busy fighting for their lives to even notice you, let alone interfere with you—that will be the time to make your move.
Until then, you'll just have to watch and wait.
**********
The Creatures do not relent. There is no driving them back. With every moment, more of the horrors claw their way up onto the platform.
The defense is coming apart. The Creatures surge deep into the mass of humanity, leaving a trail of broken bodies and rent limbs in their wake. Driving them back is futile. Your allies can only retreat and fight on.
Lucan and his Cryptkeepers fight hard, but their numbers are dwindling by the moment.
The watch holds firm, for now. But with each fresh attack, fewer of
Sir Michael's
followers remain standing.
Yet the Creatures keep coming. No matter how hard they are struck or shot or burned, they get back up again. It is only a matter of time before the living are swarmed under by the dead.

title: The Hero Unmasked!
obs:

And that's exactly what you do. Quentin flies in to give you a hand, and with his help, you become so thoroughly versed in the Swashbuckler's exploits that you might easily have lived them yourself.
Sometimes you catch yourself wondering if you actually did.
A week before you're scheduled to begin work again, you take to the rooftops as the Swashbuckler. The next night, you pull Detective
Sherezad Khan
from the clutches of a violent street gang, and she is appropriately surprised by your appearance.
"Swashbuckler? But I thought—!"
You just grin, sweep a bow, and disappear back into the night.
It's what User_input_2 would have wanted, but what about your own personal life?

No one else has noticed this kid's freak-out….
**********
A howl so loud you can feel it in your bones erupts from the boy two tables away from you. The searing pain that burns after it, you realize, is not from the sound, but the magic flare that goes with it. Panic fills your chest, and it takes you a second to realize that it's not your own panic, but the boy's, resonating against your own familiar feeling of being out of control of your own power. You know this feeling of sheer terror at your own ability.
"Danny!" Esme shouts, and the boy keens, unable to respond—because his mouth is stretching, elongating, turning into a muzzle. His shoulders crunch in on themselves, and his hands, grabbing for the wood of the table, leave claw gouges as they shift. There is fur everywhere, and the wolf that was Danny—his eyes just above the top of the table—looks terrified and ready to sink into the most basic fight or flight instincts. Esme crouches under the table, looking at least as frightened as the wolf.

"Are you sure?" Tyler asks. "You need to start thinking about college now. It's not too early."
You shrug vaguely. "Yeah, I'm just busy," you say.
Tyler sighs in disappointment, but nods. "I understand. Well, I hope I'll see you there when the play is over." He flashes another smile that makes your heart skip a beat or two, then turns to go. "Later!"
**********
The morning passes in a haze of distraction. You try to answer some texts without letting the teachers see what you're doing, and you think you succeed.
Third period comes as a profound relief: English with Ms. Rivera.
"Did you see the posters?" Tara's saying to Casey as they walk into class ahead of you. "They announced the prom theme! A Night To Remember."
"Yeah, I saw!" Casey answers, with more than her usual excitement. "And it's going to be on a boat!"
The prom! It's exciting, but it's just one more thing you need to think about and plan for. Great.
Still, in English class, at least, you can feel secure. You know Ms. Rivera will lead a great discussion, and you'll spend forty-five minutes immersed in interesting thoughts about literature.
Except when you come into the room, you don't see any books out on people's desks, just pens and pencils.
Uh-oh. That means there's an exam today—an exam you totally forgot about. What are you going to do?
**********
Well, you could try to wing it. You might be able to remember enough about the book to improvise your way through a test. If you don't, though, you'll probably fail.
Or, you could try to get the answers from someone else, either by trying to read off their paper or by using magic. You can look at a paper clairvoyantly or try to read someone else's thoughts. If you get caught doing any of those things, though, Ms. Rivera will be seriously disappointed, and you'll get sent to detention. Going to detention means you'll miss rehearsal for the play and Jessica will be really mad at you.
Although…now that you think of it, you realize if you do get sent to detention, you'll be able to see Room 014 for yourself.
Wow.
That would be super risky. You might get influenced by the Vinculum! And even if you don't, Ms. Rivera will think you've cheated on an exam, and you'll be in serious trouble. But you'll be able to get direct evidence about what's going on in Room 014, and you might even be able to put in some magical threads directly.
So what will you do?

obs:
You rush into the melee, sword in hand, trying your best to drive the attacking Creatures back.
Yet every time your blade connects, it only seems to bounce off, as if it were striking steel instead of flesh. Your arms begin to grow numb with the shock of repeated impacts.
The Creatures flinch with each blow, but the next instant, they rush you again, their strength and speed redoubled, their claws flashing in the Heart's pale light.
The blow comes too quick to be dodged, too powerful to be parried. It tears deep into your side, rending cloth and flesh as if they're nothing. An explosion of raw agony shoots through your body.
You stagger back, barely on your feet, your vision blurred and your teeth clenched tight from the pain, your hands barely able to keep hold of your weapon.
You won't be able to take another hit like that.
**********
The undying surge forward against the last remnants of the forces of the living.
Only a handful are still on their feet and fighting.
Lucan and the last holdouts of his Cryptkeepers are on the verge of destruction. But with magic and steel, they cling to a tiny patch of bloodied stone, even as their knot of defenders grows smaller and smaller.
Sir Michael and his last few watch members are no better off. They fall back the last few steps until their backs are pressed against the harsh light of the Heart itself.
With every passing second, the dead advance. With every moment, despair grows in the eyes of the living. This can't go on for much longer.

title: An Odyssey: Echoes of War
obs:
"I think I'll take this one on my own," you say.
"Let me come with you," Demodocus protests. "How am I going to be able to sing about this, if I don't witness it with my own eyes?"
"Didn't I tell you all about the garden of the Hesperides?"
"Yes," he admits. "But you were not very good at it."
"Fine," you relent. "But just you." You turn to the others. "The rest of you should get some rest for now."
Demodocus and you
make your way to the entrance of the cave that will lead you to the land of the Stymphalian birds.
*****Enter*****
As soon as you step through the threshold, you find yourself on an island in the Euxine sea. You are at the top of a cliff. Behind you lies the vast sea with its winds and waves, and before you is a forest, thick and evergreen.
"Talk to me, Demodocus," you say. "What do you know of these birds?"
"Brought up by Ares, the god of war, they used to reside near the swamp in Stymphalia, from which they received their name. They have bronze beaks, with which they gorge themselves on the flesh of humans, and metallic feathers that they can launch at their pursuers like spears." Demodocus smooths back his hair, clearly disturbed by his own recounting of the story. "They terrorized the people of Stymphalia, killing livestock and villagers alike, until Hercules killed half of them and drove the rest away."
"And now, here they are, and it is our turn to face them," you say.
And indeed, there they are, rising from the canopy, their beaks reflecting the light of the sun, their metal wings clanging as they stab the air. And there, where wing connects with body, a crescent of soft, unarmored flesh.
"According to some versions of the story," Demodocus adds, "they are not birds at all, but women, the daughters of Stymphalus and Ornis, punished for being inhospitable to Hercules." He shrugs, motioning towards the metal beasts. "But, obviously, this is not the case."
They screech as they rise, their voices like the clanging of swords in battle.
You can see five birds in total.
"This is it, Demodocus," you say. "Let's see what we are worth."

title: Diabolical
obs:
You bring the butt of the gun down on the old woman's frail skull. She whimpers a bit and collapses to the ground. You bark out orders to one of her minions to get her tied up and dropped off at the police station. The large man bristles at the command.
"Who the hell are you?" he asks, stepping toward you, though still wary of the gun. You stare into his eyes and see the fear hiding beneath the bravado.
"I'm the person who just put you out of a job. And the person who can put you and your boys back into one, a hundred times more profitable than the ones you scored with this old bat. All you have to do is follow my orders, get her out of my damn house, and get rich. What do you say?"
Later, you're not entirely sure what made him back down. Maybe he heard the sense in your words. Maybe you got lucky. And maybe he saw something in your eyes, something that told him that there's only one way for this to end.
He's the first of your minions. He won't be the last.
You get contact information from your new soldiers, then send them on their way with a promise of new work soon. You take half an hour to roam the trashed mansion, wondering what your parents will think when they see it.
You spend a few hours toying with the Darkspace camera, using its built-in firmware to log in to the dark website. Unsurprisingly, your takedown of a lightweight like Professor Murder has grabbed little attention. Fair enough. It might actually work to your advantage. You don't need everyone seeing your face, after all.
You get a welcome message from Obsidian_Heartbreak, the site's administrator. He sends you a link that allows you to reset Murder's account information.
Among other things, it asks you for a login name. By tradition, he explains, it's the name you'll always use as a member of the supervillain community. Not something to take lightly.
The first name that springs to mind is The Most Villainous of All Villains, but that's a little wordy. Perhaps Evil of Evils? Or maybe something subtle like MEG, which only another evil genius would recognize as an acronym for Most Evil Genius. Or you could just use something easy for your inferiors to grasp, like Great One.
Then there are the dramatic names: Technomancer, Battle Master, The Specter…the possibilities are endless!
After stressing over it enough to give yourself a headache, you finally think of the perfect name. It expresses everything you hope to do, and be, in this new, exciting life. You type it into the form:
**********
(Are you sure you want to be user_input? Remember, this will be your name for the rest of your villainous career!)

obs:
You kneel again next to the weeping man and touch his shoulder. "Don't punish yourself, Eurylochus," you say. "It is only human to make mistakes."
"User_input…" he mutters, but his sobs won't let him speak. He wraps his arms around your neck and clings to you like a drowning man.
You pat him on the back until his weeping eases.
There is nothing to do right now but to wait and see where the winds take you.
**********
Many hours later, you find yourself on calm waters again. There is a stillness in the air, and the sun is shining above.
Then, you see.
"Oh no," you hear Circe say. "No no no no no."
**********
At first, you mistake what you see around you for kelp floating just under the surface of the water. Pieces of a shipwreck, perhaps, or driftwood sculpted by the salt-laced craft of the sea.
But then your mind catches up to your eyes, and then you make out the sunken faces, the shriveled skin, the nibbled toes, the tangles of hair still attached to decaying scalps.
"Talk to me, Circe," you say to the sorceress, because she seems to know where you are, what it is that's going on.
"We're in the Sirens' land," she says. "Dreadful creatures–half women, half beasts. They call them the Binders, the Entanglers. These poor wretches were caught by their song. They say that the Sirens' song bestows perfect knowledge and intense pleasure. But this," she gestures at the pieces of humans floating all around you, as far as your eye can see, "this is the price you pay."
"How did they get to be this way?" Polyxena asks.
"They were regular women, once. Some goddess punished them for their poor choices…" She trails off. You both see Polyxena is about to launch into a long and impassioned discussion of what "regular women" are or do, and there is clearly no time for that. "I don't actually know the details," Circe hastens to add. "Only what my grandmother told me when I was growing up."
"Can't we just sail around them?" Ajax asks.
"No," says Circe. She points at a cluster of jagged rocks up ahead. "The currents here are such that any ship caught has to drift by their shores. If we try to go against them, we'll be crushed against those rocks."

title: It's Killing Time
obs:
You decide that forcing Boris to live with what he has done is the best revenge, and you head to his place to implement your plan while he's out for the day.
It takes you hours to search for just the right lily, but you know from your source that Boris is expected to be out all day.  You find yourself in the central square with peddlers hawking their wares, gypsies offering to tell fortunes, and merchants with carts of roasted pork, fall-off-the-bone roasted beef, and roasted chicken on the spit.  None of these draw your attention, though.  You're looking for something else entirely.
You stand in the shadow of the astronomical clock, one of the landmarks of Prague, and the oldest of its kind in the world that's still operational.  Each hour, the four figures flanking the clock are set in motion, each representing something despised at the time of the clock's making.  Vanity is represented by a figure admiring himself in the mirror, greed is represented by a miser holding a bag of gold, pleasure and entertainment illustrated by an historically inaccurate figure of a Turk.  You realize, looking at the first three, just how much they represent Boris's greed and vanity, the duo mixing for his pleasure and entertainment.
Standing in the square, staring up at the clock, you realize that the fourth figure represents you in the most fitting way.  It is death, a skeleton that strikes the time upon the hour.  A broad smile spreads across your face and, almost on cue, you spy a florist on the far side of the square near the Gothic Tyn church, whose impressive spires rise above the old town center.
The woman who sells you the lily gives you a knowing look, and you smile at her, almost as if she has read the look on your face.  She is a stout and strong Eastern European,  and you surmise that she has probably sold many of these death flowers to people of your ilk: killers, assassins, vengeance seekers.  You nod to the woman and let her keep the change, keeping the single lily close to your chest.
**********
It's almost too easy for you to break into Boris's apartment and, for a minute, you fear there's a trap.  You automatically tense into a fighting stance, ready for an ambush.  Finally, after several moments elapse and no one steps forward, you realize that Boris has just gotten sloppy.
Looking around his apartment, and seeing relics from the former Syndicate, you become even more resolved in your decision.  Spying a picture of yourself, a small rosary hanging beside it, your knees almost buckle.  [i]Boris, how did you let it come to this…[/i]  It's not even a question.  It was destiny, and you're grateful that you decided against killing the man you'd once considered a father, no matter what he'd done.  His decision had been hard enough.
You walk toward his bed and place the lily down with a grave solemnity.  You scribble down a small note on a scrap piece of paper, writing:

1: "I forgive you my friend, but this is the end."
2: "I understand."
3: "I'll be watching you."
4: "Any day, any time, your life is mine."

title: The Hero Unmasked!
obs:
The handheld is light and easy to carry around.
The lightness is what makes it susceptible to wobble, and maybe that could be a problem.
But you know how to get the best out of this little baby, and if the picture is really clear and visible, a bit of wobble isn't going to matter.
You spend a minute or two getting the camera set up properly—no sense battling the crowd right now, only to have to do this later.
By the time you're ready to just push a button and start filming, Josh has the crowd mostly settled and filing out of the room in a relatively organized manner.
You slip in among the crowd and shuffle out with them.
Josh nearly freaks when he catches sight of you with one of his precious cameras; admittedly, it's kind of hard to miss.
You just smile and shrug at him, and let the flow of the crowd carry you out.
The evacuation carries you out into the parking lot, where Rhoda, Boris, and a bunch of your other colleagues are busy trying to account for each other.
Rhoda spots you and your camera, and hurries over.
"I can't believe you stopped to grab that," she says, sounding rather cross. "What were you thinking?"
**********
"I was thinking we should get some news footage."
Rhoda comes around to your way of thinking so fast she nearly gets whiplash. "Great idea!
Where's Josh? He's the expert with these handhelds."
"He's at the back of the crowd," you tell her, "making sure everyone gets out safely.
Don't worry. I think I can manage this camera just fine."
"All right, then. Let's get you someplace where you can get a clear view of the action."
Rhoda's gaze wanders over to the fire escape of a neighboring building.
"Think you can get to the top of that fire escape without breaking anything? That's the best view I can think of, but it could be difficult just getting there."
Boris frowns. "I think User_input should stay here on the ground," he says. "It's safer, and they won't be wasting any time getting into position."
"I suppose we can still get a decent shot of Firebrand from down here."
"I was actually thinking we should focus on the people down here. The firefighters and police and so on."
Rhoda glares at Boris, but before she can say anything, someone in the crowd points up to the roof of another building some distance off and shouts, "Look! It's the Swashbuckler!"

title: Psy High
obs:
"Wow, I'm sorry about you and Steve," you say vaguely. Half your mind is elsewhere, though, trying to overhear Mackenzie's thoughts.
Her mind is a miserable jumble. [i]This is horrible! I wish it had never happened. I'm so embarrassed! I want to talk to Casey, but I don't want anyone to know![/i] Of course! Casey's one of her best friends.
"I know I'm not the right person to be here right now," you say gently. "You probably want to talk to Casey, right?"

title: It's Killing Time
obs:
You don't so much as make a move for your pockets, telling the kid to scram.  Making one final attempt he says, "No crowns for Boris?"  A bit startled by the boy's name, you shake you head and he frowns then shakes his head, too, muttering something beneath his breath before walking farther down the street to talk to other people.
As he does, you look back and forth, furtively, trying to make sure you haven't been made.  After a few minutes, you're confident you haven't been, that it was just a coincidence.
Turning back to your thoughts, still a little shocked by the urchin's name, you review Boris's plan for the day.  He's going to be taking lunch in a cafe off the square, meeting with a business acquaintance.  Being in the square yourself, you look around and realize that it's unlikely you'll be able to make a sniper shot due to the close proximity of the buildings near the cafe.
You decide it's best to scope out the restaurant up close and, as you do, you see a network of alleyways leading to other areas of the city.  You figure Boris must want a clandestine meeting place because this part of the town is relatively secluded.  You realize it would be the perfect spot for a run-by shooting, the warren of alleys enabling you to disappear to another part of town after the deed was done.  Saving that as one option, you run down the list to see where else Boris will be going today.
After lunch, Boris is slated to meet with a gambling kingpin in an upscale, historical hotel.  You know that you'll be able to get in with no problem, but reason that guns are going to have to be out because, even with a silenced weapon, with the old Czech construction, you're likely to put a bullet into another room and bring the police running.
Finishing up the list, you realize there's another option if you wait until Boris has dinner.  He's scheduled to have his supper at a place called Golem Cafe.  The message says there's going to be a big event there tonight, so a direct attack of any kind isn't likely to be successful.  You figure that you can likely find a chef to bribe and try to poison Boris and his crew.
**********
Thinking of the options, a you can't help but circle back to the beggar boy and his name.  Boris.  The same name of the man who sold you out, his betrayal made so much worse since he had been like a father to you.
You know in your heart that you had been like a child to Boris, and you wonder if it would be even better revenge to sneak into Boris's home when he was gone, leaving a black lily on his pillow, the Russian symbol of death.  You contemplate the notion, knowing that Boris would not only forever be watching over his shoulder, wondering if you were going to strike, but he would also be confronted with the fact that you could have killed him and didn't.  You wonder if that's crueler, forcing Boris to live with his guilt for the rest of his days.
Contemplating it all, you also realize you have one other option.  You could let it go.  You recognize that you could forgive Boris for what he did and move on, even though it would be difficult.
In the end, you decide to:

1: Take care of things hand-to-hand at the hotel.
2: Opt for a sly poisoning at the Golem Cafe.
3: Sneak into Boris's apartment and leave the black lily.

title: Siege of Treboulain
obs:
The daughter's armor and sword lie sprawled across the family's porch. As you approach, the daughter gives you a weak smile. Just this morning, she was probably marching with the other soldiers in the parade. Now she lies in her father's arms, with a deep gash torn across her face. She'll live, but the wound is bound to hurt for weeks.
You raise your hand in benediction. "In the Cultivator's name, I bless your daughter. May her wounds be quick to heal. Her bravery on the wall today helped us all."
Tears of joy stream down the family's faces. "Thank you, Sovereign Ivy."
Priestess Saphira rests a warm hand on your shoulder.
"That was beautiful, Your Majesty," she says in a soft voice.
*****Back to the Citadel*****
The ground slopes steeply as you follow the Pearl Boulevard up toward Treboulain's Citadel. When you reach the top of the Citadel's steps, you can see the whole of Treboulain, with the streets delineated by the luminescent green of glowshrooms. Beyond the wall, there is darkness. In the far distance, a line of fire breaks that darkness, stretching across the spit of land that Treboulain occupies. It's the Skegg's camp.
The wind shifts, bringing with it the noise of foreign voices and clanking hammers. The Skegg are building. They have committed to destroying Treboulain. And only you can stop them.
*****Crisis Meeting*****
You convene in the throne room to discuss plans with Marshal Heartstone, Dimi Floros, Priestess Saphira, Lord Daen, and dozens of other important officers, nobles, and citizens.
An aide hands Heartstone a report. The marshal grunts in thanks, glowering at the map of Treboulain spread across the table before you. Knives weigh down the corners to stop the map curling up.
As the aide departs, she gives you a respectful bow. Your actions today have won a modicum of respect from most of Treboulain's army.
Heartstone skims the report. "Our infantry remains strong, and our archers have retained most of their soldiers."
"It's too bad that we have no arborturgic soldiers to complement our army." Dimi Floros casts a smirk toward Priestess Saphira. "Why, if only we'd had them today, maybe hundreds of lives would have been saved…."
Saphira sniffs. "Our arborturgists are not soldiers. They are priests."
"Everyone's a soldier during war," says Floros.
Saphira refused your earlier request to recruit arborturgists into the army. Perhaps she will feel different now?
Of course, there will be ways for the arborturgists to help without breaking their pacifist vows, so you may not want them to become fighters. They could help strengthen fortifications, assist with growing food, or take on any number of other tasks.

title: An Odyssey: Echoes of War
obs:
"Words?" she asks, inviting you to take a seat.
She joins you and crosses her arms against her chest, waiting for you to speak.
"I hear you've been having trouble with some horses," you start.
She sniffles. "And? What is it to you?"
"Maybe I can help."
"How could you help?" she asks. "Nobody can save us from Diomedes and his beasts."
"Can you tell me about the beasts?"
She stares at you for a few moments, trying to decide whether she can trust you. Then, she wipes her nose with the back of her hand and starts talking: "There are four of them. Podarge the swift, Lampre the shining, Xanthe the yellow, and Deine the terrible. But they are all terrible, if you ask me. They come out at night to feast on human flesh. They drag you out of your bed, steal babies from their parents' laps. When they cannot find humans to mangle, they attack the animals." She pauses, her cheeks now red with anger. "Did you see any cattle as you were coming into the village? Any chickens, any pigs? No! The horses have eaten most of them, and driven the rest away." She covers her eyes with her palms. "There is no living for us here, anymore."
"I'm sorry," you say.
She uncovers her eyes and stares at you, or through you, not really seeing you at all. "I can still hear the sound their jaws made as they devoured my brother," she says. "What his flesh sounded like when it was being torn from his body, what his bones sounded like as the horses crunched them between their jaws."
You ask her about Diomedes, the man who controls the mares, to distract her from the horrors she has endured.
"He used to be the King of Thrace. He's the son of Ares and a harsh, unfair, war-loving king. One day, his people revolted against him and removed him, exiled him. He left Thrace, taking with him nothing but his horses. He had raised them on human flesh since they were foals, and so they developed an appetite for it. It drove them mad. Now Diomedes has found this little corner of the world to rule and make himself feel powerful. Whenever we disobey or he fears we might want to drive him away, he looses the horses on the villagers to keep us under control."
"Haven't other heroes been here before me?" you ask. "Killed the mares, defeated Diomedes?"
She looks at you with a puzzled look on her face. "Other heroes?" She shakes her head. "I don't know what that means."
It's the sorcery that makes the caves work the way they do. As if the entire thing resets somehow after you're gone.
"I just have this feeling," she says. "This sense that I'm living and reliving the same nightmare over and over again." She raises her eyes to you, tears shimmering in their corners. "Is it never going to end? Can you really help us?"
"I can try," you say.
"But how?" she asks.

title: The Cryptkeepers of Hallowford
obs:
There's only one place in town where the news might spread fast enough to reach the entire population before things get ugly: the sanctuary.
The building isn't exactly difficult to find. It towers over the houses around it. More important, it's only a few blocks away from the Cryptkeepers guildhouse.
You suppose Lucan would have tried to stop you from warning the town. Even in a crisis like this, he would have wanted to keep the whole thing secret.
But Lucan isn't here to stop you.
**********
You find Justice Hortensia in between audiences, her gavel still in her hand as she sits judgment over the sanctuary's polished stone dais.
Your warning is quick and to the point. The silver-haired Justice's expression settles into a look of grim resolution.
"All right. Our first priority is getting the townsfolk off the streets," she says. She turns to her attendants. "Get the word out. Remind them the sanctuary has stone walls and a stout door. It'll be safer than most houses. If any folk live close to the gates, it might be better for them to get out of town altogether."
One by one, she sends off her junior clerics to warn each district of town. Only when the last leaves does she turn to you.
"You could have warned us sooner," she says with only the barest hint of sourness in her voice. "Knowing that there were monsters under our feet before they actually attacked would have been nice."
"Lucan wanted to keep it a secret," you reply. "He thought he'd be able to handle the situation without it spilling over into town."
"Yes, that certainly went well, didn't it?" The Justice scowls. "Next time something like this happens—if there is a next time, that is—I'll expect you to put the lives of this town's inhabitants over what Lucan of the Cryptkeepers thinks is best for his bottom line."
With that brief scolding, you are sent off back to the guildhouse. By the time you get back, you can already see men and women in Watchers' robes, knocking on doors and shouting warnings from street corners. The townsfolk should be able to get to relative safety in time.
You're still thinking of what to do next when a shout of alarm calls you to the front doors.
**********
You arrive to find the walls of the guildhouse shedding puffs of whitewash, the wall behind it trembling. The defenders hold steady in their line, weapons at the ready.
The Cryptkeepers still carry only their improvised and scavenged weapons. They shake even as the walls shake, but they stand firm despite the horror that they are about to face. They know what is at stake, both for themselves and their guild. When you look into their eyes, you see the steady determination of those ready to fight and die for an organization that has been their entire life.
Your fellow adventurers are almost relaxed by comparison. They, too, have faced the Creatures, but unlike the others, each one of your colleagues is battle-hardened and experienced, well used to facing down impossible monstrosities and coming out on top. They wait with their weapons and spells at the ready, almost eager for battle.
Your allies are in position, and they are as ready as they'll ever be for what is to come.
The question is, where will you be?

title: An Odyssey: Echoes of War
obs:
"This one looks like it will take as many hands as possible," you say.
"We'll all come," Polyxena replies, looking sternly at everyone around her to preempt any disagreement. "No question about it."
On foot, you all pick up your weapons–Demodocus's is, of course, his lyre–and make your way to the entrance of the cave. Deep darkness lies ahead, and you cannot see nor hear anything beyond the cave's gaping maw.
*****Enter*****
As you step through the threshold, the smell of swamp assaults you. You are no longer in the land of the Heroes' Mist, that much is certain. Before you lies the lake of Lerna, from which the Hydra takes its name.
The smell is vile; it burns your nostrils. "Everyone, cover your noses," you say, and, turning to Demodocus, you ask: "What do you know of the Hydra?"
Demodocus, heartened by the attention, launches into a diatribe on the Lernaean Hydra's lore: How it was reared by Hera for the sole purpose of defeating Hercules with its poisonous blood and deadly teeth; how it terrorized the villages around Lake Lerna; how Hercules used both speed and strength to defeat it with the invaluable help of his friend.
"But if Hercules already slaughtered the beast, how is it still here for me to vanquish?" you ask.
"We are outside of normal time and space," Circe interjects. "This is a world of trials. It is a circle, ever-turning, eternal, and you are but a spoke briefly caught in it."
You approach the swampy waters of the lake. Above you, there is clear sky; around you, there are reeds and rocks and innumerable small insects. No sign of the cave that you entered to get here.
As you stand at the edge of the lake, everything seems quiet–serene, almost. And yet there is this sense of foreboding; the certainty that something dangerous lurks here.
You scour the still surface of the lake, green and thick with duckweed, and at first you can see nothing out of the ordinary.
*****Look More Closely*****
Then, you notice it.
In what you thought was a tangle of reeds and brambles, eyes.
Eyes, and teeth, and scales.
Looking straight at you, the head of the snake rises. It knows you've seen it now. It rises and rises until it stands high above you, as tall as two grown humans.
And beside it, eight more heads just like it. Nine slender necks sprouting from a mighty body still concealed beneath the grimy waters of the swamp.
This is it, hero. This is your time. Your moment of truth.

title: Diabolical
obs:
"Sorry, Arachnus, but I'm not here to make friends."
The sentence is barely out of your mouth when something wraps tightly around your neck with harsh steel fingers.
"I am," whispers Hackmaster as her exoskeleton's claws tighten on your throat.
"Dani, what the hell are you doing?" you manage to wheeze out. She screams and lifts you in front of the exoskeleton's face port. For the first time since you've known her, she opens the port, revealing her badly scarred face. You thought she was merely controlling the mech, but instead she's actually inside it, which make sense since her van can't travel through space.
"My. Name. Is. [i]Hackmaster[/i]!" she screeches, hurling you across the room. She turns her back on you and kneels before Doctor Arachnus.
"Master. Please. Teach me. I thought I knew what hatred was, but…but I look into your eyes and see the purity. Please."
You try to warn her, but there's no breath in your lungs. And so you have to watch as one of Doctor Arachnus's tentacles casually, almost gently, pulls Hackmaster from her armor. There is a snapping sound. You shouldn't feel bad about it. She was a traitor. You shouldn't.
Doctor Arachnus lets out a cackling laugh.
"Foolish mortal. Did you think my offer was genuine? Ara-kunos needs no assistance, has no equals. Only subjects, and slaves."
That's it, no one makes a fool out of you. Not even the world's deadliest supervillain.
**********
Here it is. Life or death. The ultimate fight. Choose wisely. The fate of the Earth depends on it.

title: Psy High
obs:
"Wow, I'm sorry about you and Steve," you say vaguely. Half your mind is elsewhere, though, trying to overhear Mackenzie's thoughts.
But it's no use—you're too distracted. And so is she.
Mackenzie's eyes narrow. "What are you getting at, user_input? You don't care about me and Steve. You don't care about anything."
Uh-oh. Apparently you didn't sound sincere enough.
"You just get away from me!" she shouts.
You do. But as you do, you hear other people hurrying in your direction, and someone shouts, "Is everything okay?"
Uh-oh. You'd better be far away from here when Mackenzie tells people she just saw you.
You know you can't do this alone, and that's why you've spent so much time gathering up your friends and allies.
Now it's time to call on all those friends to make certain Mr. Pierce and Ms. Clay never get to the Nexus.
As the clock ticks towards midnight, the boat chugs towards the Nexus. From above, you can hear muffled laughter and music—the prom is still going strong. But those happy sounds feel very far away and very out of place compared to what’s happening here.
You’ve found the room on the lowest deck that will look directly out onto the Nexus. Through its single porthole, you can see a faint glow—most people would mistake it for moonlight, but even this far away you can sense the pulse of magic that tells you the Nexus itself is glowing.
You and your friends crowd around the door, blocking the way. When Mr. Pierce, Ms. Clay, and the Gold Crown Team come striding down the hallway, you're ready.
Haley gives you an uncertain look, then draws up straighter and calls, "All right, everyone! Let's go!"
The trouble is, the "everyone" Haley's talking to doesn't include that many people. They do their best—some a little frightened at the thought of facing down the principal, some defiant and resolute—but there just aren't enough people to keep Mr. Pierce away from the Nexus.
You worked hard, and you tried hard, and you counted on your friends, and your friends are helping you.
But it still isn't enough.
"I might have known that it would be you, user_input," snaps Mr. Pierce. "You're a bad seed, and you always have been. You and your little friends—you are nothing but a mob of children. Your priorities are entirely misplaced.
You spend your time playing make-believe in the Drama Club, when you should be thinking about your future.
You are unruly and undisciplined.
You are disrespectful to your elders.
You have been given great supernatural power—yes, I know about that," he adds with a thin, superior smirk. "But you do nothing worthwhile with it. None of you children deserve to have the powers that you do. Those powers make you unpredictable. Unruly. It is absolutely evident that you need a grownup to keep you in line. I should have gotten rid of your bad influence on Kingsport High long ago."

title: The Cryptkeepers of Hallowford
obs:
"I'm only going to warn you once," you declare as you step forward. "So I suggest you listen, before you do something you regret."
That gets the watch's attention. If there's one thing that gets people listening to you, it's a good threat.
"Some of you may not know who I am," you continue, "but somehow, I doubt that, unless you've been living under a rock for the past year. But in case you have, let me introduce myself…"
You give your cloak a dramatic flick as you brandish your weapon before you. "I am Nameless of Kendrickstone. I faced down the Razorclaw of Sonnemerci. I have faced ancient magic beyond your comprehension. While you were hiding behind your walls, I broke the power of Milius Black-Clad and his army of cutthroats, each more vicious and dangerous than any of you could ever be."
It doesn't seem to work.
As impressive as your words sounded in your head, they wash over the members of the watch like water over stone. None of them even waver.
So much for that.
**********
"Enough!" Lucan snaps, his voice cutting the tense air. "There will be enough of this fruitless bickering! I, for one, demand that we waste no more time."
He points at Sir Michael
and the watch. "If you do not swear yourselves to secrecy right here and right now, then none of you will be leaving this chamber at all!"
Lucan's last words echo through the chamber, so loud that they almost seem to make the stone tremble beneath your feet.
Then the echoes stop, and you realize that the stone is trembling.
The others feel it, too. In but a moment, Lucan's ultimatum is forgotten as the shaking is joined by a dry, scraping rattle that grows louder and louder and louder.
Until the claws of the first Creatures crest the lip of the platform.
**********
Cries of shock and fear fill the chamber as the first of the Creatures clambers onto the platform. Cryptkeeper, watch, and adventurer alike turn outward, scrambling for the precious moments needed to mount a defense to this sudden threat.
The desiccated horrors are not waiting. They plunge into the confused mass with relentless speed. Shock and fear are drowned out by screams of agony as ragged claws and time-yellowed teeth rip into still-living flesh.
Your fellow adventurers are the first to get their bearings. They've faced unpleasant surprises before, and so have you. The unprepared watch and Cryptkeepers rally and, with frantic thrusts of spears and torches, begin to fight back.
**********
As the initial shock wears off, your allies and rivals both fight back with dogged ferocity. The line holds firm, and for a moment, it almost seems like you are pushing the Creatures back.
Lucan rallies his Cryptkeepers with remarkable efficiency. They form up around the Heart in a tight, steady formation, bristling with weapons.
Some of the watch buckle or reel, but most stand their ground, a hard core with
Sir Michael at their head, pushing back against the Creatures.
But this is the Heart of the Creatures' power, and they keep coming, impervious to steel and spellfire. One by one, the brave townsfolk of Hallowford fall, and unlike the Creatures, they do not get back up again.

title: Diabolical
obs:
Doctor Arachnus probably assumes you're afraid of him. It's a reasonable assumption to make. After everything he's done, most people would fear him. But this time, it's different.
He should be afraid of you.
You've spent enough time with him that you know his greatest fears. And your mastery of fear as a weapon has taught you that it doesn't matter if you understand why he fears those things or not. So you begin to talk. Calmly, quietly, proving you aren't afraid of him—because not being feared is an unusual occurrence for him and causes a subtle sort of dread.
You don't retreat as he advances toward you, but continue speaking about a world of peace and happiness. A world where the name "Doctor Arachnus" is a joke, where "Ara-kunos the Eighth" doesn't matter to anyone.
A world where his greatest threat—the threat he pretends he doesn't fear, yet launched all his insane plans to stop—is victorious.
Doctor Arachnus puts his hands over his ears and shakes his head. He isn't even trying to attack anymore. He just wants you to stop tormenting him with thoughts of such a future. But you aren't that merciful. You don't let up until he falls to the floor in a sobbing, gibbering heap.
Even then, you toss in a few more terrifying promises to be sure he isn't faking it.
With Doctor Arachnus finally taken care of and the power of the Spacetime Sphere in your grasp, there's only one question left to answer….
What kind of supervillain are you?

title: It's Killing Time
obs:
You lean down next to the boy and pull out two 10-crown notes.  You press them into his hands and he smiles, revealing missing teeth.  "Thank you," he says graciously.  He's about to walk off when a sudden whim strikes you.
"What's your name, kid?" you ask.
He looks up at you and smiles again, "Boris."
You nod, and he walks off down the cobblestone street.
As he does, you look back and forth, furtively, trying to make sure you haven't been made.  After a few minutes, you're confident you haven't been, that it was just a coincidence.
Turning back to your thoughts, still a little shocked by the urchin's name, you review Boris's plan for the day.  He's going to be taking lunch in a cafe off the square, meeting with a business acquaintance.  Being in the square yourself, you look around and realize that it's unlikely you'll be able to make a sniper shot due to the close proximity of the buildings near the cafe.
You decide it's best to scope out the restaurant up close and, as you do, you see a network of alleyways leading to other areas of the city.  You figure Boris must want a clandestine meeting place because this part of the town is relatively secluded.  You realize it would be the perfect spot for a run-by shooting, the warren of alleys enabling you to disappear to another part of town after the deed was done.  Saving that as one option, you run down the list to see where else Boris will be going today.
After lunch, Boris is slated to meet with a gambling kingpin in an upscale, historical hotel.  You know that you'll be able to get in with no problem, but reason that guns are going to have to be out because, even with a silenced weapon, with the old Czech construction, you're likely to put a bullet into another room and bring the police running.
Finishing up the list, you realize there's another option if you wait until Boris has dinner.  He's scheduled to have his supper at a place called Golem Cafe.  The message says there's going to be a big event there tonight, so a direct attack of any kind isn't likely to be successful.  You figure that you can likely find a chef to bribe and try to poison Boris and his crew.
**********
Thinking of the options, a you can't help but circle back to the beggar boy and his name.  Boris.  The same name of the man who sold you out, his betrayal made so much worse since he had been like a father to you.
You know in your heart that you had been like a child to Boris, and you wonder if it would be even better revenge to sneak into Boris's home when he was gone, leaving a black lily on his pillow, the Russian symbol of death.  You contemplate the notion, knowing that Boris would not only forever be watching over his shoulder, wondering if you were going to strike, but he would also be confronted with the fact that you could have killed him and didn't.  You wonder if that's crueler, forcing Boris to live with his guilt for the rest of his days.
Contemplating it all, you also realize you have one other option.  You could let it go.  You recognize that you could forgive Boris for what he did and move on, even though it would be difficult.
In the end, you decide to:

1: Take care of things hand-to-hand at the hotel.
2: Opt for a sly poisoning at the Golem Cafe.
3: Sneak into Boris's apartment and leave the black lily.

title: The Cryptkeepers of Hallowford
obs:
"About time!" Adanna exclaimed impatiently. "Let's go!"
So you led your companions onward, deeper into the tunnels.
You went deep below the surface then. How deep, you did not know. You were isolated from anything that might have told you, and you hadn't seen any signs of the other groups since you left Mundy and the others behind. Only the memory of the path back to the upper catacombs kept you and your companions from being entirely lost.
The tunnels around you didn't help there either. The air grew warmer and drier, in defiance of all common sense. The torches, too, began to burn brighter even as their sconces took on shapes and forms utterly unrecognisable to you: alien loops and twists of material too hard and shiny to be iron.
Yet despite the increasing impossibility of your surroundings, you continued to forge onward, picking a direction at random as you came to each branch. Your efforts yielded nothing but more and more lengths of featureless, torch-lit tunnel.
Before long, your companions began running out of patience.
"Face it, we're not going to find anything just wandering aimlessly like this," Adanna said even as she followed after you. "We should turn around, see if we can find that trail I'd picked out earlier."
"The magical aura would be a better bet," Sam replied. "It'd be easier to pick up, too."
"Anyway, we can all agree that this aimless wandering is pointless," the Korilandine woman concluded. "We've been doing this for who knows how long, and we've found nothing. Let's just stop and head back since we're obviously not going to find anything—"
Adanna was still talking when you suddenly threw your arm in front of her. You had to admit that it had been partly to stop your fellow adventurer's complaints.
But mostly it had been to stop her from falling down the immense hole cut into the floor before you.
**********
In hindsight, calling the thing you and your companions had almost walked into a "hole" was a massive understatement, no more so than calling a dragon "a pretty big lizard."
The vertical shaft you found yourself before was less drilled into the tunnel floor and more drilled through the ground your tunnel passed through. It was immense, far wider than the tunnel itself, certainly too wide for you to jump across. From what you could see, it continued above the tunnel, disappearing into the unlit gloom over your heads.
Below you, it bored deep into the earth. Dim layers of stone along its sides looked like the rings of a tree. The reason you could see these layers without the light of torch or lamp was without a doubt the strangest thing of all.
At the very bottom, hundreds, if not thousands, of paces below your feet, the stone blazed with the bright blue light of magic.
Then you heard it, you all did: the rasping whisper of dry parchment, and the sharp, scratching of bone on rock, rising from beneath your feet.
While you were looking down, something else had been looking up.
You and your companions backed away, baring your weapons as you prepared to face whatever Creature was making its way up the stone shaft. You felt your lungs heave and your heart pound in your ears as you stood,
staff in your hands}
hoping that you were ready for the thing that was climbing toward you.
You weren't.
**********
It had been human once, that much was obvious. It had two arms, two legs, a head, and a face.
Two arms, each one a disjointed horror of twisted bone shrouded in ragged scraps of long-dead skin. Its elbows were shrouded in dusty strands of decaying sinew, its skeletal hands clawed with long slender blades of yellowed nail.
Two legs, gnarled struts protruding from the reeking, distended ruin of a torso. One moment, it seemed on the verge of collapse, then the next it skittered forward with an impossible speed, its gnarled and decayed feet scraping tortured shrieks against the stone.
A head: long-dead flesh stretched over a misshapen and tortured skull.
A face: cold blue light shining out of empty sockets, tattered skin hanging in flaps over a death rictus of yellowed, cracked, and jagged teeth.
It had been human, [i]once[/i].
It wasn't anymore.
**********
You felt your hands tremble as the skeletal monstrosity advanced. Your every muscle and sinew cringed as its yellowed appendages skritched across the stone, as the horrific, impossible thing shambled toward you with terrifying agility.
The icy tentacles of fear crawled up your spine as cold sweat dripped down your back. Dangerous animals you had faced, criminals you had faced, but you had no idea how you could face this.
"We need to get back to the others!" you heard someone shout. Adanna? You weren't sure.
No, it had to have been, for it was Sam who spoke next: "Come on, Nameless! Get out of there!"
You tried to move as your companions retreated, but your legs only half answered. The Creature turned toward you, the baleful blue light from its face fading away to reveal the empty, rotted husks of dead eyes behind it.
Then it sprang at you, its arm coming out of the darkness like the barbed hooks of a whip, five cracked and twisted nails ripping through the damp, fear-soaked air…
**********
It's a miracle you're still alive.
It's a miracle that you managed to get away, that you hadn't gotten lost in the twisted passages of the lower catacombs. A miracle that you made it all the way back to that heavy iron-bound door in more or less one piece.
But you have no time to waste thinking about how you got here. Now, you need to figure out how you're going to get out.
You and your companions face not one but four of the horrific things, and it seems that your luck has finally run out. None of the other adventurers are anywhere to be seen, and the door presses cold and unyielding against your back.
"Great," Adanna snarls, her teeth gritting in frustration at a world that doesn't seem to have much fairness left in it. "What do we do now?"

title: Siege of Treboulain
obs:
crumples.
"Haven't you given them enough?"  asks in a croaked whisper.
Your throat tightens. "Leadership is simple. Find what your people need. Then make the sacrifice. Stavren said that, and I happen to agree."
 bows  head. When  looks back up, there's a firmness to how he clenches his jaw.
"I'll never forget you, Sovereign Ivy. And I'll never forget what you've done for this city.  You will always be my sovereign, to the end of my days. Goodbye, Sovereign Ivy."
 turns and trudges away from your cell. Sighing, you shut the door. It closes with an echoing click.
**********
Time passes. You keep staring at the wall. Hopefully  escaped without harm. They must have, if they crept in without anyone noticing.
The lock clicks. You turn as the door swings open.
A dozen Skegg soldiers stand outside. Without saying a word, they shove a bag over your head, then tug you from the cell and march you through winding corridors. Your trips and stumbles do nothing to slow their relentless striding. Whether you walk or get dragged along the ground, they don't seem to care.
Light bleeds through the bag. Fresh air chills your skin. They rip the bag off, and you gasp and squint at the blinding brightness. Noise slams into your ears. After the silence of your cell, the sound is deafening.
As your vision adjusts, a figure materializes before you. Emperor Markov, his blood-red armor polished to gleaming perfection. It's like he never fought in the siege at all. A huge axe rests on his shoulder.
You're standing on the Citadel's balcony, overlooking the Pearl Boulevard. Treboulain's citizens stand along the street, gazing up at you with weary, dirt-stained faces. Skegg soldiers line the steps and either side of the Boulevard, armed with spears. Against their might, Treboulain's citizens look tiny.
Smoke rises from the Temple of the Cultivator. With a start, you realize the massive 500-foot-tall redwood tree is missing from the skyline. The Skegg must have chopped it down.
You glimpse a face among the crowd. , draped in a plain cloak with the cowl pulled over their head. A wave of relief washes through you. 's still alive.
Heartstone isn't the only person you recognize. Floros and Celestino are in the crowd as well.
Markov stares at you. He's not wearing a helmet, but he might as well be, because you can read nothing from his expression.
"Sovereign Ivy," says Markov. "I respect you. I respect your relentless determination to save your city. And so I offer you one final choice: pledge your allegiance and live as my servant-sovereign, subject to my rule and my conditions, or accept a noble death."

title: The Cryptkeepers of Hallowford
obs:

You'll have to do this the hard way.
**********
But not yet.
No matter how hard you try, you can't get close to Lucan without being spotted and stopped. Not yet anyway.
You'll have to wait for a better opportunity. When the Cryptkeepers are pressed harder by the Creatures, when they're too busy fighting for their lives to even notice you, let alone interfere with you—that will be the time to make your move.
Until then, you'll just have to watch and wait.
**********
The Creatures do not relent. There is no driving them back. With every moment, more of the horrors claw their way up onto the platform.
The defense is coming apart. The Creatures surge deep into the mass of humanity, leaving a trail of broken bodies and rent limbs in their wake. Driving them back is futile. Your allies can only retreat and fight on.
Lucan and his Cryptkeepers fight hard, but their numbers are dwindling by the moment.
Sir Michael stands almost alone, most of his watch dead at his feet. Only a scant few are in any shape to fight on.
Yet the Creatures keep coming. No matter how hard they are struck or shot or burned, they get back up again. It is only a matter of time before the living are swarmed under by the dead.

title: An Odyssey: Echoes of War
obs:
"What do you think you're doing?" you scream at him. "Now is not the time for a nap. Pull yourself together! And run!"
Your shouting seems to do the trick, because Demodocus scrambles to get back up, raising a cloud of dust.
You run ahead, and he runs behind you as fast as he can.
**********
It is enough.
Finally, your lungs pushing against your ribs and your mouth as dry as parchment, you reach the sea and wade to your ship. You climb up and stand on the deck, dripping salt water and sweat.
As you are ready to cast off, Polyphemus watching from the shore, you can no longer contain your need to brag about how great a trickster you are. You duped Polyphemus, Poseidon's own son. Why shouldn't you take ownership of your glory?
"Polyphemus!" you shout, your chest puffing with pride. "My name is User_input. Remember who it was that made a fool of you!"
**********
The cyclopes' island recedes behind you. Your crew has finally started to calm down from all the excitement and exertion.
The ship sails calmly for two whole days. But on the third day, the sky darkens suddenly and a great roar rises from the depths.
"Poseidon," Circe whispers, and her voice catches in her throat.
A wave as tall as a giant rises before you, and in its heart you glimpse the mighty god, the Earth-Shaker, seizing his trident in his hand, stirring up the sea. He rides a chariot made of shells and corals, dragged by enormous mares. Their manes are made of foam, and their hind legs disappear into fish tails. You've seen the likeness of these beasts before, in pictures assembled by tiny pieces of colored glass adorning the floors of your palace, back in Ithaca. Hippocampi.
Poseidon strikes the edge of the wave with the tip of his trident, and your ship is covered with vapor. "User_input!" he roars. "How dare you
taunt my son?"
This is the result of your bragging. Your pride brought this upon you and your crew.
But there is no time for any of that right now.
Poseidon raises his fist to the sky and calls up the winds. And the winds, like obedient servants, gather: the East Wind and the South Wind, full of heat, and the West Wind, the carrier of storms, and the heaven-born North Wind. They drive a vast wave before him and crash against your ship, splintering your deck.
Next to you, Demodocus's joints slacken and he sinks to his knees. "How black the sea, how black the clouds," he whimpers. "Now we are certainly doomed. Blessed and thrice blessed were those Achaeans who fell in Troy. I wish we'd been killed the day when the Trojans were pressing us so sorely on the battlefield around the dead body of Achilles, for then we should have had the burial we deserve and all of the Achaeans would have honored our names, and our bodies wouldn't be lost in the unsung depths of the cold sea."
Ajax grasps the back of Demodocus's neck with his giant arm and pulls him to his feet. It wouldn't be a surprise if he slapped the lad about the face a couple of times, but he refrains. "Pull yourself together, poet!" he shouts. "And if you so wish for death, I'll make sure you get your due, once we're out of this cursed storm!"
**********
Enormous waves keep crashing against the hull of your ship, and you all scramble to keep yourselves tethered to the deck, or you'll be lost for good, drowned, feast for whatever lurks underneath the surface of this sea.
You can no longer see Poseidon, but you can feel his wrath. It batters your ship, soaks your hair and skin with salt water, fills your lungs until you can no longer breathe.
And when you are certain that this is your final hour, that your ship will surely sink this time, the storm abates at once, as suddenly as it started.
You find yourself on calm waters again. The clouds disperse and the sun shines above, slowly drying your skin, your hair, your clothes. Your crew right themselves one by one, timidly, reluctantly, as if unable to believe you made it out alive.
Then, you see.
"Oh no," you hear Circe say. "No no no no no."
**********
At first, you mistake what you see around you for kelp floating just under the surface of the water. Pieces of a shipwreck, perhaps, or driftwood sculpted by the salt-laced craft of the sea.
But then your mind catches up to your eyes, and then you make out the sunken faces, the shriveled skin, the nibbled toes, the tangles of hair still attached to decaying scalps.
"Talk to me, Circe," you say to the sorceress, because she seems to know where you are, what it is that's going on.
"We're in the Sirens' land," she says. "Dreadful creatures–half women, half beasts. They call them the Binders, the Entanglers. These poor wretches were caught by their song. They say that the Sirens' song bestows perfect knowledge and intense pleasure. But this," she gestures at the pieces of humans floating all around you, as far as your eye can see, "this is the price you pay."
"How did they get to be this way?" Polyxena asks.
"They were regular women, once. Some goddess punished them for their poor choices…" She trails off. You both see Polyxena is about to launch into a long and impassioned discussion of what "regular women" are or do, and there is clearly no time for that. "I don't actually know the details," Circe hastens to add. "Only what my grandmother told me when I was growing up."
"Can't we just sail around them?" Ajax asks.
"No," says Circe. She points at a cluster of jagged rocks up ahead. "The currents here are such that any ship caught has to drift by their shores. If we try to go against them, we'll be crushed against those rocks."
Demodocus turns to you. "What are we going to do, User_input?" he asks. "We've already survived so much. Perhaps our fortune has finally run out."

1: Plug everyone's ears and kill the Sirens to save future passing sailors. Riskier, but heroic.
2: Have everyone's ears plugged with beeswax and myself tied to the mast, hoping the rope will hold.
3: This whole heroic setup sounds suspicious to me. Sit down and have a real conversation with these women.

title: The Cryptkeepers of Hallowford
obs:
"So tell me, Cryptkeepers," you ask as you step forward. "How many of you have been in a fight before? Not a tavern brawl or a street fight, but a real fight, against steel and maille and spellcraft?"
The guildmembers murmur among themselves. Some of them defended Hallowford when the Creatures attacked it, but you doubt more than a few have anything resembling real combat experience.
"Now, Sir Michael," you continue, nudging your chin at the Watch Captain. "He's a fully trained knight. Generally speaking, he wouldn't still be alive unless he was really good at killing people. Cutting people open with swords, crushing their bones with maces, driving greatlances into hearts and throats and heads. That's the sort of killing knights do."
The murmurs grow louder. It seems like your words are taking hold.
"Of course, I've been in a few fights myself,"
you add. "I faced down the Razorclaw of Sonnemerci. I have faced ancient magic beyond your comprehension. While you were hiding behind your walls, I broke the power of Milius Black-Clad and his army of cutthroats, each more vicious and dangerous than any of you could ever be.
You don't want to fight me, not if you want to live."
**********
For a moment, it seems to work. A few of the Cryptkeepers waver. Some look to each other nervously, whispering under their breath.
But then Lucan steps forward, an arbalest in hand. "We are fighting for what we know to be right. For Hallowford's future. That makes us stronger than any empty bravado you can hurl at us!"
The Cryptkeepers stiffen. The fear that you had put into them burns away as the determination rekindles in their eyes.
Close but not enough.
**********
"Enough!" Lucan snaps, his voice cutting the tense air. "There will be enough of this fruitless bickering! I, for one, demand that we waste no more time."
He points at Sir Michael
and the watch. "If you do not swear yourselves to secrecy right here and right now, then none of you will be leaving this chamber at all!"
Lucan's last words echo through the chamber, so loud that they almost seem to make the stone tremble beneath your feet.
Then the echoes stop, and you realize that the stone is trembling.
The others feel it, too. In but a moment, Lucan's ultimatum is forgotten as the shaking is joined by a dry, scraping rattle that grows louder and louder and louder.
Until the claws of the first Creatures crest the lip of the platform.
**********
Cries of shock and fear fill the chamber as the first of the Creatures clambers onto the platform. Cryptkeeper, watch, and adventurer alike turn outward, scrambling for the precious moments needed to mount a defense to this sudden threat.
The desiccated horrors are not waiting. They plunge into the confused mass with relentless speed. Shock and fear are drowned out by screams of agony as ragged claws and time-yellowed teeth rip into still-living flesh.
Your fellow adventurers are the first to get their bearings. They've faced unpleasant surprises before, and so have you. The unprepared watch and Cryptkeepers rally and, with frantic thrusts of spears and torches, begin to fight back.
**********
As the initial shock wears off, your allies and rivals both fight back with dogged ferocity. The line holds firm, and for a moment, it almost seems like you are pushing the Creatures back.
Lucan rallies his Cryptkeepers with remarkable efficiency. They form up around the Heart in a tight, steady formation, bristling with weapons.
The watch assemble at Sir Michael's back. The old knight holds two of the Creatures away from the Heart with his sword and the splintered remnants of his shield. In moments, a tight wall of spears and grimly determined faces guard the Watch Captain's flanks.
But this is the Heart of the Creatures' power, and they keep coming, impervious to steel and spellfire. One by one, the brave townsfolk of Hallowford fall, and unlike the Creatures, they do not get back up again.

But to do that, you'll have to get close enough to him.

After your third or fourth attempt, it becomes obvious that you're not going to get through unless the watch are out of the picture…
Or distracted by a greater threat.
**********

The last survivors of the two expeditions are on the verge of annihilation.
Lucan stands almost alone. Only two or three of his allies are still fit to fight. The rest lie broken upon the ancient floor or cower in the light of the Heart, in the morbid hope that they will be torn apart last.
Sir Michael and his watch are no better off. Their backs are to the Heart as well. With no place to retreat, the resolve in the handful of survivors at last begins to disintegrate into panic.
Watch, Cryptkeeper, adventurer…the distinctions have ceased to matter. If you don't do something soon, you will all be among the dead.
