title: It's Killing Time
obs:
You quickly make arrangements with Hector for a pickup location on the other side.  It might not be the bravest thing to do, but you also don't want to shed any blood if you don't have to.  You reason that, from this distance, the soldiers at the barricade won't be able to see you bailing out.
Getting as low as you can, you deftly make the jump to the foliage lining the road.  After lying still for a few minutes, you realize that your gamble has paid off, and no one from the barricade saw your stealthy maneuver.  A sigh of relief escapes your lips as you see your driver make it safely through the roadblock.  You circle wide and, while the path is long, you don't encounter any hostile forces on the way.  Reaching the rendezvous point, you see Hector has a disapproving smirk on his face.  You climb in and explain your rationale but he really doesn't seem to understand it.
Forgetting the barricade incident, you turn your thoughts toward figuring out how to get out of the country.
**********
Sinking back in your seat, you're happy to have cleared the obstruction. From the look on Hector's face, you can tell he is as well.  You know that the majority of the search party will be focused on the compound, within the barricade perimeter.  That helps you breathe a little easier but just for a moment.
There are still miles of road to go to the airport, and word will definitely have spread about Cortez's death by the time you get there.  People on the general's payroll will be suspicious of visitors leaving, but it's better to leave during the chaos and slip out amid the confusion.  Once the general's troops get a firm grip on airport control, escaping under the guise of being a tourist won't be an option.  You just hope that hasn't happened yet.
Pushing that dilemma aside for the moment, hoping your fake papers will hold up when you get there, you concentrate on surveying the jungle for any sign of danger.
The sound of the radio crackling pulls you from your thoughts.  Glancing down, you spot the handset and pick it up, wanting to know what your controller wants.  You know it has to be him because he's the only one with this frequency, and you also know that if he's making an unscheduled call, it has to be something bad.
**********
"Hey," you say, pressing down the button on the handset.  "What's up?"
You take pains to hide the irritation in your voice, but Jones picks up on it.  "Not happy to hear your friendly neighborhood controller's voice?"
"It's not that. It's just that I know you're not calling me to tell me what a good job I did," you say flatly.  "If you're calling, then something's wrong."
Jones seems to sense your irritation because he says, "I'm going to get right to the point.  The man you decided to shoot in order to get the shot…well, it turns out the guy who hired us is none too happy about it."  You start to respond but Jones continues, "Don't worry, though, he paid in advance, so you'll get your money."
"That wasn't what I was going to say," you respond.  "Why isn't he happy?"
"Yeah, well, he commissioned the hit because the general had a stranglehold on the local townsfolk and was collecting protection money.  He wants to take over the general's position, and shooting the people he's going to collect from doesn't do him any favors."
"Would have been nice to know beforehand," you say, trying to keep the exasperation out of your voice.  After a second you add, "Well, it's not like I killed the guy."
"Yeah, well, he's still pretty pissed you planted a bullet in him.  It's not your fault," he says, "the intel was bad.  The client didn't let us know until after the fact."
"Why wouldn't he tell us?" you ask, astounded.
"Don't know," Jones admits.  "Maybe he didn't think you'd be trigger happy and kill a townie.  Whatever the reason is, the fact remains, he's enraged.  We've told him no refunds, but I wanted to give you a heads up in case he tries to do something stupid like tell the townsfolk what you did.  Take care now, user_input."
"Thanks," you say, clicking off the mic.
[i]He's going to get the townsfolk to come for me[/i], you think, and your mind is already fixating on ways to defend yourself.  You rationalize that there was no way you could have known.  You start to feel a little better, but then you see two jeeps speeding up behind you.
**********
The jeeps are racing to close the distance.  As they gain on you, you begin to see the occupants.  Each vehicle is overloaded, and you can tell from the ripped shirts and bandanas that they are not military.  That doesn't allay your concerns in the least, though, because they look ready to kill—and from the automatic machine guns in their hands, you know they have the capability.  Your stomach clenches as they get closer.
"Floor it," you tell Hector, but he shakes his head and looks at you with fear in his eyes.  The jeep is making sputtering sounds.
You curse silently to yourself as Hector tells you he thinks your ride is overheating.  In that instant, you realize that outrunning your pursuers is out of the question.  Knowing you have to act fast you:

title: The Cryptkeepers of Hallowford
obs:
You look to your allies and nod.
If you're going to get out of this alive, you're going to have to destroy the Heart. To do that, you'll have to get through Lucan, his Cryptkeepers, and anyone else standing in your way. So long as they're distracted, you might have a chance of getting through.
You take a breath and run toward the cage of alien metal that holds the Heart at the center of the chamber.
But you are not fast enough. Lucan's Cryptkeepers
and Sir Michael's watch
may be fighting for their lives, but they still manage to spot you before you get anywhere near close enough.
A cry of alarm goes up. Someone points an arbalest your way. You back off, moving away to the edge of the central platform.
There are still too many who would stop you from destroying the Heart. Maybe if you waited for a better opportunity, after the Creatures have worn them down more.
It's a morbid prospect, letting the undying kill and maim Hallowford's defenders so that you can get close enough to destroy the Heart, but if that's what it takes to get anyone out alive, then that's what must be done.
**********
The undying surge forward against the last remnants of the forces of the living.
Only a handful are still on their feet and fighting.
Lucan and the last holdouts of his Cryptkeepers are on the verge of destruction. But with magic and steel, they cling to a tiny patch of bloodied stone, even as their knot of defenders grows smaller and smaller.
Sir Michael and his last few watch members are no better off. They fall back the last few steps until their backs are pressed against the harsh light of the Heart itself.
With every passing second, the dead advance. With every moment, despair grows in the eyes of the living. This can't go on for much longer.

1: If I can get close unseen, I can destroy the Heart!

title: Blackstone Academy for the Magical Arts
obs:
Agent Cody handed you a brochure once upon a time, and on the back was a lay person's magic blunting spell. Even though the Liminals use magic as little as possible, they rely on some tricks to even the odds.
You start intoning the charm, knowing that your success depends on more than just your ability. Your mind flashes through choices you've made through the year, and you know that if they helped keep the balance, if what you've done kept the magical world hidden and behind the curtains, this little spell will have a greater impact.
The last syllable slips from your tongue like a hard candy falling out of your mouth, and you feel the magic fizzle. The lantern enclosure is clearer, more solid, and you can smell salt and hear waves. Maeve glares.
But she is not gone. "You think to rob me of my magic?" she demands.
Maeve steps toward you, and the ground—the lantern enclosure floor?—shakes beneath your feet. "I am no mere queen," she intones. "I am goddess of queens. My very name means intoxication, for those who look upon me are dazzled by my regal bearing. All bow before me in adoration."
The world flickers. Goddess of queens or not, her hold on the world isn't yet complete.
It means you still have a chance. But defeating her will require a great sacrifice.

title: Siege of Treboulain
obs:
Your back is straight, each step is measured, and there's a hard assuredness spread across your face. Soldiers salute as you pass. Your own guards stand straighter, and Dimi Floros nods approvingly.
"Stavren wrote that a person breaks only when they choose to be broken," the merchant says. "So you've done well to stay calm. Act as if something is certain, and the world will follow."
*****Back to the Citadel*****
The ground slopes steeply as you follow the Pearl Boulevard up toward Treboulain's Citadel. When you reach the top of the Citadel's steps, you can see the whole of Treboulain, with the streets delineated by the luminescent green of glowshrooms. Beyond the wall, there is darkness. In the far distance, a line of fire breaks that darkness, stretching across the spit of land that Treboulain occupies. It's the Skegg's camp.
The wind shifts, bringing with it the noise of foreign voices and clanking hammers. The Skegg are building. They have committed to destroying Treboulain. And only you can stop them.
*****Crisis Meeting*****
You convene in the throne room to discuss plans with Marshal Heartstone, Dimi Floros, Priestess Saphira, Lord Daen, and dozens of other important officers, nobles, and citizens.
An aide hands Heartstone a report. The marshal grunts in thanks, glowering at the map of Treboulain spread across the table before you. Knives weigh down the corners to stop the map curling up.
As the aide departs, she pointedly refuses to acknowledge you with even the slightest nod. For whatever reason, Treboulain's soldiers seem to lack respect for you at the moment.
Heartstone skims the report. "Our infantry remains strong, and our archers have retained most of their soldiers."
"It's too bad that we have no arborturgic soldiers to complement our army." Dimi Floros casts a smirk toward Priestess Saphira. "Why, if only we'd had them today, maybe hundreds of lives would have been saved…."
Saphira sniffs. "Our arborturgists are not soldiers. They are priests."
"Everyone's a soldier during war," says Floros.
Earlier, you didn't ask Saphira if her arborturgists would join your army. Perhaps you should reconsider now?
Of course, there will be ways for the arborturgists to help without breaking their pacifist vows, so you may not want them to become fighters. They could help strengthen fortifications, assist with growing food, or take on any number of other tasks.

obs:
User_input_2's face falls. "That's a shame, User_input. I really thought….
You seemed to take to the life so well. You've done some good things, User_input, and I don't think I could have done any better.
You're not letting the cops' attitude get to you, are you? That's just the way they are, you know that."
"I've been thinking about it all day, User_input_2.
Maybe I think too much, but that sort of excitement seems more than I like to deal with on a regular basis.
So I'm afraid that's it for me.
I honestly don't know how you can go on doing this. It's madness, and it's not for me.
"As you wish. If that's what you really want, I'm not going to press you."
User_input_2 wanders, almost idly, into the next room, and the door swings to behind them. You follow after, but…there's nobody there.
Opening the nearest window, you address the ledge above: "I'd be more impressed if I didn't know you were up there frantically making that quick change into the Swashbuckler outfit, User_input_2."
User_input_2, already masked, pokes their head over the ledge and grins down at you. "See? You know how it's all done already. Are you sure you won't reconsider?"
You just roll your eyes.
"Yes. Quite sure." Stepping back, you close the window on User_input_2.

title: Diabolical
obs:
"Sorry, Arachnus, but I'm not here to make friends."
The sentence is barely out of your mouth when something wraps tightly around your neck with harsh steel fingers.
"I am," whispers Hackmaster as her exoskeleton's claws tighten on your throat.
"Dani, what the hell are you doing?" you manage to wheeze out. She screams and lifts you in front of the exoskeleton's face port. For the first time since you've known her, she opens the port, revealing her badly scarred face. You thought she was merely controlling the mech, but instead she's actually inside it, which make sense since her van can't travel through space.
"My. Name. Is. [i]Hackmaster[/i]!" she screeches, hurling you across the room. She turns her back on you and kneels before Doctor Arachnus.
"Master. Please. Teach me. I thought I knew what hatred was, but…but I look into your eyes and see the purity. Please."
You try to warn her, but there's no breath in your lungs. And so you have to watch as one of Doctor Arachnus's tentacles casually, almost gently, pulls Hackmaster from her armor. There is a snapping sound. You shouldn't feel bad about it. She was a traitor. You shouldn't.
Doctor Arachnus lets out a cackling laugh.
"Foolish mortal. Did you think my offer was genuine? Ara-kunos needs no assistance, has no equals. Only subjects, and slaves."
That's it, no one makes a fool out of you. Not even the world's deadliest supervillain.
**********
Here it is. Life or death. The ultimate fight. Choose wisely. The fate of the Earth depends on it.

title: The Cryptkeepers of Hallowford
obs:
It's not hard to gather people willing to help you lay down some makeshift barriers.
Your fellow adventurers seem eager to pitch in.
It isn't particularly difficult finding material either: carts, tables, railings. The Cryptkeepers will probably have to reimburse their owners eventually, but for now, they'll do more than a good enough job of slowing the Creatures down.
The main problem is actually getting them into place. You barely have enough people with you to shift more than one piece at a time, and moving heavy wood and iron objects makes for tiring work.
The heavy lifting isn't doing your body any favors either. Your wounds bleed more profusely than ever. And you have to stop more than once to staunch the bleeding and recover from the pain.
By the time you get the first barricade up, a lot of your helpers are panting and sweating hard.
By the time you're halfway through the second, you're all on the verge of exhaustion.
Yet before long, you find yourself joined by more of your allies, with Selim Chain-Breaker at their head. The Khazari soon springs into action, hauling in oxcarts and heavy counters as if they were toys.
"I could not let you labor alone," he exclaims as he handles a length of heavy wooden rail like a stick of firewood.
Before too long, the other two barricades are finished, just as tall and stout as the first.
You're still thinking of what to do next when a shout of alarm calls you to the front doors.
**********
You arrive to find the walls of the guildhouse shedding puffs of whitewash, the wall behind it trembling. The defenders hold steady in their line, weapons at the ready.
The Cryptkeepers still carry only their improvised and scavenged weapons. They shake even as the walls shake, but they stand firm despite the horror that they are about to face. They know what is at stake, both for themselves and their guild. When you look into their eyes, you see the steady determination of those ready to fight and die for an organization that has been their entire life.
Your fellow adventurers are almost relaxed by comparison. They, too, have faced the Creatures, but unlike the others, each one of your colleagues is battle-hardened and experienced, well used to facing down impossible monstrosities and coming out on top. They wait with their weapons and spells at the ready, almost eager for battle.
Your allies are in position, and they are as ready as they'll ever be for what is to come.

title: It's Killing Time
obs:
You decide that forcing Boris to live with what he has done is the best revenge, and you head to his place to implement your plan while he's out for the day.
It takes you hours to search for just the right lily, but you know from your source that Boris is expected to be out all day.  You find yourself in the central square with peddlers hawking their wares, gypsies offering to tell fortunes, and merchants with carts of roasted pork, fall-off-the-bone roasted beef, and roasted chicken on the spit.  None of these draw your attention, though.  You're looking for something else entirely.
You stand in the shadow of the astronomical clock, one of the landmarks of Prague, and the oldest of its kind in the world that's still operational.  Each hour, the four figures flanking the clock are set in motion, each representing something despised at the time of the clock's making.  Vanity is represented by a figure admiring himself in the mirror, greed is represented by a miser holding a bag of gold, pleasure and entertainment illustrated by an historically inaccurate figure of a Turk.  You realize, looking at the first three, just how much they represent Boris's greed and vanity, the duo mixing for his pleasure and entertainment.
Standing in the square, staring up at the clock, you realize that the fourth figure represents you in the most fitting way.  It is death, a skeleton that strikes the time upon the hour.  A broad smile spreads across your face and, almost on cue, you spy a florist on the far side of the square near the Gothic Tyn church, whose impressive spires rise above the old town center.
The woman who sells you the lily gives you a knowing look, and you smile at her, almost as if she has read the look on your face.  She is a stout and strong Eastern European,  and you surmise that she has probably sold many of these death flowers to people of your ilk: killers, assassins, vengeance seekers.  You nod to the woman and let her keep the change, keeping the single lily close to your chest.
**********
It's almost too easy for you to break into Boris's apartment and, for a minute, you fear there's a trap.  You automatically tense into a fighting stance, ready for an ambush.  Finally, after several moments elapse and no one steps forward, you realize that Boris has just gotten sloppy.
Looking around his apartment, and seeing relics from the former Syndicate, you become even more resolved in your decision.  Spying a picture of yourself, a small rosary hanging beside it, your knees almost buckle.  [i]Boris, how did you let it come to this…[/i]  It's not even a question.  It was destiny, and you're grateful that you decided against killing the man you'd once considered a father, no matter what he'd done.  His decision had been hard enough.
You walk toward his bed and place the lily down with a grave solemnity.  You scribble down a small note on a scrap piece of paper, writing:

title: Psy High
obs:
You've got more important things to worry about right now. You sneak on past, leaving Mackenzie to her tears.
You know you can't do this alone, and that's why you've spent so much time gathering up your friends and allies.
Now it's time to call on all those friends to make certain Mr. Pierce and Ms. Clay never get to the Nexus.
As the clock ticks towards midnight, the boat chugs towards the Nexus. From above, you can hear muffled laughter and music—the prom is still going strong. But those happy sounds feel very far away and very out of place compared to what’s happening here.
You’ve found the room on the lowest deck that will look directly out onto the Nexus. Through its single porthole, you can see a faint glow—most people would mistake it for moonlight, but even this far away you can sense the pulse of magic that tells you the Nexus itself is glowing.
You and your friends crowd around the door, blocking the way. When Mr. Pierce, Ms. Clay, and the Gold Crown Team come striding down the hallway, you're ready.
Haley gives you an uncertain look, then draws up straighter and calls, "All right, everyone! Let's go!"
The trouble is, the "everyone" Haley's talking to doesn't include that many people. They do their best—some a little frightened at the thought of facing down the principal, some defiant and resolute—but there just aren't enough people to keep Mr. Pierce away from the Nexus.
You worked hard, and you tried hard, and you counted on your friends, and your friends are helping you.
But it still isn't enough.
"I might have known that it would be you, user_input," snaps Mr. Pierce. "You're a bad seed, and you always have been. You and your little friends—you are nothing but a mob of children. Your priorities are entirely misplaced.
You think you are being kind when you take care of other people, but you are really just soft.
You are disrespectful to your elders.
You have been given great supernatural power—yes, I know about that," he adds with a thin, superior smirk. "But you do nothing worthwhile with it. None of you children deserve to have the powers that you do. Those powers make you unpredictable. Unruly. It is absolutely evident that you need a grownup to keep you in line. I should have gotten rid of your bad influence on Kingsport High long ago."

title: Diabolical
obs:
"You fool." Cold claws wrap around your throat. You choke as the fingers of Hackmaster's exoskeleton tighten.
"Dani, what the hell are you doing?" you manage to wheeze out. She screams, and lifts you in front of the exoskeleton's face port. For the first time since you've known her, she opens the port, revealing her badly scarred face. You thought she was merely controlling the mech, but instead she's actually inside it, which make sense since her van can't travel through space.
"My. Name. Is. [i]Hackmaster[/i]!" she screeches, hurling you across the room. She turns her back on you and kneels before Doctor Arachnus.
"Master. Please. Teach me. I thought I knew what hatred was, but…but I look into your eyes and see the purity. Please."
You try to warn her, but there's no breath in your lungs. And so you have to watch as one of Doctor Arachnus's tentacles casually, almost gently, pulls Hackmaster from her armor. There is a snapping sound. You shouldn't feel bad about it. She was a traitor. You shouldn't.
Doctor Arachnus lets out a cackling laugh.
"Foolish mortal. Did you think my offer was genuine? Ara-kunos needs no assistance, has no equals. Only subjects, and slaves."
That's it, no one makes a fool out of you. Not even the world's deadliest supervillain.
As you prepare to attack, Doctor Arachnus's armor begins to move even more rapidly and gracefully. He flexes his tentacles and claws, apparently relishing the sudden complete control, even if a look of confusion shows that he does not understand its source.
A voice hisses from deep within the armor itself. A voice you remember from your trip to France, although it now contains some of Doctor Arachnus's keening whine. "We're going to kill you, user_input," Nautilus whispers. "You're going to die."
**********
Here it is. Life or death. The ultimate fight. Choose wisely. The fate of the Earth depends on it.

title: An Odyssey: Echoes of War
obs:
You ready yourself, and then you notice Demodocus preparing to follow you.
"Where do you think you're going?" you ask him.
This stops the poet in his tracks. "With you?" he says uncertainly.
"No," you reply. "I'm going alone."
You squeeze his shoulder. "I'll tell you all about it when I get back," you say.
"Promise?" he asks.
"I promise," you reply.
*****Enter*****
When you step through the threshold, the world shimmers around you and you realize you are not in a cave at all. Instead, you are in a new place altogether.
The first thing you notice is the sweet, bright light. Everything around you is tinted gold. The sun is shining low, near the end of its daily journey. But it's not just that. Everything around you is golden. The grass under your feet, the flowering shrubs, the gates to the orchard that stands before you.
This, then, is the Garden of Hespera, Hera's orchard, where it is always sunset.
Behind the gates, you can see a single apple tree, its branches bent with golden apples. A fruit from that tree that became the Apple of Discord, which in turn led to the Trojan War.
And behind the tree, you can see two enormous columns–but no, not columns at all, but legs, the legs of a Titan, so tall as to rival the mountain behind him. You look up, and you can hardly make out his torso, his arms, his neck straining under the weight of the sky. Atlas.
The gate squeaks open and three women appear in front of it. They are dressed in ocher, orange, and yellow robes threaded with gold. The Hesperides, daughters of Atlas, nieces of Nyx.
"A visitor," one of them says. "How wonderful. We were getting terribly bored."
"Don't be silly, Aegle," another replies. "They just want the apples."
Aegle frowns. "You don't know that," she says. "Maybe this one's different."
The second woman turns to you, sizes you up. "Are you different?"
The third Hesperis takes a step forward. There is something menacing in her face now, something serpent-like. "Tell us what you want," she orders. "Do you want the apples?"

title: The Cryptkeepers of Hallowford
obs:
You may not be a trained combat mage, but that doesn't mean you can't have some wards set up around the exits. After all, the Cryptkeepers have mages of their own in residence—maybe you can use their skills?
As luck would have it, two of the guildmembers from the group you led out have some experience in setting up wards. While they have little training as actual battle mages, they do know how to channel their will into defensive patterns and traps. That'll probably be plenty of help.
Once your fellow adventurers catch on to what you're doing, they're more than eager to help as well. There are plenty of trained spellcasters in their number, and one or two even happen to specialize in setting down particularly nasty arcane defenses.
Before long, all three exits are thoroughly covered in defensive patterns. While it may not be enough to stop the Creatures outright, the overlapping fields of magical power will certainly be enough to slow them down.
You're still thinking of what to do next when a shout of alarm calls you to the front doors.
**********
You arrive to find the walls of the guildhouse shedding puffs of whitewash, the wall behind it trembling. The defenders hold steady in their line, weapons at the ready.
The Cryptkeepers still carry only their improvised and scavenged weapons. They shake even as the walls shake, but they stand firm despite the horror that they are about to face. They know what is at stake, both for themselves and their guild. When you look into their eyes, you see the steady determination of those ready to fight and die for an organization that has been their entire life.
Your fellow adventurers are almost relaxed by comparison. They, too, have faced the Creatures, but unlike the others, each one of your colleagues is battle-hardened and experienced, well used to facing down impossible monstrosities and coming out on top. They wait with their weapons and spells at the ready, almost eager for battle.
The members of the town watch stand ready as well.
Your warning and your fighting retreat bought some time for them to muster, but perhaps not enough. Only a fraction of the watch seems to have reached you in time. Sir Michael leads a small group of them beside you, with his sword in one hand and a shield emblazoned with the crest of the Duke of Torinhall in the other. His volunteers carry their spears and halberds unsteadily behind him. For all of their padded aketons and steel kettle helms, these are still ordinary townsfolk, thrust from their normal lives into a dire situation they may not survive. They have every right to be afraid.
More of them wait before the other exits, each led by one of Sir Michael's senior watch members.
Your allies are in position, and they are as ready as they'll ever be for what is to come.
The question is, where will you be?

title: An Odyssey: Echoes of War
obs:
Without hesitation, you grab Demodocus by the chiton and start dragging him behind you while running as fast as you can.
At first he complains, but then he abandons himself to his fate, and even tries to help you by shuffling his feet. The only thing he accomplishes is to beat up a cloud of dust behind you.
The dust makes it harder for the cyclopes to see where you're going.
*****Run*****
You stumble down the path to the shore and throw yourselves into the sea as quickly as you can. Your breath burns your throat, your lungs fighting to keep up. You wade water at first and then you swim. Your crew is struggling behind you, weighed down by the supplies and treasure they grabbed.
But you all make it.
You climb onto the ship and stand on the deck, dripping seawater and sweat.
The cyclopes are now on the shore. They are grabbing boulders and throwing them at your ship with all their might, missing narrowly.
"Who are you?" they ask. "Who are you that killed our brother?"
You said your name was Nobody before, and
your reasons have not changed since then.
But Demodocus can no longer contain his need to sing your praises. "Cyclopes!" he shouts, standing on the deck next to you. "The human who killed the giant Polyphemus is User_input! Remember the name and spread the word of their might as far as you can!"
**********
The cyclopes' island recedes behind you. Your crew has finally started to calm down from all the excitement and exertion.
The ship sails calmly for two whole days. But on the third day, the sky darkens suddenly and a great roar rises from the depths.
"Poseidon," Circe whispers, and her voice catches in her throat.
A wave as tall as a giant rises before you, and in its heart you glimpse the mighty god, the Earth-Shaker, seizing his trident in his hand, stirring up the sea. He rides a chariot made of shells and corals, dragged by enormous mares. Their manes are made of foam, and their hind legs disappear into fish tails. You've seen the likeness of these beasts before, in pictures assembled by tiny pieces of colored glass adorning the floors of your palace, back in Ithaca. Hippocampi.
Poseidon strikes the edge of the wave with the tip of his trident, and your ship is covered with vapor. "User_input!" he roars. "How dare you
harm my son?"
Demodocus turns to you, his eyes full of remorse. This is the result of his bragging. His adoration of you and his eagerness to spread your name throughout the world has brought this upon you and your crew.
But there is no time for any of that right now.
Poseidon raises his fist to the sky and calls up the winds. And the winds, like obedient servants, gather: the East Wind and the South Wind, full of heat, and the West Wind, the carrier of storms, and the heaven-born North Wind. They drive a vast wave before him and crash against your ship, splintering your deck.
Next to you, Demodocus's joints slacken and he sinks to his knees. "How black the sea, how black the clouds," he whimpers. "Now we are certainly doomed. Blessed and thrice blessed were those Achaeans who fell in Troy. I wish we'd been killed the day when the Trojans were pressing us so sorely on the battlefield around the dead body of Achilles, for then we should have had the burial we deserve and all of the Achaeans would have honored our names, and our bodies wouldn't be lost in the unsung depths of the cold sea."
Ajax grasps the back of Demodocus's neck with his giant arm and pulls him to his feet. It wouldn't be a surprise if he slapped the lad about the face a couple of times, but he refrains. "Pull yourself together, poet!" he shouts. "And if you so wish for death, I'll make sure you get your due, once we're out of this cursed storm!"
**********
Enormous waves keep crashing against the hull of your ship, and you all scramble to keep yourselves tethered to the deck, or you'll be lost for good, drowned, feast for whatever lurks underneath the surface of this sea.
You can no longer see Poseidon, but you can feel his wrath. It batters your ship, soaks your hair and skin with salt water, fills your lungs until you can no longer breathe.
And when you are certain that this is your final hour, that your ship will surely sink this time, the storm abates at once, as suddenly as it started.
You find yourself on calm waters again. The clouds disperse and the sun shines above, slowly drying your skin, your hair, your clothes. Your crew right themselves one by one, timidly, reluctantly, as if unable to believe you made it out alive.
Then, you see.
"Oh no," you hear Circe say. "No no no no no."
**********
At first, you mistake what you see around you for kelp floating just under the surface of the water. Pieces of a shipwreck, perhaps, or driftwood sculpted by the salt-laced craft of the sea.
But then your mind catches up to your eyes, and then you make out the sunken faces, the shriveled skin, the nibbled toes, the tangles of hair still attached to decaying scalps.
"Talk to me, Circe," you say to the sorceress, because she seems to know where you are, what it is that's going on.
"We're in the Sirens' land," she says. "Dreadful creatures–half women, half beasts. They call them the Binders, the Entanglers. These poor wretches were caught by their song. They say that the Sirens' song bestows perfect knowledge and intense pleasure. But this," she gestures at the pieces of humans floating all around you, as far as your eye can see, "this is the price you pay."
"How did they get to be this way?" Polyxena asks.
"They were regular women, once. Some goddess punished them for their poor choices…" She trails off. You both see Polyxena is about to launch into a long and impassioned discussion of what "regular women" are or do, and there is clearly no time for that. "I don't actually know the details," Circe hastens to add. "Only what my grandmother told me when I was growing up."
"Can't we just sail around them?" Ajax asks.
"No," says Circe. She points at a cluster of jagged rocks up ahead. "The currents here are such that any ship caught has to drift by their shores. If we try to go against them, we'll be crushed against those rocks."
Demodocus turns to you. "What are we going to do, User_input?" he asks. "We've already survived so much. Perhaps our fortune has finally run out."

title: The Cryptkeepers of Hallowford
obs:
"Town Watch of Hallowford!" you begin as you step forward. "Is this really what you want? To fight your fellow townsfolk because some
Knight from Torinhall tells you to?"
"Maybe it is!" one watch member shouts back.
"Maybe we think Sir Michael has a point. Even if he wasn't born here, he's lived here these past twenty years. He knows what's best for this town. How long have you been here, adventurer?"
You try to find an answer to that, but you can't, not one that sticks.
Anything you say only seems to reinforce their loyalties and make them more and more hostile to you.
You're not going to get anywhere like this.
**********
"Enough!" Lucan snaps, his voice cutting the tense air. "There will be enough of this fruitless bickering! I, for one, demand that we waste no more time."
He points at Sir Michael
and the watch. "If you do not swear yourselves to secrecy right here and right now, then none of you will be leaving this chamber at all!"
Lucan's last words echo through the chamber, so loud that they almost seem to make the stone tremble beneath your feet.
Then the echoes stop, and you realize that the stone is trembling.
The others feel it, too. In but a moment, Lucan's ultimatum is forgotten as the shaking is joined by a dry, scraping rattle that grows louder and louder and louder.
Until the claws of the first Creatures crest the lip of the platform.
**********
Cries of shock and fear fill the chamber as the first of the Creatures clambers onto the platform. Cryptkeeper, watch, and adventurer alike turn outward, scrambling for the precious moments needed to mount a defense to this sudden threat.
The desiccated horrors are not waiting. They plunge into the confused mass with relentless speed. Shock and fear are drowned out by screams of agony as ragged claws and time-yellowed teeth rip into still-living flesh.
Your fellow adventurers are the first to get their bearings. They've faced unpleasant surprises before, and so have you. The unprepared watch and Cryptkeepers rally and, with frantic thrusts of spears and torches, begin to fight back.
**********
As the initial shock wears off, your allies and rivals both fight back with dogged ferocity. The line holds firm, and for a moment, it almost seems like you are pushing the Creatures back.
Lucan rallies his Cryptkeepers with remarkable efficiency. They form up around the Heart in a tight, steady formation, bristling with weapons.
Some of the watch buckle or reel, but most stand their ground, a hard core with
Sir Michael at their head, pushing back against the Creatures.
But this is the Heart of the Creatures' power, and they keep coming, impervious to steel and spellfire. One by one, the brave townsfolk of Hallowford fall, and unlike the Creatures, they do not get back up again.

title: Psy High
obs:
Mackenzie sniffs hard, and eyes you suspiciously.
"I'm sorry Steve dumped you," you say gently. "He was a real jerk to do it during the prom. He was a jerk to do it at all. I know you really liked him." Actually, you don't know that, but for Mackenzie to be this upset, it must be true.
Mackenzie's eyes narrow. "What are you getting at, user_input? You don't care about me and Steve. You don't care about anything."
Uh-oh. Apparently you didn't sound sincere enough.
"You just get away from me!" she shouts.
You do. But as you do, you hear other people hurrying in your direction, and someone shouts, "Is everything okay?"
Uh-oh. You'd better be far away from here when Mackenzie tells people she just saw you.
You know you can't do this alone, and that's why you've spent so much time gathering up your friends and allies.
Now it's time to call on all those friends to make certain Mr. Pierce and Ms. Clay never get to the Nexus.
As the clock ticks towards midnight, the boat chugs towards the Nexus. From above, you can hear muffled laughter and music—the prom is still going strong. But those happy sounds feel very far away and very out of place compared to what’s happening here.
You’ve found the room on the lowest deck that will look directly out onto the Nexus. Through its single porthole, you can see a faint glow—most people would mistake it for moonlight, but even this far away you can sense the pulse of magic that tells you the Nexus itself is glowing.
You and your friends crowd around the door, blocking the way. When Mr. Pierce, Ms. Clay, and the Gold Crown Team come striding down the hallway, you're ready.
Haley gives you an uncertain look, then draws up straighter and calls, "All right, everyone! Let's go!"
The trouble is, the "everyone" Haley's talking to doesn't include that many people. They do their best—some a little frightened at the thought of facing down the principal, some defiant and resolute—but there just aren't enough people to keep Mr. Pierce away from the Nexus.
You worked hard, and you tried hard, and you counted on your friends, and your friends are helping you.
But it still isn't enough.
"I might have known that it would be you, user_input," snaps Mr. Pierce. "You're a bad seed, and you always have been. You and your little friends—you are nothing but a mob of children. Your priorities are entirely misplaced.
You are unruly and undisciplined.
You are disrespectful to your elders.
You have been given great supernatural power—yes, I know about that," he adds with a thin, superior smirk. "But you do nothing worthwhile with it. None of you children deserve to have the powers that you do. Those powers make you unpredictable. Unruly. It is absolutely evident that you need a grownup to keep you in line. I should have gotten rid of your bad influence on Kingsport High long ago."

obs:
Perhaps now is the chance you've been waiting for.
With your erstwhile "allies" fighting for their lives against the undying tide, there's nobody stopping you from simply running in and taking the Heart. If you move quickly and quietly, you might not even get noticed at all until you are well out of harm's way.
Should be easy, right?
**********
Maybe not as easy as you think.
You only manage to take a few steps toward the Heart before one of its protectors spots you.
They're not exactly waving a weapon in your face yet, but if you make any attempt to steal the Heart while they're still watching, that will surely change in a hurry.
So you retreat to the edge of the central platform, to wait for a better opportunity. Maybe when the Heart is less well-guarded—or at least when the would-be guards are far more distracted—you'll have a better chance.
**********
The undying surge forward against the last remnants of the forces of the living.
Only a handful are still on their feet and fighting.
Lucan and the last holdouts of his Cryptkeepers are on the verge of destruction. But with magic and steel, they cling to a tiny patch of bloodied stone, even as their knot of defenders grows smaller and smaller.
Sir Michael and his last few watch members are no better off. They fall back the last few steps until their backs are pressed against the harsh light of the Heart itself.
With every passing second, the dead advance. With every moment, despair grows in the eyes of the living. This can't go on for much longer.

Jules and Rosalind run toward you, making sure you're okay, both of them eying the lighthouse nervously.
And then you notice them: three wizards who had been involved with the original spell, lying unconscious at compass points around the lighthouse. You wonder what Maeve did to them, how she called them so close, and what she stole in hopes of powering her escape.

title: The Cryptkeepers of Hallowford
obs:
"I no longer care what Lucan or his Cryptkeepers think of me," Selim says angrily. "The price they demand for their esteem is far too high to be paid by any person with decency left in their heart."
"But you're not going to just leave Hallowford to fend for itself, are you?" you ask. You haven't known Selim for long, but you bet he isn't going to do that.
"No, I would not leave these people to their doom." He shakes his head. "But there are others. Lucan may delude himself into thinking that he and his guild are Hallowford's last hope, but they are not the only ones willing to fight to defend this town."
You nod. "Sir Michael, you mean?"
"Yes, exactly," Selim confirms. "I mean to seek them out and offer them my service."
Selim stops and turns to you. "I know you may not think of me as a friend, and I do not think I would ask this of you if the situation were less desperate," he begins, "but Sir Michael will need as many skilled adventurers as he can find, and despite our differences, I cannot say you are not that."
He extends his hand, though his expression remains firm. "Will you come with me? You would not be my first choice for an ally, but it seems we are all swiftly running out of options."

You take a breath and run toward the cage of alien metal that holds the Heart at the center of the chamber.

and Sir Michael's watch
may be fighting for their lives, but they still manage to spot you before you get anywhere near close enough.
A cry of alarm goes up. Someone points an arbalest your way. You back off, moving away to the edge of the central platform.
There are still too many who would stop you from destroying the Heart. Maybe if you waited for a better opportunity, after the Creatures have worn them down more.
Let the undying horrors do half your job for you. That'll make things easier.
**********
The undying surge forward against the last remnants of the forces of the living.
Only a handful are still on their feet and fighting.
Lucan and the last holdouts of his Cryptkeepers are on the verge of destruction. But with magic and steel, they cling to a tiny patch of bloodied stone, even as their knot of defenders grows smaller and smaller.
Sir Michael and his last few watch members are no better off. They fall back the last few steps until their backs are pressed against the harsh light of the Heart itself.
With every passing second, the dead advance. With every moment, despair grows in the eyes of the living. This can't go on for much longer.

title: An Odyssey: Echoes of War
obs:
"This one looks like it will take as many hands as possible," you say.
"We'll all come," Polyxena replies, looking sternly at everyone around her to preempt any disagreement. "No question about it."
On foot, you all pick up your weapons–Demodocus's is, of course, his lyre–and make your way to the entrance of the cave. Deep darkness lies ahead, and you cannot see nor hear anything beyond the cave's gaping maw.
*****Enter*****
As you step through the threshold, the smell of swamp assaults you. You are no longer in the land of the Heroes' Mist, that much is certain. Before you lies the lake of Lerna, from which the Hydra takes its name.
The smell is vile; it burns your nostrils. "Everyone, cover your noses," you say, and, turning to Demodocus, you ask: "What do you know of the Hydra?"
Demodocus, heartened by the attention, launches into a diatribe on the Lernaean Hydra's lore: How it was reared by Hera for the sole purpose of defeating Hercules with its poisonous blood and deadly teeth; how it terrorized the villages around Lake Lerna; how Hercules used both speed and strength to defeat it with the invaluable help of his friend.
You approach the swampy waters of the lake. As before, there is no sign of the cave you entered to find yourselves here. Only reeds, and rocks, and insects.
As you stand at the edge of the lake, everything seems quiet–serene, almost. And yet there is this sense of foreboding; the certainty that something dangerous lurks here.
You scour the still surface of the lake, green and thick with duckweed, and at first you can see nothing out of the ordinary.
*****Look More Closely*****
Then, you notice it.
In what you thought was a tangle of reeds and brambles, eyes.
Eyes, and teeth, and scales.
Looking straight at you, the head of the snake rises. It knows you've seen it now. It rises and rises until it stands high above you, as tall as two grown humans.
And beside it, eight more heads just like it. Nine slender necks sprouting from a mighty body still concealed beneath the grimy waters of the swamp.
This is it, hero. This is your time. Your moment of truth.

title: An Odyssey: Echoes of War
obs:
"I know it hurts," she says. "No use pretending."
You nod.
She pushes the substance deep into your wound, hurting you even more. The sweet smell does not make it better. Not one bit. When she's done, she covers the wound with some clean linen. "There," she says. "All done." Then, she stands up and walks away, allowing you to sulk in private.
**********
The ship sails calmly for two whole days. But on the third day, the sky darkens suddenly and a great roar rises from the depths.
"Poseidon," Circe whispers, and her voice catches in her throat.
A wave as tall as a giant rises before you, and in its heart you glimpse the mighty god, the Earth-Shaker, seizing his trident in his hand, stirring up the sea. He rides a chariot made of shells and corals, dragged by enormous mares. Their manes are made of foam, and their hind legs disappear into fish tails. You've seen the likeness of these beasts before, in pictures assembled by tiny pieces of colored glass adorning the floors of your palace, back in Ithaca. Hippocampi.
Poseidon strikes the edge of the wave with the tip of his trident, and your ship is covered with vapor. "User_input!" he roars. "How dare you
harm my son?"
This is the result of your pride. Your need to spread your name throughout the world brought this upon you and your crew.
But there is no time for any of that right now.
Poseidon raises his fist to the sky and calls up the winds. And the winds, like obedient servants, gather: the East Wind and the South Wind, full of heat, and the West Wind, the carrier of storms, and the heaven-born North Wind. They drive a vast wave before him and crash against your ship, splintering your deck.
Next to you, Demodocus's joints slacken and he sinks to his knees. "How black the sea, how black the clouds," he whimpers. "Now we are certainly doomed. Blessed and thrice blessed were those Achaeans who fell in Troy. I wish we'd been killed the day when the Trojans were pressing us so sorely on the battlefield around the dead body of Achilles, for then we should have had the burial we deserve and all of the Achaeans would have honored our names, and our bodies wouldn't be lost in the unsung depths of the cold sea."
Ajax grasps the back of Demodocus's neck with his giant arm and pulls him to his feet. It wouldn't be a surprise if he slapped the lad about the face a couple of times, but he refrains. "Pull yourself together, poet!" he shouts. "And if you so wish for death, I'll make sure you get your due, once we're out of this cursed storm!"
**********
Enormous waves keep crashing against the hull of your ship, and you all scramble to keep yourselves tethered to the deck, or you'll be lost for good, drowned, feast for whatever lurks underneath the surface of this sea.
You can no longer see Poseidon, but you can feel his wrath. It batters your ship, soaks your hair and skin with salt water, fills your lungs until you can no longer breathe.
And when you are certain that this is your final hour, that your ship will surely sink this time, the storm abates at once, as suddenly as it started.
You find yourself on calm waters again. The clouds disperse and the sun shines above, slowly drying your skin, your hair, your clothes. Your crew right themselves one by one, timidly, reluctantly, as if unable to believe you made it out alive.
Then, you see.
"Oh no," you hear Circe say. "No no no no no."
**********
At first, you mistake what you see around you for kelp floating just under the surface of the water. Pieces of a shipwreck, perhaps, or driftwood sculpted by the salt-laced craft of the sea.
But then your mind catches up to your eyes, and then you make out the sunken faces, the shriveled skin, the nibbled toes, the tangles of hair still attached to decaying scalps.
"Talk to me, Circe," you say to the sorceress, because she seems to know where you are, what it is that's going on.
"We're in the Sirens' land," she says. "Dreadful creatures–half women, half beasts. They call them the Binders, the Entanglers. These poor wretches were caught by their song. They say that the Sirens' song bestows perfect knowledge and intense pleasure. But this," she gestures at the pieces of humans floating all around you, as far as your eye can see, "this is the price you pay."
"How did they get to be this way?" Polyxena asks.
"They were regular women, once. Some goddess punished them for their poor choices…" She trails off. You both see Polyxena is about to launch into a long and impassioned discussion of what "regular women" are or do, and there is clearly no time for that. "I don't actually know the details," Circe hastens to add. "Only what my grandmother told me when I was growing up."
"Can't we just sail around them?" Ajax asks.
"No," says Circe. She points at a cluster of jagged rocks up ahead. "The currents here are such that any ship caught has to drift by their shores. If we try to go against them, we'll be crushed against those rocks."
Demodocus turns to you. "What are we going to do, User_input?" he asks. "We've already survived so much. Perhaps our fortune has finally run out."

title: The Cryptkeepers of Hallowford
obs:
"Why not just stand and fight here?" the Cryptkeeper asks. "We could defend this room."
You shake your head. "If we do that, the Creatures will just go around us, cut us off, and overwhelm us," you explain. "What we need to do is hold them off as long as we can, then fall back to the next room. We can barricade the doors to buy us some time to recover, but we can't let ourselves get pinned down."
So that's exactly what you do.
The next hour comes as a series of rapid, chaotic clashes as you and your allies fall back, room by room, winning just enough time to catch your breath before being assailed by the monstrosities again.
You fight at the forefront of every skirmish,
and you soon have the wounds to show for it: a handful of deep cuts and a long, bleeding gash along your thigh.
You aren't the only one taking wounds. Despite your best efforts, the constant attacks are taking their toll: bit by bit, your force is being worn to nothing. Only your unwillingness to stop retreating keeps their losses from being worse.
Though you look for ways to try to slow your pursuers down, you don't exactly have the time to plan intricate ambushes. As you give up room after room without seeming to do much damage to the Creatures at your heels, you feel your allies growing more and more disheartened.
You try your best to keep everyone's spirits up, but your best only falls flat as your allies seem to grow more and more hopeless. Soon it seems like you aren't even offering much of a fight at all before falling back again, room by room, until you find yourself fleeing through the front doors and into the courtyard.
**********
You stumble out into the bright light of the courtyard to find
yourself face-to-face with the leveled spear points of the town watch arrayed in readiness before you.
Edith looks at you in surprise. "Did you warn the watch that we were being attacked?"
You shake your head. "I never had the time to send anyone to warn them."
"You didn't need to,"
says a wiry, silver-haired man in maille and surcoat as he strides toward you with the gait of a veteran soldier. So this must be Sir Michael of Torinhall.
"Based on what you told me, I could put together the pieces myself. I
know there's some kind of threat underneath the guildhouse, though it'd be nice to know exactly what it is."
You explain as best you can as quickly as you're able, which admittedly isn't very well. It's hardly easy to describe a swarm of undying abominations to someone who's never seen them before.
Sir Michael evidently thinks so, too. "You're going to have to give me some more details.
These things sound like bone-horrors or rag-shamblers to me, but that can't be right."
"Look," you reply, trying to keep your impatience in check. "I'd love to draw you a sketch or something, but they're right behind us."
The old knight nods grimly as he hefts his blade. "All right, better get to work then." He raises his hand to point beyond his line of the town watch.
"Your fellow adventurers are setting up some kind of staging area just behind that corner. I'm sure they'd welcome your company."
You nod and begin to make your way back.
"Oh and, Nameless?"
You turn. Apparently Sir Michael is not quite finished.
"I should thank you," the gray-haired veteran says.
"We would have been caught off guard if it weren't for the fact that you told us enough of the truth to prepare us for something like this. However—" His eyes grow stern. "—that doesn't mean I won't be wanting the rest of it once this is over."
You nod. After this, you suppose you're going to have to give Sir Michael some answers.
**********
Your fellow adventurers rush toward you the moment they see you.
"Nameless!" Adanna shouts as she takes the lead. "Where betwixt heaven and sand have you been?"
"In there," you reply, jerking a thumb at the bulk of the guildhouse.
Questions follow. "What's going on?", "How bad is it?", "How many of the Cryptkeepers are alive?" You try to answer them as best you can, though with every answer, the faces looking back at you seem to get more and more grim.
"That sounds bad," someone says, as if that weren't obvious enough already.
You nod. "It is. What can I do to help?"
"That's actually what we were talking about," Adanna replies. "How to help out the guards, I mean."
"Got a few suggestions then?" you ask.
That gets your fellow adventurers talking all at once. It seems they've got more than a few ideas. "We could collapse the entrances. Lucan won't like it, but it'll slow the things down," says one.
"We can block the entrances with barricades, give us some proper defenses," suggests another.
"Set up some magical defenses!" pipes up a third. "That might stop them!"
"I'm sure you've got some other ideas, too," Adanna adds.
"Although you might want to consider getting your wounds healed up first."
So what to do?
**********
You take another step forward as you try to figure out exactly what to do, but your legs seem to buckle under your weight. Your hand reaches out for the nearest wall as you suddenly find yourself unable to support your own weight.
The pain from your wounds redoubles. You need to see a healer. You can't move around, let alone fight like this.
Luckily for you, more than enough of your fellow adventurers are skilled in the process of magical healing.
It isn't difficult to find one who's willing to fix you up a bit. While the process is hardly pleasant, it does end up being surprisingly quick.
Evidently, she's had a lot of practice.
Unfortunately, your wounds prove too deep to be healed completely without time and a day of bedrest, something none of you have. Still, your healer tries her best. By the time she is done, most of your wounds are closed, and you feel fit enough to at least put up a decent fight, should things come to it.
You can only hope that will be enough.
You're still thinking of what to do next when a shout of alarm calls you to the front doors.
**********
You arrive to find the walls of the guildhouse shedding puffs of whitewash, the wall behind it trembling. The defenders hold steady in their line, weapons at the ready.
The Cryptkeepers still carry only their improvised and scavenged weapons. They shake even as the walls shake, but they stand firm despite the horror that they are about to face. They know what is at stake, both for themselves and their guild. When you look into their eyes, you see the steady determination of those ready to fight and die for an organization that has been their entire life.
Your fellow adventurers are almost relaxed by comparison. They, too, have faced the Creatures, but unlike the others, each one of your colleagues is battle-hardened and experienced, well used to facing down impossible monstrosities and coming out on top. They wait with their weapons and spells at the ready, almost eager for battle.
The members of the town watch stand ready as well.
Your warning gave them enough time to assemble at least a good portion of their force. Sir Michael stands with them now, his sword at the ready, his shield positioned in front of him in a fighter's stance. A half dozen of his volunteers stand behind him, clad in padded jackets and kettle helms, their spears and halberds held in unsteady fingers. Underneath their armor, they are still laborers and crafters, thrown from their mundane work into this sudden and desperate fight.
There are another dozen or so split between the other exits, each commanded by one of the old knight's subordinates.
Your allies are in position, and they are as ready as they'll ever be for what is to come.
The question is, where will you be?

1: I'll support my allies from the rear.
2: I'm going to stay back and make sure none of the Creatures get through.

and they will not rally to us so long as their leaders forbid it!"
He shakes his head. "If we are to survive, if any of us are to survive, then the Heart must be destroyed!"

title: An Odyssey: Echoes of War
obs:
You take the bag away from Eurylochus and throw it overboard.
You could punish Eurylochus. You could roar and threaten and punch. You could even forgive him. What difference would it make?
You walk away and curl up in a corner.
There is nothing to do right now but to wait and see where the winds take you.
**********
Many hours later, you find yourself on calm waters again. There is a stillness in the air, and the sun is shining above.
Then, you see.
"Oh no," you hear Circe say. "No no no no no."
**********
At first, you mistake what you see around you for kelp floating just under the surface of the water. Pieces of a shipwreck, perhaps, or driftwood sculpted by the salt-laced craft of the sea.
But then your mind catches up to your eyes, and then you make out the sunken faces, the shriveled skin, the nibbled toes, the tangles of hair still attached to decaying scalps.
"Talk to me, Circe," you say to the sorceress, because she seems to know where you are, what it is that's going on.
"We're in the Sirens' land," she says. "Dreadful creatures–half women, half beasts. They call them the Binders, the Entanglers. These poor wretches were caught by their song. They say that the Sirens' song bestows perfect knowledge and intense pleasure. But this," she gestures at the pieces of humans floating all around you, as far as your eye can see, "this is the price you pay."
"How did they get to be this way?" Polyxena asks.
"They were regular women, once. Some goddess punished them for their poor choices…" She trails off. You both see Polyxena is about to launch into a long and impassioned discussion of what "regular women" are or do, and there is clearly no time for that. "I don't actually know the details," Circe hastens to add. "Only what my grandmother told me when I was growing up."
"Can't we just sail around them?" Ajax asks.
"No," says Circe. She points at a cluster of jagged rocks up ahead. "The currents here are such that any ship caught has to drift by their shores. If we try to go against them, we'll be crushed against those rocks."
Demodocus turns to you. "What are we going to do, Cleo?" he asks. "We've already survived so much. Perhaps our fortune has finally run out."
0: Plug everyone's ears with beeswax and sail past them. This is the smartest, least risky thing to do.
1: Plug everyone's ears and kill the Sirens to save future passing sailors. Riskier, but heroic.
2: Have everyone's ears plugged with beeswax and myself tied to the mast, hoping the rope will hold.
3: This whole heroic setup sounds suspicious to me. Sit down and have a real conversation with these women.

title: An Odyssey: Echoes of War
obs:
You announce your decision to your crew and tell them to wait on the ship until you return.
Demodocus, however, follows you to the shore.
When you look at him, your eyebrows asking him what in Hades he thinks he's doing, he protests. "How am I supposed to sing about your deeds if I don't witness them firsthand?"
He does have a point. So, together, you make your way to the entrance of the cave.
*****Enter*****
The moment you pass through the threshold, you realize you are not in a cave. You have been transported to a different place altogether. And you can feel the tips of spears pressing against your skin. A bunch of angry women are scowling at you.
"Who are you?" the woman who seems to be in charge asks.
"User_input are User_input, Ruler of Ithaca and child of Gaia," Demodocus replies in your stead. "And I am Demodocus, the renowned poet," he adds.
"Are you here to claim our Queen Hippolyta's girdle?"
You catch on immediately. "Why yes, that's exactly why we are here."
They lower their spears at once. "Then we shall take you to our queen," the woman replies.
*****Follow Them*****
With the threat of spears removed, or at least postponed, you have a chance to take in your surroundings.
Around you lies a desert, golden and flickering under the sun as if on fire. You can see no sign of cities or palaces anywhere, but the determined way the Amazons are leading you suggest there is something you are missing.
The Amazons themselves seem fully integrated into this environment: clad in thin, light fabrics that cover enough to save them from the sun's unrelenting eye, but not so much as to restrict movement. Each of them carries a spear in hand, and bow and quiver strapped to the back. They seem to have some kind of scorn for shields, however, as if defending oneself is a ridiculous idea.
Demodocus looks quite taken with them, judging by the way he stares at them, his lips moving as if mouthing silent verses devoted to the rippling muscles of their backs.
"Do we have far to go?" you ask.
"Why? Are you tired?" the leader of the women, who has by now introduced herself as Ainippe, asks back. Then, she laughs. "Not at all. In fact, we're here."
The moment she says so, a complex of low buildings comes into view, like a mirage. They are made of the same sand the desert consists of, which would explain why they were not visible from a distance.
It's either that, or more of the gods' games.
When you reach the low gate of the largest building, the women form two lines on either side, spears planted on the ground at their sides.
"Go on in," Ainippe says, a condescending smile on her lips. "She might not even bite."
*****Enter*****
If you expected a palace and a throne room, this is not at all what you find before you. The room is clearly intended for training: it's sparse, equipped with iron weights and wooden sticks and human-shaped figures made of dried palm leaves, and carries the permanent scent of stale sweat that is the identifying trait of all training rooms.
In the middle of the room is a round arena, its ground covered in fine, white dust. And in the middle of that arena stands Hippolyta, Queen of the Amazons. Nothing distinguishes her from the rest of the Amazons you've seen, except for the girdle fastened at her waist.
Noticing you staring at her girdle, Hippolyta speaks: "I see you've spotted the item you came here for."
"I take it others have tried to win it before?"
Hippolyta smirks. "'Tried' being the important part in that statement." She looks at you, sizing you up. "Many have tried," she says. "Nobody has succeeded so far."
"Not even Hercules?" you ask.
She inhales sharply and frowns. "Do not speak that man's name in my presence."
"Why not?"
"We have history," she replies, then adds cryptically: "History that has come to pass, and more that is yet to be."
You study her face. The high cheekbones, the aquiline nose, the stubborn chin. You've seen these features before.
"I fought with your sister Penthesilea in Troy," you say.
She stands up a bit straighter, clenches her jaw. "With, or against?"
"Against," you say, "since she chose to assist the Trojans."
"I see," she says. Her eyes downturn for the first time.
There is still grief there.
"She was a good warrior, a valiant soldier."
"Killed by Achilles," she says. "Friend of yours?"
"Friend, yes," you reply.
"Then this is going to be fun," she says. "I assume you mean to fight me?"
0: Challenge her to a duel. 
1: Exchange her girdle for a performance by Demodocus.
2: Talk her into giving me the girdle. A very tall order, but perhaps it's worth a shot.

title: Psy High
obs:
"I'm sorry Steve dumped you," you say gently. "He was a real jerk to do it during the prom. He was a jerk to do it at all. I know you really liked him." Actually, you don't know that, but for Mackenzie to be this upset, it must be true.
Mackenzie's eyes narrow. "What are you getting at, user_input? You don't care about me and Steve. You don't care about anything."
Uh-oh. Apparently you didn't sound sincere enough.
"You just get away from me!" she shouts.
You do. But as you do, you hear other people hurrying in your direction, and someone shouts, "Is everything okay?"
Uh-oh. You'd better be far away from here when Mackenzie tells people she just saw you.
You know you can't do this alone, and that's why you've spent so much time gathering up your friends and allies.
Now it's time to call on all those friends to make certain Mr. Pierce and Ms. Clay never get to the Nexus.
As the clock ticks towards midnight, the boat chugs towards the Nexus. From above, you can hear muffled laughter and music—the prom is still going strong. But those happy sounds feel very far away and very out of place compared to what’s happening here.
You’ve found the room on the lowest deck that will look directly out onto the Nexus. Through its single porthole, you can see a faint glow—most people would mistake it for moonlight, but even this far away you can sense the pulse of magic that tells you the Nexus itself is glowing.
You and your friends crowd around the door, blocking the way. When Mr. Pierce, Ms. Clay, and the Gold Crown Team come striding down the hallway, you're ready.
Haley gives you an uncertain look, then draws up straighter and calls, "All right, everyone! Let's go!"
The trouble is, the "everyone" Haley's talking to doesn't include that many people. They do their best—some a little frightened at the thought of facing down the principal, some defiant and resolute—but there just aren't enough people to keep Mr. Pierce away from the Nexus.
You worked hard, and you tried hard, and you counted on your friends, and your friends are helping you.
But it still isn't enough.
"I might have known that it would be you, user_input," snaps Mr. Pierce. "You're a bad seed, and you always have been. You and your little friends—you are nothing but a mob of children. Your priorities are entirely misplaced.
You are unruly and undisciplined.
You are disrespectful to your elders.
You have been given great supernatural power—yes, I know about that," he adds with a thin, superior smirk. "But you do nothing worthwhile with it. None of you children deserve to have the powers that you do. Those powers make you unpredictable. Unruly. It is absolutely evident that you need a grownup to keep you in line. I should have gotten rid of your bad influence on Kingsport High long ago."

1: I'll make a dive for the talisman to try to grab it away from him.
2: "You don't know the first thing about using your power in the right way!" I'll make him angry so he'll get distracted from what he's doing.
3: I can overpower him with magic.

obs:
Selim's eyebrow rises. "You knew of this?"
You nod. "Sir Michael told me about it. He actually invited me to it, but I turned him down, thought maybe there were better alternatives."
"And now you have found that there are none," Selim responds sadly, "as I have."

He extends his hand, though his expression remains firm. "Will you come with me? You would not be my first choice for an ally, but it seems we are all swiftly running out of options."

title: The Cryptkeepers of Hallowford
obs:
You rush into the melee, staff in hand, trying your best to drive the attacking Creatures back.
Every time, your staff strikes home, but it is you who staggers back, your arms numb from the shock of impact.
And it is your foe who rushes forward, claw flashing in the pale light.
The blow comes too quick to be dodged, too powerful to be parried. It tears deep into your side, rending cloth and flesh as if they're nothing. An explosion of raw agony shoots through your body.
You stagger back, barely on your feet, your vision blurred and your teeth clenched tight from the pain, your hands barely able to keep hold of your weapon.
You won't be able to take another hit like that.
**********
The Creatures do not relent. There is no driving them back. With every moment, more of the horrors claw their way up onto the platform.
The defense still holds, but it won't for much longer. The Creatures rip and tear at the fringes, cutting down anyone who is not forced back. The stink of fear mingles with the stench of fresh blood.
Lucan and his Cryptkeepers hold on, but there are only so many of them left, and that number is dropping by the second.
The watch holds firm, for now. But with each fresh attack, fewer of
Sir Michael's
followers remain standing.
Yet no effort can change the simple fact that the undying monsters cannot be felled, their numbers cannot be thinned. Inevitably, the living will give way to the dead.

1: I have to deal with Sir Michael.

title: Psy High
obs:
"Wow, thanks for asking!" you say, smiling up at Tyler. "I was already hoping I could join the Gold Crown Team. This is a great opportunity."
Tyler's gorgeous smile grows brighter. "Oh, I'm so glad," he says. "I knew you'd be perfect Gold Crown Team material. Go talk to Ms. Clay after school, and she'll get you set up."
You smile back. "I'll do that. Talk to you later?"
Tyler nods. "Absolutely."
Tyler runs a hand through his already-perfect hair, and turns to go.
**********
The morning passes in a haze of distraction. You try to answer some texts without letting the teachers see what you're doing, and you think you succeed.
Third period comes as a profound relief: English with Ms. Rivera.
"Did you see the posters?" Tara's saying to Casey as they walk into class ahead of you. "They announced the prom theme! A Night To Remember."
"Yeah, I saw!" Casey answers, with more than her usual excitement. "And it's going to be on a boat!"
The prom! It's exciting, but it's just one more thing you need to think about and plan for. Great.
Still, in English class, at least, you can feel secure. You know Ms. Rivera will lead a great discussion, and you'll spend forty-five minutes immersed in interesting thoughts about literature.
Except when you come into the room, you don't see any books out on people's desks, just pens and pencils.
Uh-oh. That means there's an exam today—an exam you totally forgot about. What are you going to do?
**********
Well, you could try to wing it. You might be able to remember enough about the book to improvise your way through a test. If you don't, though, you'll probably fail.
Or, you could try to get the answers from someone else, either by trying to read off their paper or by using magic. You can look at a paper clairvoyantly or try to read someone else's thoughts. If you get caught doing any of those things, though, Ms. Rivera will be seriously disappointed, and you'll get sent to detention. Going to detention means you'll miss rehearsal for the play and Jessica will be really mad at you.
Although…now that you think of it, you realize if you do get sent to detention, you'll be able to see Room 014 for yourself.
Wow.
That would be super risky. You might get influenced by the Vinculum! And even if you don't, Ms. Rivera will think you've cheated on an exam, and you'll be in serious trouble. But you'll be able to get direct evidence about what's going on in Room 014, and you might even be able to put in some magical threads directly.
So what will you do?

title: An Odyssey: Echoes of War
obs:
"Ow!" you exclaim, making sure your facial expression matches your dismay.
Circe laughs. "Sorry, captain," she says. She pushes the substance deep into your wound, hurting you even more. It's unclear how necessary this is.
"Take your time, why don't you," you say.
She laughs again, like you're suddenly the funniest person on the ship. "Almost done," she says. She covers your wound with some linen and stands up. "Make sure you keep this clean, yes?" she says and walks away.
**********
The ship sails calmly for two whole days. But on the third day, the sky darkens suddenly and a great roar rises from the depths.
"Poseidon," Circe whispers, and her voice catches in her throat.
A wave as tall as a giant rises before you, and in its heart you glimpse the mighty god, the Earth-Shaker, seizing his trident in his hand, stirring up the sea. He rides a chariot made of shells and corals, dragged by enormous mares. Their manes are made of foam, and their hind legs disappear into fish tails. You've seen the likeness of these beasts before, in pictures assembled by tiny pieces of colored glass adorning the floors of your palace, back in Ithaca. Hippocampi.
Poseidon strikes the edge of the wave with the tip of his trident, and your ship is covered with vapor. "User_input!" he roars. "How dare you
harm my son?"
This is the result of your bragging. Your pride brought this upon you and your crew.
But there is no time for any of that right now.
Poseidon raises his fist to the sky and calls up the winds. And the winds, like obedient servants, gather: the East Wind and the South Wind, full of heat, and the West Wind, the carrier of storms, and the heaven-born North Wind. They drive a vast wave before him and crash against your ship, splintering your deck.
Next to you, Demodocus's joints slacken and he sinks to his knees. "How black the sea, how black the clouds," he whimpers. "Now we are certainly doomed. Blessed and thrice blessed were those Achaeans who fell in Troy. I wish we'd been killed the day when the Trojans were pressing us so sorely on the battlefield around the dead body of Achilles, for then we should have had the burial we deserve and all of the Achaeans would have honored our names, and our bodies wouldn't be lost in the unsung depths of the cold sea."
Ajax grasps the back of Demodocus's neck with his giant arm and pulls him to his feet. It wouldn't be a surprise if he slapped the lad about the face a couple of times, but he refrains. "Pull yourself together, poet!" he shouts. "And if you so wish for death, I'll make sure you get your due, once we're out of this cursed storm!"
**********
Enormous waves keep crashing against the hull of your ship, and you all scramble to keep yourselves tethered to the deck, or you'll be lost for good, drowned, feast for whatever lurks underneath the surface of this sea.
You can no longer see Poseidon, but you can feel his wrath. It batters your ship, soaks your hair and skin with salt water, fills your lungs until you can no longer breathe.
And when you are certain that this is your final hour, that your ship will surely sink this time, the storm abates at once, as suddenly as it started.
You find yourself on calm waters again. The clouds disperse and the sun shines above, slowly drying your skin, your hair, your clothes. Your crew right themselves one by one, timidly, reluctantly, as if unable to believe you made it out alive.
Then, you see.
"Oh no," you hear Circe say. "No no no no no."
**********
At first, you mistake what you see around you for kelp floating just under the surface of the water. Pieces of a shipwreck, perhaps, or driftwood sculpted by the salt-laced craft of the sea.
But then your mind catches up to your eyes, and then you make out the sunken faces, the shriveled skin, the nibbled toes, the tangles of hair still attached to decaying scalps.
"Talk to me, Circe," you say to the sorceress, because she seems to know where you are, what it is that's going on.
"We're in the Sirens' land," she says. "Dreadful creatures–half women, half beasts. They call them the Binders, the Entanglers. These poor wretches were caught by their song. They say that the Sirens' song bestows perfect knowledge and intense pleasure. But this," she gestures at the pieces of humans floating all around you, as far as your eye can see, "this is the price you pay."
"How did they get to be this way?" Polyxena asks.
"They were regular women, once. Some goddess punished them for their poor choices…" She trails off. You both see Polyxena is about to launch into a long and impassioned discussion of what "regular women" are or do, and there is clearly no time for that. "I don't actually know the details," Circe hastens to add. "Only what my grandmother told me when I was growing up."
"Can't we just sail around them?" Ajax asks.
"No," says Circe. She points at a cluster of jagged rocks up ahead. "The currents here are such that any ship caught has to drift by their shores. If we try to go against them, we'll be crushed against those rocks."
Demodocus turns to you. "What are we going to do, User_input?" he asks. "We've already survived so much. Perhaps our fortune has finally run out."

obs:

[i]Isn't it obvious?[/i]

You used to joke, when you and User_input were kids, about being the same person in separate bodies. It's not a joke anymore.
